courses.title: Gurbani Exegesis with Prof. Sahib Singh
courses.summary: An author-as-professor course about Prof. Sahib Singh (1892-1977), among the most influential interpreters of Sri Guru Granth Sahib. The course studies who he was, the grammar-based method he built for reading Gurbani, his ten-volume Sri Guru Granth Sahib Darpan, his companion Gurbani Viakaran, his study of the…
outcomes: Describe the life, training, and motivating concerns of Prof. Sahib Singh as an interpreter of Sri Guru Granth Sahib.
Explain the core claim of his grammatical method: that the script's vowel-signs and word-endings carry meaning.
Identify the aims and structure of his major works, the Sri Guru Granth Sahib Darpan and the Gurbani Viakaran.
Apply grammatical principles of number, part of speech, and case to narrow the possible meanings of a line.
Summarize the main points of scholarly discussion and disagreement about his approach.
Practice a disciplined, grammar-aware reading habit grounded in humility and respect for the text.
references: Singh, Sahib. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Darpan. 10 vols. Jalandhar: Raj Publishers.
Singh, Sahib. Gurbani Viakaran. Amritsar: Singh Brothers.
Singh, Sahib. About the Compilation of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. Amritsar: Singh Brothers.
Singh, Pashaura, and Louis E. Fenech, eds. The Oxford Handbook of Sikh Studies. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2014.
Mann, Gurinder Singh. The Making of Sikh Scripture. New York: Oxford University Press, 2001.

lessons.title: Who Was Prof. Sahib Singh?
lessons.summary: Introduces Prof. Sahib Singh (1892-1977), his training, the interpretive problem he saw, and the convictions that shaped his lifelong study of Sri Guru Granth Sahib.

lessons.title: His Place in Sikh Scholarship
lessons.summary: Situates Sahib Singh against the interpretive traditions he inherited, shows what his reproducible method added, and explains why his influence endured across both devotional and academic settings.

lessons.title: The Grammatical Method: Core Idea
lessons.summary: Explains the heart of Sahib Singh's contribution: that laga-matra in the Gurmukhi of the Granth carry grammatical meaning, illustrated with an original English analogy and the principle of consistency.

lessons.title: How Grammar Resolves Interpretive Questions
lessons.summary: Shows, with original English examples, how the principles of number, part of speech, and case turn ambiguous lines into questions with checkable evidence, and how a reading decision gets made.

lessons.title: Influence and Scholarly Discussion
lessons.summary: Presents the scope of Sahib Singh's influence alongside neutral scholarly questions about his method, how defenders respond, and the mature student's balanced stance of rigor with humility.

courses.title: The Sikh Encyclopedic Tradition
courses.summary: This course introduces the encyclopedic and lexicographical legacy of Bhai Kahn Singh Nabha, centered on his monumental reference work the ਮਹਾਨ ਕੋਸ਼. Students learn how this dictionary-encyclopedia was built, how it explains the vocabulary of ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ, and how to use it alongside his other works to study Sikh terms,…
outcomes: Describe the life and scholarly project of Bhai Kahn Singh Nabha and the place of the ਮਹਾਨ ਕੋਸ਼ within it.
Explain what a lexicographical and encyclopedic method is and how it differs from simple translation.
Use an encyclopedia entry to clarify a difficult word in ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ.
Identify the main companion works of the author and what each one was meant to do.
Evaluate the strengths and limits of a reference work as a source for study.
Apply a careful, source-based approach when looking up Sikh terms and concepts.

courses.title: Modern Sikh Literature with Bhai Vir Singh
courses.summary: A university-level survey of the life, works, and lasting influence of Bhai Vir Singh (1872-1957), the writer often called the father of modern Punjabi literature (ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਸਾਹਿਤ). The course studies how his fiction, poetry, prose, and scholarship grew out of the Singh Sabha (ਸਿੰਘ ਸਭਾ) renewal and reshaped Sikh…
outcomes: Explain how the Singh Sabha (ਸਿੰਘ ਸਭਾ) renewal shaped the purpose and reach of Bhai Vir Singh's writing.
Identify his major works by name, including the novels Sundari, Bijay Singh, Satwant Kaur, and Baba Naudh Singh.
Describe how his lyric and epic poetry, such as Rana Surat Singh, use nature imagery to carry spiritual meaning.
Account for his prose and scholarship, including the essay collection Amar Lekh and the commentary Santhya Sri Guru Granth Sahib.
Analyze the unified spiritual vision (ਭਗਤੀ) that runs across the different forms he wrote.
Evaluate his legacy as a builder of modern Punjabi literary culture and read his work with care today.

courses.title: The Sikh Religion in English Scholarship
courses.summary: How Sikhi was presented to the English-speaking world through Max Arthur Macauliffe's six-volume study, The Sikh Religion (1909) — its making in partnership with Sikh scholars, its strengths and limits, and its lasting place in Sikh studies.
outcomes: Describe the structure and scope of Macauliffe's six-volume The Sikh Religion (1909) and how it was organised around the lives of the Gurus.
Explain why an English-language presentation of Sikhi mattered in the colonial period and who its intended readers were.
Identify the Sikh scholars and traditional sources Macauliffe relied on, especially his close work with Bhai Kahn Singh Nabha.
Evaluate the strengths of Macauliffe's method, including his respectful tone and reliance on the ਆਦਿ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ.
Assess the limits of his work, such as its reliance on hagiographic janam-sakhi material and its dated assumptions.
Place Macauliffe within the wider history of Sikh studies alongside later scholars such as J. S. Grewal and the contributors to The Oxford Handbook of Sikh Studies.
references: Macauliffe, Max Arthur. The Sikh Religion: Its Gurus, Sacred Writings and Authors. 6 vols. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1909.

courses.summary: Sikhi and Islam both grew in the soil of South Asia and West Asia, and both place the worship of one God at their center. This course compares them with care and respect. courses.title: Applied Sikh Ethics: Gurmat Wisdom for Modern Dilemmas
courses.summary: A capstone course that takes the ethical principles you already learned and puts them to work on real questions facing people today. We do not invent new rules. Instead, we ask how the steady teachings of Gurbani — truth, honest living, service, humility, and care for all creation — help a thoughtful Sikh reason…
outcomes: Apply core Gurmat principles (truth, honest labour, service, humility, the unity of all life) to concrete modern problems rather than treating them as abstract ideas.

courses.title: The Saint-Soldier and the Ethics of Just War
courses.summary: This course studies how the Sikh tradition thinks about the use of force. The central question is simple but hard: when, if ever, is it right to fight? The Sikh answer is built on two linked ideas — ਧਰਮ ਯੁੱਧ (a righteous struggle) and the ਸੰਤ-ਸਿਪਾਹੀ (the saint-soldier who is devoted to God and also ready to defend…
outcomes: Explain the meaning of ਧਰਮ ਯੁੱਧ (righteous struggle) and how it differs from war fought for land, glory, or revenge.
Describe the figure of the ਸੰਤ-ਸਿਪਾਹੀ (saint-soldier) and how devotion and defence are meant to be held together.

Identify the moral limits Sikh ethics places on the conduct of conflict, including treatment of the weak and the defeated.
Connect the doctrine of ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ (worldly and spiritual authority) to the duty of defending justice.
Evaluate Giani Nahar Singh Ji's reading of the saint-soldier ideal against modern just-war debates and common misunderstandings.

courses.summary: Sikh teaching names five inner forces that quietly rob a person of peace and clear thinking: lust, anger, greed, attachment, and pride. courses.title: Sovereignty and the Khalsa

courses.title: Countless Worlds: Cosmology in Gurbani
courses.summary: A plain-English, graduate-level reading of the vast cosmology pictured in Gurbani: countless realms, suns, moons, and worlds; the unknowable scale of creation; and how this vision sits beside (not inside) modern astronomy, without claiming Gurbani predicts science.
outcomes: Describe the recurring Gurbani theme that creation contains countless worlds, suns, moons, and forms of life, expressed through words of vast multiplicity.
Explain how the imagery of layered regions above and below conveys an unmeasured, many-tiered cosmos rather than a fixed map.
Show why scale in Gurbani serves a devotional and humbling purpose, pointing beyond counting to the limitlessness of the Creator.
Distinguish reverent thematic resonance with modern astronomy from concordism, the flawed habit of reading scientific claims into scripture.
Situate these readings within mainstream Sikh studies scholarship and the cautions scholars raise about interpretation.
Apply careful, non-fabricating reading habits: describing themes faithfully without inventing exact references or treating poetry as data.
references: Singh, Pashaura, and Louis E. Fenech, eds. The Oxford Handbook of Sikh Studies. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2014.
Singh, Nikky-Guninder Kaur. The Birth of the Khalsa: A Feminist Re-Memory of Sikh Identity. Albany: State University of New York Press, 2005.
Singh, Nikky-Guninder Kaur. Sikhism: An Introduction. London: I. B. Tauris, 2011.

lessons.title: The Shape of the Question
lessons.summary: Introduces what Gurbani means by cosmology, why scale matters in it, and the ground rule of this course: describe the themes reverently and avoid reading modern science into the text.

lessons.title: Countless Worlds, Suns, and Moons
lessons.summary: Examines the keyword of countlessness and the picture it builds: not one world but innumerable worlds, each with its own suns and moons.

lessons.title: Layers Above and Below
lessons.summary: Reads the imagery of skies above and nether regions below as a way of saying the cosmos is many-tiered and its limits are unreachable.

lessons.title: Scale as Wonder, Not Measurement
lessons.summary: Argues that Gurbani's enormous numbers are devotional, meant to produce awe and humility and to point beyond counting to the limitless Creator.

lessons.title: Resonance With Modern Astronomy, Carefully
lessons.summary: Explores the genuine emotional resonance between Gurbani's countless worlds and modern cosmology while firmly rejecting concordism.

lessons.title: Reading Faithfully: Method and Cautions
lessons.summary: Gathers the course into a practical method for reading Gurbani's cosmology faithfully, without fabrication or concordism.

courses.title: Creation, Evolution & Hukam
courses.summary: A plain-English, graduate-level reflection on how Sikhi thinks about where the cosmos and life came from. Gurbani does not give a dated, six-day account; it speaks of creation unfolding by ਹੁਕਮ (divine order) over time only the Creator truly knows, and of the soul travelling through many life-forms. We explore why…
outcomes: Explain how Gurbani frames creation as an unfolding of ਹੁਕਮ (divine order/command) rather than a one-off, dated event.
Describe the Gurbani motif that the depth and timing of creation are known to the Creator alone, and what that humility implies for cosmology.
Summarise the Indic and Sikh motif of the soul's journey through 8.4 million life-forms and its place in the tradition's imagination of life's variety.
Distinguish theological reflection on origins from scientific explanation, and articulate why Sikhi is not committed to a literal six-day creation.
Identify and avoid concordism — the error of reading modern science back into scripture or treating scripture as a science textbook.
Discuss why many Sikh thinkers find evolutionary biology compatible with a worldview built on ਹੁਕਮ, process, and an unknowable divine measure.
references: Singh, Pashaura, and Louis E. Fenech, eds. The Oxford Handbook of Sikh Studies. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2014.
Mandair, Arvind-Pal Singh. Sikhism: A Guide for the Perplexed. London: Bloomsbury Academic, 2013.
Singh, Nikky-Guninder Kaur. Sikhism: An Introduction. London: I. B. Tauris, 2011.
McLeod, W. H. Sikhism. London: Penguin, 1997.

lessons.title: How Sikhi Asks the Question of Origins
lessons.summary: Sikhi does not approach 'where did everything come from?' as a dated, literal report. It treats origins as a window onto the Creator and the order that holds reality together.

lessons.title: Creation by Hukam: Order, Not a Calendar Event
lessons.summary: Gurbani's keyword for how things come to be is Hukam, the divine order. Creation is presented less as a single past act and more as the continuous, lawful unfolding of all things.

lessons.title: 'The Creator Alone Knows When': Cosmic Time and Humility
lessons.summary: Gurbani repeatedly refuses to pin a date on creation, insisting the timing is known to the Creator alone. This built-in humility leaves room for whatever deep time science discovers.

lessons.title: Many Forms: The Soul's Journey Through 8.4 Million Life-Forms
lessons.summary: A widely attested Indic and Sikh motif imagines the soul passing through 8.4 million life-forms. We read it carefully — as a picture of life's vast variety and the preciousness of human birth, not as a biology lesson.

lessons.title: Why Sikhi Sits at Ease With Evolutionary Science
lessons.summary: Pulling the threads together: an order-based, process-friendly theology with no fixed creation date and a continuum-of-life imagination has little reason to fear evolutionary biology.

lessons.title: Against Concordism: Keeping Science and Scripture Honest
lessons.summary: The course closes with a methodological guardrail: do not make Gurbani prove science, and do not make science settle theology. Respecting each on its own terms is what keeps the harmony genuine.

courses.title: Air, Water, Earth: Ecology and the Science of Nature in Gurbani
courses.summary: Sikhi reads nature as the living face of the Creator. This course connects the famous closing line of Japji Sahib — air is the Guru, water the father, the earth the great mother — to modern environmental science: ecosystems, interdependence, and the Sikh basis for climate responsibility.
outcomes: Explain the closing teaching of Japji Sahib that names air as the Guru, water as the father, and the earth as the great mother, and read it in plain language.
Define kudrat (nature/creation) and describe how Sikhi treats the natural world as a window onto the Creator rather than as mere raw material.
Connect Gurbani's vision of one interconnected creation to the scientific idea of ecosystems and the interdependence of living things.
Describe how air, water, and soil function as shared life-support systems in both Gurbani's imagery and basic environmental science.
Articulate a Sikh ethical basis for environmental responsibility, drawing on seva, sarbat da bhala, and respect for kudrat.
Apply Gurmat-rooted reasoning to contemporary questions of pollution, conservation, and climate action in everyday life.
references: Cole, W. Owen, and Piara Singh Sambhi. The Sikhs: Their Religious Beliefs and Practices. London: Routledge & Kegan Paul, 1978.
Singh, Pashaura, and Louis E. Fenech, eds. The Oxford Handbook of Sikh Studies. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2014.

lessons.title: Kudrat: Nature as a Window to the Creator

courses.title: Mind, Consciousness, and the Self: Sikh Thought in Dialogue with Science
courses.summary: A graduate-level course that puts the Sikh understanding of mind and self into conversation with modern science. It examines two key ideas in Gurbani, the restless mind (the mind) and the deeper self (the soul or consciousness), and asks how they relate to what neuroscience now says about the brain. It treats…
outcomes: Distinguish the Sikh concepts of the mind and the soul or consciousness, and explain how each is described in Gurbani.
Summarize, modestly and accurately, what well-established neuroscience does and does not show about meditation, attention, and wellbeing.
Explain the relationship between brain and consciousness as both a scientific and a philosophical problem.
Describe Naam Simran as a practice of trained attention and relate it to general research on focused awareness.
Assess why a purely material account of the self is, by itself, an incomplete description from the Sikh point of view.
Evaluate where Sikh thought and science genuinely meet, where they speak past each other, and where each must stay humble.

lessons.summary: Introduces the course and the two central Gurbani terms, the restless mind and the deeper self, and sets up the dialogue with science.

lessons.title: What Neuroscience Can and Cannot Say About Consciousness
lessons.summary: Lays out, modestly, what brain science has established and where the hard problem of consciousness begins.

lessons.title: The Restless Mind and the Science of Attention
lessons.summary: Connects Gurbani's restless mind to ordinary research on attention, distraction, and mind-wandering.

lessons.title: Naam Simran as Trained Attention and Wellbeing
lessons.summary: Examines Naam Simran as a practice of focused remembrance and relates it modestly to research on meditation and wellbeing.

courses.title: Modern Physics, Time, and Hukam: A Capstone
courses.summary: A closing reflection for students who have finished the other science courses. We look honestly at what modern physics actually says about the beginning of the universe, the vastness of deep time, and the law-like order of nature, and we set that next to the Sikh idea of hukam, the divine order, and Gurbani's frank…
outcomes: Summarise, in plain language and without overstatement, what the Big Bang model does and does not claim about the origin of the universe.
Explain why a scientific model of cosmic beginnings is not the same kind of statement as a theological claim about a Creator, and why one cannot be read off the other.
Describe the scale of deep time and cosmic distance, and discuss how that scale reframes human importance without erasing it.
Articulate the Sikh idea of hukam as divine order and connect it carefully to the regularity that physics calls natural law, while noting the limits of the comparison.
Recognise and avoid concordism, the habit of claiming that scripture anticipated modern science, and explain why this move weakens both faith and science.
Reflect on the shared humility of physicist and seeker before the unknown, and state where empirical inquiry ends and theological reflection begins.
references: Pashaura Singh and Louis E. Fenech, eds. The Oxford Handbook of Sikh Studies. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2014.

lessons.title: Deep Time and the Scale of Things
lessons.summary: Walks through the sheer size of cosmic time and distance, and asks how that scale should and should not change how we see ourselves.

lessons.title: Order in Nature and the Idea of Hukam
lessons.summary: Compares the law-like regularity physics finds in nature with the Sikh idea of hukam, and marks the limits of that comparison.

lessons.title: The Mystery of Time and the Limits of Knowing
lessons.summary: Looks at how strange time turns out to be in physics, and how Gurbani frankly places the moment of creation beyond human knowledge.

lessons.title: The Humility of the Physicist and the Seeker
lessons.summary: Closes the track by drawing out the shared humility both vocations require, and naming clearly where each one's authority ends.

courses.title: Sikhi & Science: A Harmonious View
courses.summary: An introduction to how the Sikh tradition relates to modern science. Gurmat invites us to observe and reflect on creation (kudrat), and Sikh thought never developed a "creation versus science" war. This course explains why, distinguishes the kinds of questions spirituality and empirical inquiry each answer, and…
outcomes: Explain why the Sikh tradition has no inherited "creation versus science" conflict and how this differs from some other religious histories.
Describe how Gurmat treats kudrat (creation/nature) as something to be observed, reflected on, and held in wonder.
Distinguish the questions empirical science answers (how, what, when) from those spiritual inquiry addresses (why, meaning, value).
Apply a non-concordist reading of Gurbani that values resonance with science without claiming the Gurus predicted modern theories.
Summarize what academic Sikh studies says about scripture, cosmos, and the limits of literal reading.
Navigate the science section of the course library and choose where to study next.

lessons.title: Kudrat: An Invitation to Observe Creation

lessons.title: No Inherited War: Sikhi and the Science Conflict
lessons.summary: Why the famous religion-versus-science conflict is largely a Western, historically specific story that the Sikh tradition did not inherit.

lessons.title: Different Questions: How Versus Why
lessons.summary: Science explains how the world works; spiritual inquiry addresses meaning, value, and purpose. The two address different questions.

lessons.title: Resonance, Not Prediction
lessons.summary: How to read Gurbani's cosmic imagery honestly: as poetry that resonates with a scientific outlook, not as hidden prediction of modern theories.

courses.title: Science & Religion: Conflict or Harmony?
courses.summary: A graduate-level, plain-English course on the big-picture relationship between science and religion, read through a Sikh lens. It asks why Sikhi never had a 'Galileo moment' or a public war with science, distinguishes the kind of questions science answers (how the world works) from the kind Gurmat addresses (why…
outcomes: Explain why Sikhi has not had a structural 'war with science' like the Galileo episode, and what features of Gurmat make that conflict unlikely.
Distinguish the 'how' questions that empirical science answers from the 'why' and 'meaning' questions that Gurmat addresses, without collapsing one into the other.
Describe the four standard models of the science-religion relationship (conflict, independence, dialogue, integration) and recognise their strengths and weaknesses.
Read selected themes of Gurbani as a worldview of one creative reality and a vast, ordered, awe-inspiring cosmos, while avoiding reading scripture as a science textbook.
Evaluate common claims that science 'disproves' or 'proves' religion, and identify where such claims overreach their evidence.
Articulate a Sikh stance of humble dialogue that takes both empirical inquiry and spiritual insight seriously.
references: Singh, Pashaura, and Louis E. Fenech, eds. The Oxford Handbook of Sikh Studies. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2014.
Mandair, Arvind-Pal Singh. Sikhism: A Guide for the Perplexed. London: Bloomsbury, 2013.
Barbour, Ian G. When Science Meets Religion: Enemies, Strangers, or Partners? San Francisco: HarperSanFrancisco, 2000.

lessons.title: Why No 'Galileo Moment' in Sikhi?
lessons.summary: Sets up the central question, recalls the Galileo episode as the classic image of science-religion war, and explains structural features of Gurmat that have kept Sikhi from a comparable public clash with science.

lessons.title: Two Different Questions: How and Why
lessons.summary: Draws the core distinction between the empirical 'how' questions science answers and the meaning-and-purpose 'why' questions Gurmat addresses, and shows why confusing the two produces most false conflicts.

lessons.title: The Conflict Model and the Warfare Myth
lessons.summary: Examines the first of the four standard models, the conflict model, traces the 'warfare' narrative made famous in the nineteenth century, and shows why historians and Sikh thought both find it too simple.

lessons.title: Independence, Dialogue, and Integration
lessons.summary: Works through the remaining three models, weighing the strengths and limits of keeping the two domains separate, letting them talk, and seeking a unified worldview, and locates Sikhi within them.

lessons.title: Gurbani's Cosmos: Wonder Without a Textbook
lessons.summary: Reads Gurbani's themes of a vast ordered cosmos, divine order, and wonder as a worldview compatible with science, while carefully warning against concordism that treats scripture as a hidden science manual.

lessons.title: A Sikh Stance of Humble Dialogue
lessons.summary: Brings the threads together into a constructive Sikh posture toward science: confident in the Guru's vision, curious about the world, humble about the limits of all knowledge, and resistant to ego-driven certainty on either side.

courses.title: Sikh Women: Leaders, Warriors, and Equal Partners in Sikhi
courses.summary: A history of Sikh women as theologians, regents, military commanders, and Panthic leaders — from Guru Nanak's defence of women to Mata Sundri, Sada Kaur, Maharani Jind Kaur, Mai Bhago, and today.
outcomes: Explain how Guru Nanak's ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ rejected female infanticide, sati, and the social devaluation of women
Identify foundational women named or honoured in Sikh tradition, including Mata Khivi whose seva is recorded in ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ
Describe Mata Sundri's role leading the Panth and issuing ਹੁਕਮਨਾਮੇ after Guru Gobind Singh
Analyse the military and political leadership of Sada Kaur and Maharani Jind Kaur in the Sikh Empire era
Recount the battlefield leadership of Mai Bhago (ਮਾਤਾ ਭਾਗ ਕੌਰ) and Bibi Sharan Kaur
Distinguish Gurbani's teaching on equality from later institutional restrictions such as the SGPC exclusion of women from ਪੰਜ ਪਿਆਰੇ seva

lessons.summary: Sikh women on the battlefield — Mai Bhago who led the forty Muktay back to fight, and Bibi Sharan Kaur of the Chamkaur tradition.

lessons.summary: Two women who shaped the Sikh Empire — Sada Kaur the military commander and kingmaker, and Maharani Jind Kaur the regent who terrified the British.

courses.title: Sundari: The First Punjabi Novel and Its Sikh Vision

courses.title: Bhagti / Bhakti as the Foundation of Sikh Jeevan
courses.summary: An introduction to Bhagti (devotion) as the living foundation of Sikh life. Gurbani teaches that knowledge without devotion is empty pride; this course centres Naam Simran as the root of Sikh jeevan.
outcomes: Define ਭਗਤੀ (Bhagti) as Gurbani presents it, distinguishing it from ritual and mere belief
Explain why Gurbani warns that knowledge without devotion produces only ਅਭਿਮਾਨ (pride)

courses.title: Anhad Shabad: Bhai Randhir Singh's Autobiography of Inner Experience
courses.summary: An advanced study of Bhai Randhir Singh's autobiography, exploring Naam Simran, Anhad Naad, and Sehaj as one of modern Sikh literature's most personal accounts of inner spiritual experience.

Explain the meaning of ਅਨਹਦ ਨਾਦ (Anhad Naad) as taught in Gurbani and distinguish it from ordinary sound

courses.summary: The third Pramaan Sagar course examines how Giani Mal Singh grounds Sikh ethics in Gurbani — seva, kirat karni, family and community conduct, Dasvandh — and reasons through ambiguous moral cases from scriptural evidence.

courses.title: Overcoming the Sikh Inferiority Complex
courses.summary: How colonial history bred a Sikh tendency to shrink, and how Gurbani's vision of universal divine dignity, the spirit of Chardi Kala, and confident historical models restore self-worth rooted in being a child of Waheguru.
outcomes: Trace how colonial rule and post-colonial pressures produced an internalised inferiority complex among many Sikhs.
Explain Gurbani's radical teaching that the same divine light, ਜੋਤਿ, dwells in every being, leaving no ground for self-contempt.

Identify how ਸੰਗਤ (Sangat) and representation rebuild collective Sikh confidence.

courses.title: Jail Chitthian: Bhai Randhir Singh's Letters from Prison
courses.summary: Study Bhai Randhir Singh's Jail Chitthian (Prison Letters), a Sikh spiritual classic on Naam Simran, Gurbani reflection, and Chardi Kala forged in British colonial prisons (1915-1930).

Describe the practice and inner experience of ਨਾਮ ਸਿਮਰਨ (Naam Simran) as presented in the text
Evaluate the concept of ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ (Chardi Kala) as a response to oppression and suffering
Assess the literary and devotional legacy of Jail Chitthian and distinguish AKJ-specific positions from broader Sikh discourse

courses.title: Banda Singh Bahadur: Sikh Sovereignty and Revolutionary Rule
courses.summary: The life and revolution of Banda Singh Bahadur (1670-1716): from the ascetic Madho Das to the first Sikh sovereign, his land reforms, the Battle of Sirhind, and his martyrdom in Delhi.

Explain how Guru Gobind Singh Ji commissioned Banda Singh and the authority of the ਹੁਕਮਨਾਮੇ (hukamnamas) that mobilized the Khalsa

Evaluate Banda Singh's revolutionary land reforms that abolished feudal ਜ਼ਮੀਂਦਾਰੀ (zamindari) and empowered peasant cultivators
Assess the symbols of early Sikh sovereignty: the capital at Lohgarh, coinage, the Nanakshahi calendar seal, and the slogan ਫ਼ਤਹ ਦਰਸ਼ਨ
Reflect on the meaning of Banda Singh Bahadur's capture at Gurdaspur (1715) and his martyrdom in Delhi (1716) as an enduring witness of ਸਿਦਕ (faith)

courses.title: Meat, Drugs, and Alcohol: What Gurbani and Sikh History Actually Say

Distinguish between a cultural Sikh and a practicing Sikh, and locate yourself honestly without shame on that spectrum

courses.title: Sri Gur Pratap Suraj Granth: An Introduction
courses.source: Sri Gur Pratap Suraj Granth by Kavi Santokh Singh
courses.summary: A scholarly introduction to the ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਤਾਪ ਸੂਰਜ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ of ਕਵੀ ਸੰਤੋਖ ਸਿੰਘ (1769-1843) — the vast 51,820-verse poetic biography of the Ten Gurus and Banda Singh Bahadur. The course surveys its twelve ਰਾਸ volumes plus the ਗੁਰ ਨਾਨਕ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼, its ਬ੍ਰਜ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ idiom, its composition under Sikh patronage at ਕੈਥਲ, the rich ਟੀਕਾ tradition it generated, and its complex standing between devotional masterpiece and contested historical source.
outcomes: Identify Kavi Santokh Singh and outline the major phases of his life and literary career from Amritsar to Kaithal.
Describe the overall architecture of the Suraj Granth, including the Gur Nanak Prakash and the twelve Raas of the Suraj Prakash, and explain the solar metaphor encoded in its structure.
Explain the linguistic character of the work as Braj Bhasha shaped by Punjabi, Sanskrit and Persian vocabulary, and why this idiom was chosen.
Situate the Granth within the patronage networks of Kaithal, Buria and the Phulkian states that made its composition possible.
Trace the reception history of the text, including Bhai Vir Singh's monumental annotated edition and the Sampardai katha tradition.
Critically evaluate the Granth as a historical source, distinguishing its devotional and hagiographic registers from verifiable history.
Assess the scholarly contributions of Rattan Singh Jaggi and others who have produced critical apparatus, dictionaries and studies of the work.

courses.title: Gurbilas Patshahi 10: Guru Gobind Singh Ji's Court
courses.summary: An advanced study of the ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹੀ ੧੦, Koer Singh's mid-eighteenth-century poetic biography of ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ. The course examines the text as a foundational work of early Sikh historiography: its genre and ਕਵਿ conventions, the courtly world of ਪਾਉਂਟਾ ਸਾਹਿਬ and its ਬੱਤੀ ਕਵੀ (fifty-two poets), the founding of the ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ, the ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ period and its battles, the place of the ਦਸਮ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ, and the great ਸਾਖੀਆਂ of ਭਾਈ ਦਯਾ ਸਿੰਘ and ਭਾਈ ਮਨੀ ਸਿੰਘ. Students learn to read a ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ critically — weighing its devotional aims, its ਪੁਰਾਤਨ sources, and its contested reliability — guided throughout by the scholarship of Piara Singh Padam, who edited and annotated the standard modern edition.
outcomes: Define the ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ as a literary and historiographical genre and situate Koer Singh's c.1751 text within it
Analyse the courtly culture of ਪਾਉਂਟਾ ਸਾਹਿਬ, the role of the ਬੱਤੀ ਕਵੀ, and Guru Gobind Singh Ji's patronage of letters
Reconstruct the founding of the ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ at ਵਿਸਾਖੀ 1699 as Koer Singh narrates it and compare it with other ਪੁਰਾਤਨ sources
Trace the ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ battles and the role of the ਪੰਜ ਪਿਆਰੇ in the Gurbilas account
Evaluate the text's treatment of the ਦਸਮ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ and its composition
Critically assess the major ਸਾਖੀਆਂ of ਭਾਈ ਦਯਾ ਸਿੰਘ and ਭਾਈ ਮਨੀ ਸਿੰਘ for historical and didactic value
Apply scholarly methods of source criticism, drawing on Piara Singh Padam's editorial apparatus, to read early Sikh chronicles responsibly

courses.title: Gurbilas Patshahi 6: Guru Hargobind Ji and Miri-Piri
courses.summary: An advanced study of the Gurbilas Patshahi 6, the early Sikh verse-chronicle (ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ) celebrating the reign of Guru Hargobind Ji, the sixth Nanak. The course examines the text as a literary and historical source for the doctrine of ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ — the union of temporal and spiritual sovereignty — the founding of the ਅਕਾਲ ਤਖ਼ਤ, the militarisation of the Panth, the four battles against Mughal forces, the Guru's imprisonment in Gwalior, his relations with Emperor Jahangir, and the development of Amritsar and the Kartarpur period. Students engage critically with questions of authorship, dating, and the place of ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ literature within the wider corpus of Sikh historiography.
outcomes: Explain the genre of ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ literature and locate Gurbilas Patshahi 6 within the development of Sikh historical writing, including the scholarly debates over its authorship and date.
Analyse the doctrine of ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ as articulated through the imagery of the two swords and the founding of the ਅਕਾਲ ਤਖ਼ਤ, and assess how the text theologises Sikh sovereignty.
Reconstruct the principal military engagements of Guru Hargobind Ji's reign as narrated in the text and evaluate their reliability against other primary sources.
Interpret the Guru's imprisonment at Gwalior and his relations with Emperor Jahangir as presented in the chronicle and in Mughal sources.
Assess the role of Amritsar, the ਲੋਹਗੜ੍ਹ fort, and the Kartarpur period in the institutional consolidation of the Panth.
Evaluate the historiographical value and limitations of Gurbilas Patshahi 6 as a source for seventeenth-century Sikh history.

courses.title: Suraj Prakash: Guru Gobind Singh Ji — The Warrior-Saint
courses.source: Sri Gur Pratap Suraj Granth, Rut 6-12 by Kavi Santokh Singh
courses.summary: An advanced textual and historical seminar on the portions of Kavi Santokh Singh's monumental Sri Gur Pratap Suraj Granth (1843) that narrate the life of the tenth Master, ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ. Reading the relevant Ruts of the Suraj Prakash alongside primary contemporary sources — the ਬਚਿੱਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ, the ਜ਼ਫ਼ਰਨਾਮਾ, the rehatnamas, and the Bhatt vahis — students examine the Guru's birth at Patna, the Paonta years and the literary darbar of fifty-two poets, the founding of the ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ in 1699, the battles of Bhangani, Nadaun, and the Anandpur sieges, the evacuation and shaheedis at Chamkaur and Sirhind, the composition of the ਜ਼ਫ਼ਰਨਾਮਾ, the southern journey, and the conferral of eternal Guruship upon ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ. The course foregrounds the figure of the ਸੰਤ-ਸਿਪਾਹੀ and trains students to read Braj-inflected nineteenth-century Sikh hagiography critically, distinguishing kavi convention from historical kernel.
outcomes: Situate Kavi Santokh Singh's ਸੂਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ within the genre of Sikh hagiographical literature and explain its sources, language, and prosodic structure of Ruts and Ainsus.
Reconstruct the chronology of ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ's life from birth at Patna (1666) to joti-jot at Nanded (1708) using both the Suraj Prakash and corroborating primary sources.
Analyze the theological meaning of the ਸੰਤ-ਸਿਪਾਹੀ ideal and the doctrine of ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ as embodied in the Guru's life.
Explain the creation of the ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ in 1699, the role of the ਪੰਜ ਪਿਆਰੇ, and the institution of ਖੰਡੇ ਦੀ ਪਾਹੁਲ.
Critically read the Guru's battles — Bhangani, Nadaun, Anandpur — as narrated in the Suraj Prakash against the ਬਚਿੱਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ.
Interpret the shaheedis of the ਸਾਹਿਬਜ਼ਾਦੇ at Chamkaur and Sirhind and their place in Sikh collective memory.
Read and contextualize the ਜ਼ਫ਼ਰਨਾਮਾ as an epistle of moral victory addressed to Aurangzeb.
Explain the doctrinal significance of the command conferring eternal Guruship upon ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ.

courses.title: Suraj Prakash: The Life of Guru Nanak Dev Ji
courses.source: Sri Gur Pratap Suraj Granth, Rut 1 by Kavi Santokh Singh
courses.summary: An intermediate, semester-length study of the life of ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ as narrated in the first Rut (ਰੁੱਤ) of Kavi Santokh Singh's monumental Braj-Punjabi epic ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਤਾਪ ਸੂਰਜ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ, popularly called ਸੂਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼. Following the framework of Dr. Rattan Singh Jaggi's critical scholarship, the course reads the Suraj Prakash account of ਜਨਮ-ਸਾਖੀ tradition alongside its sources, tracing Guru Nanak's birth at ਰਾਇ ਭੋਇ ਦੀ ਤਲਵੰਡੀ, the childhood ਸਾਖੀਆਂ of the snake's shade and the grazed fields, the Sultanpur years and the ਵੇਈਂ revelation, the four ਉਦਾਸੀਆਂ, the great encounters with ਸੱਜਣ ਠੱਗ, ਭਾਈ ਲਾਲੋ, ਮਲਿਕ ਭਾਗੋ and ਵਲੀ ਕੰਧਾਰੀ, and the founding of ਕਰਤਾਰਪੁਰ. Throughout, students learn to read the text critically — as ਹੈਜੀਓਗ੍ਰਾਫੀ (hagiography), as theology, and as a literary monument of nineteenth-century Sikh devotional historiography.
outcomes: Situate ਸੂਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ within the wider ਜਨਮ-ਸਾਖੀ and ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ literary traditions and identify Kavi Santokh Singh's sources and method.
Narrate the major episodes of Guru Nanak's life as told in Rut 1, from ਜਨਮ at Talwandi to ਜੋਤੀ-ਜੋਤਿ at Kartarpur.
Distinguish between the historical kernel, the devotional embellishment, and the theological purpose of each ਸਾਖੀ.
Read selected ਚੌਪਈ and ਦੋਹਰਾ passages and explain their Braj-influenced poetic conventions.
Analyze the Suraj Prakash miracle narratives (the ਨਾਗ shade, the grazing buffaloes, the moved boulder of ਵਲੀ ਕੰਧਾਰੀ) as theological statements rather than mere wonders.
Evaluate scholarly debates about the historicity of the ਉਦਾਸੀਆਂ and the chronology of Guru Nanak's travels.
Apply the critical methods of Dr. Rattan Singh Jaggi, W. H. McLeod, and others to a primary-source hagiographical text.

courses.title: Vaaran Bhai Gurdas: The Formation of the Sikh Panth
courses.summary: An intermediate, semester-length study of the first six Vaars of Bhai Gurdas Ji — the writings Guru Arjan Dev Ji called the ਕੁੰਜੀ (key) to Sri Guru Granth Sahib. Reading these Vaars as both devotional poetry and the earliest Sikh historiography, the course traces how the ਪੰਥ was formed: the cosmic mission behind Guru Nanak Sahib's coming, the gift of ਗੁਰਮੁਖੀ under Guru Angad Dev Ji, ਸੰਗਤ and ਪੰਗਤ under Guru Amar Das Ji, the founding of Amritsar under Guru Ram Das Ji, the compilation of the Adi Granth under Guru Arjan Dev Ji, and the doctrine of ਮੀਰੀ ਪੀਰੀ under Guru Hargobind Sahib.
outcomes: Situate Bhai Gurdas Ji within the early Sikh tradition and explain why his Vaars are called the key to Sri Guru Granth Sahib.
Reconstruct the cosmic and historical narrative of Vaar 1 — the condition of the world before Guru Nanak Sahib, his mission, and the ਉਦਾਸੀਆਂ.
Trace the institutional development of the Panth across the Guruship from Guru Angad Dev Ji to Guru Hargobind Sahib as narrated in Vaars 2-6.
Explain the doctrinal vocabulary of these Vaars, including ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ, ਮਨਮੁਖਿ, ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ, and ਮੀਰੀ ਪੀਰੀ.
Read selected pauris in Gurmukhi with attention to imagery, metre, and theological argument.
Evaluate the Vaars as a source for Sikh historiography alongside the work of modern scholars.
Apply the ethical vision of the Vaars — humility, seva, and the discipline of the Gurmukh — to the lived practice of Sikhi.

courses.title: Naam Simran: The Practice of Divine Remembrance
courses.source: Gurbani — Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
courses.summary: An academically rigorous, devotionally grounded study of ਨਾਮ ਸਿਮਰਨ (the remembrance of the Divine Name) as taught throughout Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. The course moves from the theology of ਨਾਮ through its disciplines—ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲਾ, ਅਜਪਾ ਜਾਪ, and the ਗੁਰਮੰਤ੍ਰ—to the obstacles of ਹਉਮੈ and the ਪੰਜ ਵਿਕਾਰ, the inner experience of ਅਨਹਦ ਸ਼ਬਦ, and the integration of remembrance into daily life. Throughout, students engage directly with Gurbani at its original Ang references.
outcomes: Define ਨਾਮ theologically and distinguish mechanical recitation from absorbed ਸਿਮਰਨ.
Explain the Gurmat teaching on ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲਾ and the disciplines of ਨਾਮ ਜਪਣਾ.
Analyse the role of the ਗੁਰੂ and ਸ਼ਬਦ in transmitting ਨਾਮ.
Identify the obstacles of ਹਉਮੈ and the ਪੰਜ ਵਿਕਾਰ and how Gurbani dissolves them.
Describe the nature of ਮਨ and the experience of ਅਨਹਦ ਸ਼ਬਦ.
Integrate ਨਾਮ into ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰਨੀ and cultivate a lifelong practice oriented toward ਨਦਰਿ.

courses.title: Bansavalinama: The Lineage of the Gurus
courses.source: Bansavalinama Dasan Patsahian Ka by Kesar Singh Chibbar
courses.summary: An intermediate seminar on the ਬੰਸਾਵਲੀਨਾਮਾ ਦਸਾਂ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹੀਆਂ ਕਾ (c.1769) of ਕੇਸਰ ਸਿੰਘ ਛਿੱਬਰ — one of the earliest connected biographical chronicles of all ten Gurus composed in Braj-inflected Punjabi verse. Students examine its structure of ten ਚਰਨ (chapters), its distinctive genealogical material on the Guru families, its theological vision of Sikhi as ਮੀਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਪੀਰੀ, and the Chibbar family's privileged access to the institutional memory of the Guru-darbar as ਦੀਵਾਨ and ਦਿਵਾਨੀ scribes. The course rigorously assesses both the historical value and the well-documented limitations of the text, comparing it with the ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ tradition, the Gur Bilas literature, and modern critical historiography.
outcomes: Trace the compositional structure of the ਬੰਸਾਵਲੀਨਾਮਾ across its ten ਚਰਨ and situate it within eighteenth-century Sikh literary production.
Identify the unique genealogical and biographical information the text preserves about the families of the ten Gurus and evaluate its reliability against corroborating sources.
Analyse the Braj Bhasha poetics, idiom, and oral-formulaic features of Chibbar's verse and what they reveal about his audience and intentions.
Reconstruct the Chibbar family's hereditary service as ਦੀਵਾਨ to the later Gurus and explain how this access shaped the chronicle's perspective and biases.
Compare the ਬੰਸਾਵਲੀਨਾਮਾ critically with the ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ, ਗੁਰ ਬਿਲਾਸ, and Gurbilas Patshahi 6 traditions on key events.
Apply source-critical methods to distinguish the text's verifiable historical core from its hagiographic, polemical, and Brahmanical embellishments.

courses.title: Vaaran Bhai Gurdas: A Key to the Guru Granth Sahib
courses.source: Vaaran Bhai Gurdas by Bhai Gurdas Ji
courses.summary: An intermediate course on the forty ਵਾਰਾਂ of ਭਾਈ ਗੁਰਦਾਸ ਜੀ — the scribe of the Adi Granth, first ਜਥੇਦਾਰ of the Akal Takhat, and the poet whose work Guru Arjan Dev Ji called ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ ਦੀ ਕੁੰਜੀ, the key to Gurbani. Students study his biography, the structure and language of the Vaaran and Kabitt-Savaiye, and the theological framework through which he interprets ਗੁਰਮਤਿ for the ordinary ਗੁਰਸਿੱਖ.
outcomes: Narrate the life of ਭਾਈ ਗੁਰਦਾਸ ਜੀ and his service across the period of four Gurus, including his role in scribing the ਆਦਿ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ.
Explain why Guru Arjan Dev Ji named the Vaaran the ਕੁੰਜੀ (key) to the Guru Granth Sahib and what 'key' means hermeneutically.
Describe the poetic architecture of the forty ਵਾਰਾਂ, the ਪਉੜੀ form, and the distinct ਕਬਿੱਤ-ਸਵਈਏ.
Analyze the central theological themes — ਗੁਰੂ, ਸ਼ਬਦ, ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ, ਗੁਰਮੁਖ, ਹਉਮੈ — as Bhai Gurdas develops them.
Read selected ਪਉੜੀਆਂ closely, identifying metaphor, parable, and historical allusion.
Situate the Vaaran within the wider literary and exegetical tradition of Sikhi and evaluate their authority in the Panth.
references: Bhai Gurdas. Vaaran Bhai Gurdas Ji. Annotated edition by Bhai Vir Singh. Amritsar: Khalsa Samachar, multiple editions.

courses.title: Panth Prakash: Sikh History 1700–1800
courses.source: Sri Panth Prakash by Giani Gian Singh
courses.summary: An advanced, semester-length study of Giani Gian Singh's Sri Panth Prakash (late 19th c.), the monumental Punjabi verse-and-prose chronicle of the eighteenth-century ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ. The course examines the text's methodology and sources, its account of the Sikh struggle from Guru Gobind Singh Ji and Baba Banda Singh Bahadur through the era of the ਜਥੇ and ਮਿਸਲਾਂ, the two ਘੱਲੂਘਾਰੇ, the rise of the ਸਰਬੱਤ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ and ਗੁਰਮਤਾ, and the consolidation of sovereignty under ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਰਣਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ. Throughout, students learn to read Panth Prakash critically as historiography — weighing its devotional purpose, oral and documentary sources, chronological reliability, and its decisive contribution to the Sikh historical imagination.
outcomes: Situate Giani Gian Singh and the ਨਿਰਮਲ scholarly tradition within nineteenth-century Sikh historiography and explain why Sri Panth Prakash was written.
Analyze the methodology and source-base of Panth Prakash — oral testimony, earlier gurbilas and rahitnama literature, Persian akhbarat, and eyewitness chains — and assess its reliability.
Reconstruct the major episodes of the 1700–1800 century as narrated by Giani Gian Singh: Baba Banda Singh Bahadur, the persecutions, the two ਘੱਲੂਘਾਰੇ, and the rise of the ਮਿਸਲਾਂ.
Explain the institutional logic of the eighteenth-century Panth — ਸਰਬੱਤ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ, ਗੁਰਮਤਾ, ਰਾਖੀ, and ਦਲ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ — through Panth Prakash's account.
Evaluate Panth Prakash alongside parallel sources (Rattan Singh Bhangu, Persian chronicles, colonial historians) to distinguish corroborated history from hagiographic embellishment.
Articulate the lasting contribution of Giani Gian Singh's corpus to ਸਿੱਖ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ and modern Sikh self-understanding.

courses.title: Das Gur Katha: Stories of the Ten Gurus
courses.summary: An intermediate survey of ਦਸ ਗੁਰ ਕਥਾ as a genre of Sikh biographical literature. Students examine the major works that narrate the lives of the Ten Gurus — the ਸਾਖੀ tradition, the ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ corpus, the ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ literature, and modern hagiographic and critical biographies — analyzing their sources, literary styles, and theological frameworks. The course explores how the same events are remembered differently across competing biographical traditions, and how narrative (ਕਥਾ) became one of the primary vehicles for transmitting Sikh theology, ethics, and communal memory.
outcomes: Define ਦਸ ਗੁਰ ਕਥਾ as a literary genre and distinguish it from ਇਤਿਹਾਸ (formal history) and devotional ਕੀਰਤਨ
Identify the major textual traditions that narrate the lives of the Ten Gurus, including the ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ, ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ, and ਸੂਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ corpora
Analyze the literary devices, oral roots, and theological aims of the ਸਾਖੀ form
Compare how different biographical traditions portray the same Guru or event, and explain why these portrayals diverge
Evaluate the relationship between hagiography, communal memory, and verifiable history in Sikh sources
Apply critical reading skills to interpret a ਸਾਖੀ for both its narrative and its doctrinal message

courses.title: Twarikh Guru Khalsa: A Systematic Sikh History
courses.source: Twarikh Guru Khalsa by Giani Gian Singh
courses.summary: An advanced study of ਤਵਾਰੀਖ਼ ਗੁਰੂ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ, Giani Gian Singh's monumental late-nineteenth-century prose history of the Ten ਗੁਰੂ Sahiban and the early ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ. The course examines the text's scope, its synthesis of ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ, ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ, ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ, ਰਹਿਤਨਾਮੇ, and Indo-Persian chronicle traditions, its relationship to the author's earlier verse ਪੰਥ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼, and its position within nineteenth-century ਸਿੰਘ ਸਭਾ historiography. Students engage critically with scholarly debates over the work's reliability, its narrative method, and its enduring impact on modern Sikh historical consciousness.
outcomes: Trace the structure and scope of ਤਵਾਰੀਖ਼ ਗੁਰੂ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ across its treatment of all Ten ਗੁਰੂ Sahiban and the early ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ.
Analyze how Giani Gian Singh integrated ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ, ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ, ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ, and Indo-Persian chronicle sources into a single continuous narrative.
Compare ਤਵਾਰੀਖ਼ ਗੁਰੂ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ with the author's earlier ਸ਼੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰ ਪੰਥ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ and with rival nineteenth-century histories.
Evaluate the historiographical debates concerning the text's reliability, method, and theological framing.
Situate the work within the intellectual context of the ਸਿੰਘ ਸਭਾ movement and colonial-era Punjab.
Assess the lasting influence of the text on modern Sikh historical memory, vernacular pedagogy, and scholarship.

courses.title: Vaaran Bhai Gurdas: Spiritual Practice and Inner Life
courses.summary: An advanced theological study of Vaars 7 through 15 of the Vaaran Bhai Gurdas — the work Guru Arjan Sahib called the ਕੁੰਜੀ (key) to Sri Guru Granth Sahib. This course undertakes an extended textual and devotional reading of Bhai Gurdas's mapping of the inner life: ਨਾਮ ਸਿਮਰਨ as the ground of practice, the contrast of ਗੁਰਮੁਖ and ਮਨਮੁਖ, the disciplines of ਸੇਵਾ and ਸੰਗਤ, the relocation of ਤੀਰਥ from outer pilgrimage to inner purification, the meaning of ਧਰਮ, and the social ethics of compassion and humility. Students learn to read the Vaaran as a sustained practical theology of how a Sikh actually lives, drawing on classical and modern commentary to recover Bhai Gurdas as the first systematic interpreter of Gurmat.
outcomes: Explain why Guru Arjan Sahib named the Vaaran the ਕੁੰਜੀ (key) to Sri Guru Granth Sahib and analyze how Bhai Gurdas functions as the earliest systematic theologian of Gurmat
Trace Bhai Gurdas's account of ਨਾਮ ਸਿਮਰਨ as the foundation of spiritual practice and articulate its relationship to ਗੁਰਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ (grace) and ਮਿਹਰ
Distinguish the ਗੁਰਮੁਖ from the ਮਨਮੁਖ as competing orientations of the self and apply this typology to lived ethical decisions
Analyze ਸੇਵਾ and ਸੰਗਤ as the two outward disciplines through which the inner life is cultivated and tested
Critically assess Bhai Gurdas's reframing of ਤੀਰਥ from geographical pilgrimage to the inner ਤੀਰਥ of the Guru's word and the ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ
Interpret Bhai Gurdas's vision of ਧਰਮ, ਨਿਮਰਤਾ (humility), and ਦਇਆ (compassion) as a coherent social ethic rooted in spiritual discipline

lessons.title: The ਕੁੰਜੀ to Gurbani: Bhai Gurdas as Sikhi's First Theologian
lessons.summary: Introduces Bhai Gurdas, the standing of the Vaaran, and the method of reading Vaars 7-15 as a practical theology of the inner life.

lessons.title: Vaar 7: ਨਾਮ ਸਿਮਰਨ as the Foundation of Practice
lessons.summary: Reads Vaar 7's account of remembrance of the Name as the root discipline, examining its relation to grace and the transformation of the mind.

lessons.title: Vaar 8 (I): The Portrait of the ਗੁਰਮੁਖ
lessons.summary: Examines Bhai Gurdas's idealized portrait of the Guru-oriented person, the qualities of the ਗੁਰਮੁਖ, and the path of self-surrender.

lessons.title: Vaar 8 (II): The Pathology of the ਮਨਮੁਖ
lessons.summary: Analyzes Bhai Gurdas's diagnosis of the self-oriented person, the workings of ਹਉਮੈ, and the consequences of a life turned away from the Guru.

lessons.title: Vaar 9: ਸੇਵਾ — Service as the School of Humility
lessons.summary: Studies Bhai Gurdas's theology of selfless service as the practical means by which ਹਉਮੈ is dissolved and the ਗੁਰਮੁਖ is formed.

lessons.title: Vaar 10: ਸੰਗਤ and the ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ
lessons.summary: Explores Bhai Gurdas's theology of holy congregation as the transformative community at the heart of Sikh spiritual practice.

lessons.title: Vaar 11: From Outer ਤੀਰਥ to Inner Pilgrimage
lessons.summary: Examines Bhai Gurdas's reinterpretation of pilgrimage, relocating the sacred bathing place from rivers to the Guru's word and the inner self.

lessons.title: Vaar 12: ਧਰਮ — Righteous Living Rooted in Remembrance
lessons.summary: Studies Bhai Gurdas's conception of righteous living, the householder ideal, and the grounding of ethics in spiritual discipline rather than ritual.

lessons.title: Vaars 13-14: Social Ethics, ਦਇਆ, and the Mark of the Sikh
lessons.summary: Examines how the inner disciplines flower into social virtues — compassion, just dealing, and the distinctive ethical marks of the Sikh.

lessons.title: Vaar 15: ਨਿਮਰਤਾ — Humility as the Crown of the Inner Life
lessons.summary: Studies Bhai Gurdas's culminating teaching that humility is both the root and the crown of spiritual attainment, gathering all the disciplines into one.

lessons.title: Synthesis: The Architecture of Spiritual Discipline in the Vaaran
lessons.summary: Draws together Vaars 7-15 into a coherent practical theology and reflects on Bhai Gurdas's enduring contribution to Sikh spiritual life.

lessons.title: The Gurmukh and the Manmukh: Two Orientations of the Self

courses.title: Vaaran Bhai Gurdas: Social Ethics and Community Life
courses.summary: This intermediate course examines Vaars 26-40 of ਵਾਰਾਂ ਭਾਈ ਗੁਰਦਾਸ as a social charter for the early Sikh community. Reading ਭਾਈ ਗੁਰਦਾਸ as the first authoritative interpreter of ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ, students explore how the Vaars articulate a revolutionary social ethic: the rejection of ਜਾਤ-ਪਾਤ, the dignity of women, the economy of ਲੰਗਰ and ਸੇਵਾ, the ethics of the Sikh merchant and householder, and the institutions—the ਧਰਮਸਾਲ, the ਸੰਗਤ, and the ਗ੍ਰੰਥੀ—that bound the ਪੰਥ together. The course treats the Vaars not as abstract poetry but as a lived constitution for the ਗੁਰਮੁਖ within the ਸਾਧ ਸੰਗਤ.
outcomes: Explain why ਵਾਰਾਂ ਭਾਈ ਗੁਰਦਾਸ are called the ਕੁੰਜੀ (key) to ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ and how they function as the earliest exegesis of the ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ.
Analyze the rejection of ਜਾਤ-ਪਾਤ and ਵਰਨ-ਆਸ਼ਰਮ in Vaars 26-40 and contrast it with prevailing Brahmanical social order.
Describe the social economy of ਲੰਗਰ, ਸੇਵਾ, and ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰਨੀ as a model of redistributive community life.
Evaluate the status and dignity of women in the early Sikh community as reflected in the Vaars and contemporary Gurmat.
Assess the business ethics of the Sikh merchant and householder (ਗ੍ਰਿਹਸਤੀ) including ਵੰਡ ਛਕਣਾ and honest trade.
Articulate the role of the ਧਰਮਸਾਲ, ਸੰਗਤ, and ਗ੍ਰੰਥੀ in institutionalizing the early ਪੰਥ as a social charter.

lessons.title: ਸੇਵਾ: The Ethic of Selfless Service

lessons.title: Women in the Early Sikh Community

lessons.title: ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰਨੀ and the Ethics of the Sikh Merchant

lessons.title: The ਗ੍ਰਿਹਸਤੀ Ideal: Spirituality in the World

lessons.title: The ਗੁਰਮੁਖ and the ਮਨਮੁਖ as Social Types
lessons.summary: Analyzes the contrast between the Guru-oriented and self-willed person as the ethical centre of the Vaars' social vision.

lessons.title: Sikhs and Non-Sikhs: Boundaries and Neighbourliness
lessons.summary: Explores how the Vaars define Sikh identity while teaching respect and good relations with non-Sikhs.

lessons.title: The Vaars as a Living Constitution: Synthesis
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the course into an integrated account of the Vaars as a social charter and considers their enduring significance.

courses.title: Bhai Nand Lal Goya: Life, Times, and Literary Legacy
courses.source: Collected Works of Bhai Nand Lal Goya
courses.summary: A comprehensive intermediate study of ਭਾਈ ਨੰਦ ਲਾਲ ਜੀ "ਗੋਯਾ" (c. 1633-1713), the Persian-trained scholar of Ghazni who became one of the most beloved Sikhs of ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ and one of the ਪੰਜ ਵਿਦਵਾਨ of the Anandpur court. The course traces his youth on the Mughal frontier, his service at the imperial court of Bahadur Shah, his transformative arrival at Anandpur Sahib, and his Persian and Punjabi compositions — ਦੀਵਾਨ-ਏ-ਗੋਯਾ, ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀਨਾਮਾ, ਗੰਜਨਾਮਾ, ਤਨਖਾਹਨਾਮਾ and others — situating him as the bridge between the classical Persian literary tradition and Sikh theology.
outcomes: Reconstruct the biography of ਭਾਈ ਨੰਦ ਲਾਲ ਜੀ from Ghazni to Anandpur Sahib, distinguishing documented fact from later hagiographic tradition.
Explain the literary-historical context of Indo-Persian ਫ਼ਾਰਸੀ poetry and the ਤਸੱਵੁਫ਼ (Sufi) tradition that shaped his idiom.
Analyze the major works — ਦੀਵਾਨ-ਏ-ਗੋਯਾ, ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀਨਾਮਾ, ਗੰਜਨਾਮਾ, ਤਨਖਾਹਨਾਮਾ, ਰਹਿਤਨਾਮਾ — for their theology, form, and audience.
Evaluate how ਗੋਯਾ translated Sikh concepts of ਨਾਮ, ਗੁਰੂ and ਪ੍ਰੇਮ into the vocabulary of Persian mysticism.
Assess his historical significance as a cultural bridge and as a primary witness to the court of ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ.
Apply critical methods to the textual transmission and authenticity debates surrounding works attributed to him.

courses.title: Ghazaliyat of Bhai Nand Lal: Sikh Persian Poetry
courses.source: Ghazaliyat by Bhai Nand Lal Goya
courses.summary: An advanced literary and theological study of the ਗ਼ਜ਼ਲੀਆਤ (Ghazaliyat) of ਭਾਈ ਨੰਦ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਯਾ, the foremost Persian poet of the court of ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ. The course reads the Persian ghazal as a vessel for ਗੁਰਮਤਿ: students master the formal architecture of the ghazal (ਮਤਲਾ, ਰਦੀਫ਼, ਕਾਫ਼ੀਆ, ਮਕਤਾ, ਤਖ਼ੱਲੁਸ), trace how Goya transforms the Sufi vocabulary of divine love into devotion to the Guru as ਮਹਿਬੂਬ (Beloved), and situate his verse beside ਰੂਮੀ and ਹਾਫ਼ਿਜ਼. Special attention is given to how Goya names ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ within Persian imagery, the doctrine of ਫ਼ਨਾ (annihilation of the self) recast as merger in the Guru, and the place of his ਦੀਵਾਨ-ਏ-ਗੋਯਾ in the broader Sikh literary canon.
outcomes: Analyze the formal structure of the Persian ghazal — ਮਤਲਾ, ਰਦੀਫ਼, ਕਾਫ਼ੀਆ, ਬੈਤ, and ਮਕਤਾ — and identify these elements within Bhai Nand Lal's ਦੀਵਾਨ-ਏ-ਗੋਯਾ.
Explain how ਭਾਈ ਨੰਦ ਲਾਲ adapts the Sufi conceit of the divine ਮਹਿਬੂਬ to express devotion to the Guru and to ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ.
Compare Goya's mysticism of love and ਫ਼ਨਾ with that of ਰੂਮੀ and ਹਾਫ਼ਿਜ਼, noting both inheritance and theological departure.
Interpret key Persian-Sikh images — wine, the cup-bearer, the moth and flame, the face of the Beloved — as ਗੁਰਮਤਿ symbols rather than literal indulgence.
Situate the Ghazaliyat within the wider corpus of Bhai Nand Lal (ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀਨਾਮਾ, ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹਨਾਮਾ, ਜੋਤਿ ਬਿਗਾਸ) and within Persianate Sikh literature.
Evaluate the use of ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ and ਨਾਮ in a Persian poetic register and assess what is gained theologically by writing Sikh devotion in Persian.
Read selected ਅਸ਼ਆਰ (couplets) closely, attending to sound, the turn of the radif, and the signature of the ਮਕਤਾ.

courses.title: Zindagi Nama: Bhai Nand Lal's Autobiography in Verse
courses.source: Zindagi Nama by Bhai Nand Lal Goya
courses.summary: An advanced literary and devotional study of the Zindagi Nama (Book of Life), the great Persian masnavi of ਭਾਈ ਨੰਦ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਯਾ, court-poet of ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ. Reading the poem as a versified spiritual autobiography, the course traces Goya's journey from Persianate scholar of Ghazni and Multan to a ਗੁਰਸਿੱਖ at Anandpur Sahib, and examines how the masnavi form carries an interior account of the ਗੁਰੂ-ਸਿੱਖ relationship, ਨਾਮ ਸਿਮਰਨ, and the ethics of devotion. Students learn to read the Zindagi Nama both as world literature in the masnavi tradition and as a unique first-person witness to life in the Guru's court, while attending to its theology of ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ, ਹੁਕਮ, and ਬੰਦਗੀ. Key concepts and terms are presented in Gurmukhi Unicode throughout.
outcomes: Situate the Zindagi Nama within the corpus of ਭਾਈ ਨੰਦ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਯਾ and within the wider Persianate and Sikh literary worlds.
Explain the conventions of the masnavi form and analyze how its rhyming couplets shape the work as a versified spiritual autobiography.
Trace the spiritual milestones of Goya's life from Persian scholar to ਗੁਰਸਿੱਖ as the poem itself narrates them.
Interpret the Zindagi Nama's theology of ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ, ਨਾਮ, ਹੁਕਮ, and ਬੰਦਗੀ in relation to mainstream ਗੁਰਮਤਿ.
Analyze how the poem portrays the ਗੁਰੂ-ਸਿੱਖ relationship and the figure of the ਮੁਰਸ਼ਿਦ-Guru.
Assess the Zindagi Nama as a historical source for life in the court of ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ at Anandpur Sahib.
Evaluate problems of language, translation, and reception that shape how the poem is read today.
Compose a sustained scholarly close reading of a passage from the Zindagi Nama using primary text and secondary scholarship.

courses.title: Jot Bigas and Rah-i-Rast: Bhai Nand Lal's Punjabi Works
courses.source: Jot Bigas and Rah-i-Rast by Bhai Nand Lal Goya
courses.summary: This intermediate course examines the two Punjabi compositions of ਭਾਈ ਨੰਦ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਯਾ, the celebrated court poet of ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ: the ਜੋਤਿ ਬਿਗਾਸ (Expansion of Divine Light) and the ਰਹਿਤਨਾਮਾ known as ਰਹਿ-ਇ-ਰਾਸਤ (The Straight Path). While ਭਾਈ ਨੰਦ ਲਾਲ is best remembered as a master of Persian verse, these two works reveal him writing in Punjabi for the Sikh ਸੰਗਤ, articulating the metaphysics of ਜੋਤਿ, the centrality of ਨਾਮ, devotion to the ਗੁਰੂ, and the ethical discipline of the ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ. Students will analyze the theological content, the contrast between his Persian and Punjabi registers, his place in the ਰਹਿਤਨਾਮਾ tradition, and his lasting contribution to early Sikh literature. The course situates these texts in the historical context of the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries at ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ.
outcomes: Identify the historical and biographical context of ਭਾਈ ਨੰਦ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਯਾ and his service at the court of ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ
Distinguish the theological themes of the ਜੋਤਿ ਬਿਗਾਸ, especially the metaphysics of ਜੋਤਿ and the role of ਨਾਮ and ਸਿਮਰਨ
Analyze the ethical and ਰਹਿਤ content of the ਰਹਿ-ਇ-ਰਾਸਤ within the wider ਰਹਿਤਨਾਮਾ tradition
Compare ਭਾਈ ਨੰਦ ਲਾਲ's Punjabi register with his Persian masterpieces and assess questions of authorship and attribution

Apply scholarly source-critical methods to ਰਹਿਤਨਾਮਾ literature and the problems of redaction

courses.title: Faridkot Wala Teeka: The Royal SGGS Commentary
courses.source: Faridkot Wala Teeka (Sri Guru Granth Sahib Steek)
courses.summary: An advanced study of the monumental ਫਰੀਦਕੋਟ ਵਾਲਾ ਟੀਕਾ — the first complete, officially-sanctioned commentary on the entire ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ. Commissioned by ਰਾਜਾ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਸਿੰਘ of ਫਰੀਦਕੋਟ and completed under ਗਿਆਨੀ ਬਦਨ ਸਿੰਘ in the late nineteenth century, this nine-volume ਬ੍ਰਜ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ work shaped a generation of ਨਿਰਮਲਾ exegesis. The course traces its patronage, its team of scholars, its hermeneutical method, its ਵੇਦਾਂਤ-inflected doctrinal stance, its place within the wider history of Gurbani ਟੀਕਾ, and the controversies it provoked in the ਸਿੰਘ ਸਭਾ era. Students learn to read the Teeka critically, to weigh it against later commentaries, and to use the seven-language digital editions now hosted on the Sikh Archive.
outcomes: Reconstruct the historical circumstances of the Teeka's commissioning under ਰਾਜਾ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਸਿੰਘ and the role of the ਫਰੀਦਕੋਟ riyasat as a centre of Sikh learning
Identify the principal scholars of the project — ਗਿਆਨੀ ਬਦਨ ਸਿੰਘ, ਪੰਡਿਤ ਤਾਰਾ ਸਿੰਘ ਨਰੋਤਮ and the editorial committee — and explain their division of labour
Describe the nine-volume structure of the printed Teeka and its ਅੰਗ-by-ਅੰਗ, ਪਉੜੀ-by-ਪਉੜੀ commentary format
Analyse the Teeka's ਬ੍ਰਜ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ register and its hermeneutical procedure of ਪਦ ਅਰਥ, ਅਨ੍ਵੈ and ਭਾਵਾਰਥ

Compare the Faridkot Teeka with the ਗਰਬ ਗੰਜਨੀ ਟੀਕਾ, the ਸ਼ਬਦਾਰਥ and ਦਰਪਣ traditions
Use the seven-language digital editions on the Sikh Archive to perform comparative close reading of selected ਸ਼ਬਦ

courses.title: Guru Granth Darpan: Prof Sahib Singh's Life Work
courses.source: Sri Guru Granth Sahib Darpan by Prof Sahib Singh
courses.summary: A comprehensive intermediate study of Prof Sahib Singh (1892-1977) and his monumental ten-volume ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦਰਪਣ, the standard Punjabi word-for-word commentary (ਟੀਕਾ) on the ਆਦਿ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ. The course traces his improbable journey from a Hindu Pohuwindi family to becoming the foremost grammarian of ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ, examines the grammatical methodology that anchors the Darpan, and evaluates why his ਟੀਕਾ became the most trusted Punjabi commentary among Sikh scholars, ਟਕਸਾਲ traditions, and ordinary ਸੰਗਤ alike.
outcomes: Reconstruct the biography of Prof Sahib Singh and explain how his life as a teacher and ਪ੍ਰਿੰਸੀਪਲ shaped the Darpan

Explain the word-for-word (ਪਦ-ਅਰਥ) and paraphrase (ਅਰਥ) structure of a typical Darpan entry
Evaluate why the Darpan became the standard Punjabi ਟੀਕਾ and how it differs from earlier commentaries
Analyze how Prof Sahib Singh resolves difficult or contested ਤੁਕਾਂ of ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ using grammar rather than tradition alone
Assess the present status of the Darpan among academic scholars, ਟਕਸਾਲਾਂ, and critics

courses.title: Vaaran Bhai Gurdas: Theology and Philosophy (Vaars 16-25)
courses.summary: An advanced seminar on the theology and philosophy embedded in Vaars 16-25 of the Vaaran of ਭਾਈ ਗੁਰਦਾਸ, the corpus ਗੁਰੂ ਅਰਜਨ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ called the ਕੁੰਜੀ (key) to ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ. Articulate the Sikh doctrine of ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ as ਨਿਰਗੁਣ and ਸਰਗੁਣ as developed by ਭਾਈ ਗੁਰਦਾਸ
Explain the operation of ਹੁਕਮ as divine ordinance and ਨਾਦਰਿ as unmerited grace, distinguishing them from karmic causation

Perform independent close readings of individual ਪਉੜੀਆਂ using primary-source and scholarly tools

courses.title: Dr Daljit Singh Jawa: English Translation of SGGS

courses.title: The Santhya Tradition: Correct Reading of Gurbani

courses.summary: An intermediate study of ਸੰਥਿਆ — the living oral tradition by which correct ਉਚਾਰਣ (pronunciation), ਅਰਥ (meaning), and ਲਗਾਂ-ਮਾਤਰਾਂ (vowel-sign reading) of Gurbani are transmitted from teacher to student. Compare the ਟਕਸਾਲੀ and ਨਿਹੰਗ santhya lineages and their distinctive emphases.
Apply the basic principles of ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ ਵਿਆਕਰਣ (Gurbani grammar) to read ਲਗਾਂ-ਮਾਤਰਾਂ correctly.
Distinguish the role of the ਗ੍ਰੰਥੀ from that of the ਵਿਦਵਾਨ and the ਸੰਥਿਆ ਦਾਤਾ.
Demonstrate ਸ਼ੁੱਧ ਉਚਾਰਣ awareness, including ਬਿੰਦੀ, ਟਿੱਪੀ, ਅੱਧਕ and pause (ਵਿਸਰਾਮ).

courses.title: Reading SGGS with Multiple Commentaries: A Comparative Approach
courses.summary: An expert-level methodology seminar on reading ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ through several commentary traditions at once. Students learn to triangulate the classical Faridkot ਟੀਕਾ, Sahib Singh's modern Guru Granth Darpan, Daljit Singh Jawa's English exposition, and the oral ਸੰਤਥਿਆ of the Sant tradition. The course builds a disciplined comparative practice: how different ਟੀਕਾਕਾਰ handle grammar, ਰਹਾਉ lines, theological disputes, and the gap between scholar (ਵਿਦਵਾਨ) and ਸੰਤ. It is designed as a full-semester study in ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ exegesis and hermeneutics.
outcomes: Compare and contrast at least four distinct ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ commentary traditions and articulate the assumptions each brings to a tuk.
Apply ਲਗਾਂ-ਮਾਤ੍ਰਾ (vowel-sign) grammar from Sahib Singh's system to resolve ambiguous readings of Gurbani.
Identify the ਰਹਾਉ line as the interpretive key (central refrain) and evaluate how commentators build their reading around it.
Analyze how commentators handle theological disputes such as ਅਵਤਾਰਵਾਦ, ਮੂਰਤੀ ਪੂਜਾ, and the nature of ਮੁਕਤੀ.
Distinguish the role of the ਵਿਦਵਾਨ scholar from that of the ਸੰਤ in oral interpretation and weigh the authority of each.
Construct an independent, evidence-based comparative ਟੀਕਾ of a chosen ਸ਼ਬਦ that cites and adjudicates among sources.

courses.title: Hukamnamas: The Official Letters of the Sikh Gurus
courses.summary: A semester-length intermediate study of the ਹੁਕਮਨਾਮੇ — the official letters and edicts issued by the Sikh Gurus to their ਸੰਗਤਾਂ across India. Working from Ganda Singh's foundational compiled edition, the course examines what these roughly seventy surviving documents are, their language and diplomatics, their geographic reach, and what they reveal about early Sikh administration, the ਮਸੰਦ system, the offering economy, ਦੇਗ and weaponry, and the lived organization of the Panth from Guru Hargobind through Guru Gobind Singh and into the era of Banda Singh Bahadur and the Mata Sahibs.
outcomes: Define what a ਹੁਕਮਨਾਮਾ is and distinguish it from related genres such as the ਆਗਿਆ-ਪੱਤਰ, the ਬਚਨ, and later Khalsa edicts

Analyze the language, script, seals, and diplomatic structure of the letters across Punjabi, Braj Bhasha, and Persian registers
Map the geographic distribution of the ਸੰਗਤਾਂ addressed and explain what this reveals about the spread of Sikhi
Reconstruct features of early Sikh administration, the ਮਸੰਦ network, and the offering economy from the textual evidence
Evaluate Ganda Singh's editorial method, his compilation Hukamname, and the documents' value and limits as historical sources

courses.title: Zafarnama: Guru Gobind Singh Ji's Letter of Victory
courses.source: Zafarnama by Guru Gobind Singh Ji (Dasam Granth)
courses.summary: An advanced, semester-length study of the ਜ਼ਫ਼ਰਨਾਮਾ — the "Letter of Victory" composed in Persian verse by ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ and addressed to the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb after the battle of ਚਮਕੌਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ and the martyrdoms of the ਸਾਹਿਬਜ਼ਾਦੇ. The course examines the epistle as literature, as theology, and as political-moral indictment. Students analyze its 111 couplets in the qasida tradition, its opening hymn of praise to ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ, its scathing exposure of Aurangzeb's treachery and broken oaths sworn on the Qur'an, its doctrine of the righteous sword (ਤੇਗ਼), and the celebrated declaration that when all peaceful means fail it is lawful to take up the sword. We situate the text within the Persian literary canon (Firdausi, Sa'di), within ਸਿੱਖ history, and within the manuscript tradition of the ਦਸਮ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ, closing with its historical reception — Aurangzeb's reported remorse and the letter's afterlife as a charter of conscientious resistance.
outcomes: Reconstruct the historical events of 1704-1705 — the siege of ਅਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ, the false oaths, ਚਮਕੌਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ, and the martyrdoms — that form the immediate context of the ਜ਼ਫ਼ਰਨਾਮਾ.
Analyze the epistle's structure as a Persian qasida of 111 couplets, including its opening ਹਮਦ (praise of God) and its rhetorical movement from invocation to indictment to challenge.

Explain the central theological theme that the righteous use of the sword (ਤੇਗ਼) is lawful only when every peaceful recourse is exhausted, and connect it to the doctrine of ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ and the ਸੰਤ-ਸਿਪਾਹੀ ideal.
Interpret key couplets in their Persian original, in Gurmukhi transcription, and in English translation, evaluating competing scholarly renderings.
Assess the moral logic by which ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ claims victory in apparent defeat — the concept of ਜ਼ਫ਼ਰ (victory) as moral rather than military.
Evaluate the historical reception and authenticity debates surrounding the letter within the ਦਸਮ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ manuscript tradition.

courses.title: Sarkar Khalsa: The Sikh Empire of Maharaja Ranjit Singh
courses.summary: An advanced survey of the ਸਰਕਾਰ ਖਾਲਸਾ (the Sikh state) under ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਰਣਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ, ruling from the Lahore ਦਰਬਾਰ between 1799 and 1849. The course traces the rise of the ਮਿਸਲ confederacy into a unified kingdom, the ਖਾਲਸਾ army's French-trained modernization (the ਫੌਜ-ਏ-ਖ਼ਾਸ), territorial expansion from Lahore to Multan, Kashmir and Peshawar, and a deliberately pluralist administration that placed Muslims, Hindus, Dogras and Europeans in the highest offices. Students examine the empire's revenue and trade economy, the symbolic politics of the ਕੋਹਿਨੂਰ diamond and the ਸਰਕਾਰੀ patronage of ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ and the rebuilding of ਸ੍ਰੀ ਹਰਿਮੰਦਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ, and the structural fragilities — succession, the Dogra factions, and the British frontier — that brought the kingdom down in the two Anglo-Sikh Wars by 1849.
outcomes: Trace the transformation of the ਮਿਸਲ confederacy into a centralized monarchy under ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਰਣਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ and explain the ideology of sovereignty exercised in the name of the ਖਾਲਸਾ.
Analyze the structure, recruitment, and French/Italian-led modernization of the ਫੌਜ-ਏ-ਖ਼ਾਸ and assess how military reform underwrote territorial expansion.
Evaluate the religiously plural character of the Lahore ਦਰਬਾਰ, identifying the Muslim, Hindu, Dogra, and European officials who held senior civil and military command.
Map the empire's expansion across Multan, Kashmir, the Hazara, and Peshawar and explain the diplomatic logic of the Sutlej boundary with the British.
Describe the revenue, ਜਾਗੀਰ, and trade systems that financed the state, and interpret the symbolic economy of the ਕੋਹਿਨੂਰ and royal patronage.
Assess the causes of the empire's collapse after 1839, weighing succession crises, factional intrigue, and British strategy across the two Anglo-Sikh Wars.

courses.title: Sikh Constitutional Theory: Gurmata to Modern Governance
courses.summary: An expert-level study of how the Sikh tradition has theorised legitimate collective authority — from the Gurbani vision of ਹਲੇਮੀ ਰਾਜੁ and the institution of the ਪੰਜ ਪਿਆਰੇ, through the deliberative sovereignty of the ਸਰਬੱਤ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ and the binding ਗੁਰਮਤਾ, to the personalised statecraft of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, the bureaucratic constitutionalism of the 1920 SGPC, and the unresolved dilemmas of Sikh political representation today. The course treats Sikh constitutionalism not as a borrowed liberal framework but as an indigenous theory of authority grounded in ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ, the doctrine of ਗੁਰੂ ਪੰਥ, and ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ as final sovereign.
outcomes: Reconstruct the Gurbani basis of Sikh political theory, especially the ideal of ਹਲੇਮੀ ਰਾਜੁ and the doctrine of ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ, and explain why Sikh authority is theological before it is institutional.
Explain how the ਪੰਜ ਪਿਆਰੇ function as a constitutional check that subordinates even the Guru to the collective Khalsa body.
Analyse the deliberative procedure of the ਸਰਬੱਤ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ and the binding character of a ਗੁਰਮਤਾ as a form of consensual sovereignty.
Evaluate the constitutional structure of the Misl confederacy and the centralising model of Maharaja Ranjit Singh's Sarkar-e-Khalsa.
Assess the 1920 formation of the SGPC and the Gurdwara Act of 1925 as the first codified, electoral Sikh constitutional order.
Critically appraise contemporary debates over Sikh political representation, sovereignty, and the relationship between ਪੰਥ and state.
references: Singh, Gurharpal, and Giorgio Shani. Sikh Nationalism: From a Dominant Minority to an Ethno-Religious Diaspora. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2022.

courses.title: The Misl Period: Sikh Confederacy and Self-Governance
courses.summary: An advanced, semester-length study of the Sikh Misl period (c. 1748-1799), the era in which the Sikh Panth, emerging from the trauma of the Ghallugharas, organized itself into twelve confederate misls under the umbrella of the ਦਲ ਖਾਲਸਾ. The course examines the political genesis of the misls under ਨਵਾਬ ਕਪੂਰ ਸਿੰਘ and ਜੱਸਾ ਸਿੰਘ ਆਹਲੂਵਾਲੀਆ, the distinctive governance instruments of ਗੁਰਮਤਾ, ਰਾਖੀ, and the biannual ਸਰਬੱਤ ਖਾਲਸਾ, the economic and land-tenure systems that financed Sikh power, and the shifting diplomacy among Afghans, Marathas, and Mughals. It closes by analyzing how this decentralized commonwealth was consolidated into monarchy under ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਰਣਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ, and what the period reveals about Sikh political philosophy translated into practice.
outcomes: Explain how the trauma of the ਛੋਟਾ ਘੱਲੂਘਾਰਾ and ਵੱਡਾ ਘੱਲੂਘਾਰਾ shaped the decentralized, mobile structure of the misls
Describe the institutional architecture of the ਦਲ ਖਾਲਸਾ, including the ਸਰਬੱਤ ਖਾਲਸਾ, ਗੁਰਮਤਾ, and the role of ਨਵਾਬ ਕਪੂਰ ਸਿੰਘ and ਜੱਸਾ ਸਿੰਘ ਆਹਲੂਵਾਲੀਆ
Identify the twelve misls, their leading families, and their geographic territories
Analyze the ਰਾਖੀ system and ਪੱਟੀਦਾਰੀ land tenure as economic and political instruments
Evaluate Sikh diplomacy and warfare against ਅਹਿਮਦ ਸ਼ਾਹ ਅਬਦਾਲੀ, the Marathas, and the declining Mughal state
Assess the transition from confederate self-governance to the centralized monarchy of ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਰਣਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ
Articulate the Sikh political-theological concepts of ਹਲੇਮੀ ਰਾਜ, ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ, and ਗੁਰੂ ਪੰਥ as expressed in misl-era governance

courses.title: British Annexation and Sikh Resistance (1849–1919)
courses.summary: This advanced course traces the seventy-year arc from the fall of the ਸਰਕਾਰ-ਏ-ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ (the Sikh state of Maharaja Ranjit Singh) to the eve of the Akali agitation. It examines the two Anglo-Sikh Wars, the diplomacy of the Treaty of Lahore and the Treaty of Bhairowal, the formal annexation of ਪੰਜਾਬ in 1849, and the dispossession of Maharaja Duleep Singh. Students will study the paradox of Sikh participation in the suppression of the 1857 rebellion, the transformation of the ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ into the colonial "martial race," and the deep currents of religious and political reform that followed: the Nirankari and Namdhari (ਕੂਕਾ) movements, the ਸਿੰਘ ਸਭਾ revival with its contest between ਤੱਤ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ and ਸਨਾਤਨ ਸਿੱਖੀ, the founding of Khalsa College and the codification of a distinct Sikh identity, the transnational radicalism of the ਗ਼ਦਰ Party, and the trauma of the ਜਲ੍ਹਿਆਂਵਾਲਾ ਬਾਗ਼ massacre. The course closes at the threshold of the Gurdwara Reform Movement, the ਅਕਾਲੀ ਦਲ, and the SGPC. Drawing on Harnik Deol's sociology of religious nationalism and the major historiography of colonial Punjab, the course equips students to analyze how conquest, collaboration, reform, and resistance together forged modern Sikh political consciousness.
outcomes: Reconstruct the political and military narrative of the two Anglo-Sikh Wars and explain how the Treaties of Lahore and Bhairowal converted military defeat into administrative annexation.
Analyze the colonial restructuring of ਪੰਜਾਬ after 1849, including land settlement, the canal colonies, and the manufacture of the Sikh 'martial race' through army recruitment.
Evaluate the paradox of Sikh loyalism during the 1857 rebellion and its long-term consequences for Sikh-British relations.
Distinguish the theological and social programs of the Nirankari, Namdhari, and ਸਿੰਘ ਸਭਾ reform movements, and explain the contest between ਤੱਤ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ and ਸਨਾਤਨ ਸਿੱਖੀ over Sikh identity.
Assess the rise of revolutionary and constitutional nationalism among Sikhs, from the ਗ਼ਦਰ Party through the ਜਲ੍ਹਿਆਂਵਾਲਾ ਬਾਗ਼ massacre.
Trace the institutional consolidation of the Panth into the ਅਕਾਲੀ ਦਲ and the SGPC as the culmination of reform and resistance.
Critically apply Harnik Deol's framework of religion and nationalism to the formation of modern Sikh political identity.
