lessons.summary: The history and setting of Goindval as the location of the baoli and as Guru Amar Das Ji's center of ministry.

lessons.title: Building the Baoli: The Account in Historical Sources
lessons.summary: The traditional account of the construction of the Goindval baoli and what historical sources tell us about it.

lessons.title: The Eighty-Four Steps: Symbol and Practice
lessons.summary: The symbolism of the eighty-four steps of the Goindval baoli and their connection to Sikh theological concepts.

lessons.title: Japji Sahib at Each Step: The Prescribed Practice
lessons.summary: The specific spiritual practice associated with the Goindval baoli — reciting Japji Sahib at each of the eighty-four steps.

lessons.title: The Baoli as Alternative Pilgrimage Site
lessons.summary: How the Goindval baoli functioned as a specifically Sikh alternative to the dominant Hindu pilgrimage system.

lessons.title: Sacred Water: The Theology of Bathing at the Baoli
lessons.summary: The theological understanding of bathing at the Goindval baoli — what makes the water sacred and what the practice is understood to accomplish.

lessons.title: The Guru's Presence and Sacred Space
lessons.summary: How the Guru's presence — physical during his lifetime, spiritual thereafter — constitutes the sacred character of Sikh holy sites.

lessons.title: Comparing Goindval with Haridwar and Other Hindu Pilgrimage Sites
lessons.summary: A comparison of the Goindval baoli with major Hindu pilgrimage sites — their similarities and fundamental differences in theological framework.

lessons.title: Goindval and the Development of Sikh Sacred Geography
lessons.summary: The Goindval baoli's place in the longer development of Sikh sacred geography, from Kartarpur through Goindval to Amritsar and beyond.

lessons.title: The Baoli Today: Living Heritage
lessons.summary: The present state of the Goindval baoli, its management, and how it continues to function as a living site of Sikh pilgrimage.

courses.title: Guru Amar Das Ji's Gurbani: Themes of Equality and Liberation
courses.summary: This advanced course offers a thematic study of Guru Amar Das Ji's extensive Gurbani — over 900 compositions in the Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji — with particular focus on the themes of equality, liberation, the critique of false religion, and the vision of the ideal spiritual community. Students will engage closely with selected compositions and with scholarly commentary, developing skills of textual analysis and theological interpretation.
outcomes: Identify the scope and distribution of Guru Amar Das Ji's compositions in the Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
Analyze the major theological themes of Guru Amar Das Ji's Gurbani, particularly equality and liberation
Interpret selected compositions using traditional and critical scholarly tools
Explain Guru Amar Das Ji's critique of ritual religion and caste hierarchy in his compositions
Connect the themes of his Gurbani to his biographical context and social reform agenda
Evaluate how Guru Amar Das Ji's theological vision shapes the Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji as a whole
references: Singh, Sahib. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Darpan. 10 vols. Jalandhar: Raj Publishers, 1962–1964.
Shackle, Christopher, and Arvind-Pal Singh Mandair. Teachings of the Sikh Gurus: Selections from the Sikh Scriptures. London: Routledge, 2005.
Kohli, Surindar Singh. A Critical Study of Adi Granth. New Delhi: Punjabi Writers' Cooperative Industrial Society, 1961.
Singh, Harbans. The Heritage of the Sikhs. New Delhi: Manohar, 1994.
Macauliffe, Max Arthur. The Sikh Religion: Its Gurus, Sacred Writings and Authors. Vol. 2. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1909.
Mandair, Arvind-Pal Singh. Sikhism: A Guide for the Perplexed. London: Bloomsbury, 2013.

lessons.title: Introduction: The Scope of Guru Amar Das Ji's Gurbani
lessons.summary: An overview of Guru Amar Das Ji's Gurbani — its volume, distribution, and place in the Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.

lessons.title: The Mehla 3 Designation and Authorship
lessons.summary: Understanding the Mehla 3 designation in the SGGS and what it means for reading Guru Amar Das Ji's compositions.

lessons.title: The Theme of Inner vs. Outer Religion
lessons.summary: Guru Amar Das Ji's sustained critique of outer religious performance divorced from inner transformation.

lessons.title: Equality Before the Divine: The Radical Claim
lessons.summary: The theological claim of human equality in Guru Amar Das Ji's Gurbani and its implications for social practice.

lessons.title: The Critique of Caste in Gurbani
lessons.summary: A detailed examination of how Guru Amar Das Ji's Gurbani critiques the caste system — its claims, its practices, and its spiritual consequences.

lessons.title: Liberation and the Path Through
lessons.summary: Guru Amar Das Ji's theology of liberation — its nature, its means, and the role of the Guru's grace in achieving it.

lessons.title: The Guru's Grace: Nadar and Kirpa
lessons.summary: The theology of divine grace in Guru Amar Das Ji's compositions — its nature, operation, and relationship to human effort.

lessons.title: Sahaj: The State of Effortless Ease
lessons.summary: The concept of sahaj in Guru Amar Das Ji's Gurbani and its significance as a description of the spiritually mature state.

lessons.title: Slanderers and the Mirror of Gurbani
lessons.summary: Guru Amar Das Ji's treatment of the theme of slander (ninda) in his compositions and its spiritual significance.

lessons.title: Women's Spiritual Equality in Guru Amar Das Ji's Compositions
lessons.summary: The treatment of women and gender in Guru Amar Das Ji's Gurbani, with attention to key compositions that affirm women's spiritual equality.

lessons.title: Anand Sahib in the Context of the Wider Gurbani
lessons.summary: Reading Anand Sahib in the context of Guru Amar Das Ji's wider theological vision across his 900+ compositions.

lessons.title: Conclusion: Guru Amar Das Ji's Theological Vision
lessons.summary: A synthesis of Guru Amar Das Ji's theological vision as expressed in his Gurbani and its lasting significance.

courses.title: The Dasam Granth: History, Manuscripts, and the Scholarly Landscape
courses.summary: The Dasam Granth is a large scriptural compilation attributed to Guru Gobind Singh Ji (1666–1708), the tenth Sikh Guru, comprising approximately 1,428 pages of diverse literary and devotional compositions. This course surveys the manuscript history, the canonical debates, and the major scholarly positions that have shaped how Sikhs and academics understand this text. Students engage with the primary compositions, the historical transmission of manuscripts, and the institutional processes by which the Granth received its current form.
outcomes: Identify the major compositions contained within the Dasam Granth and their literary genres
Trace the manuscript tradition from Guru Gobind Singh's court poets through to printed editions
Evaluate key scholarly debates regarding attribution and canonicity
Analyze the historical context of the Baisakhi 1699 Khalsa formation and its relationship to the Granth's themes
Distinguish between the positions of scholars such as Dr. Kamalroop Singh, Dr. Rattan Singh Jaggi, and Bhai Vir Singh
Apply source-critical methods to primary textual evidence in Dasam Granth scholarship
references: Singh, Kamalroop, and Gurinder Singh Mann. The Granth of the Tenth King. Archimedes Press, 2015.
Jaggi, Rattan Singh. Dasam Granth Parichay. Punjabi University Patiala, 1966.
Loehlin, C. H. The Granth of Guru Gobind Singh and the Khalsa Brotherhood. Lucknow: Lucknow Publishing House, 1971.
Fenech, Louis E. The Sikh Zafar-namah of Guru Gobind Singh. Oxford University Press, 2013.
McLeod, W. H. Who Is a Sikh? The Problem of Sikh Identity. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1989.
Bhai Vir Singh, ed. Shabad Murat. Khalsa Samachar, Amritsar, 1947.
Oberoi, Harjot. The Construction of Religious Boundaries. University of Chicago Press, 1994.
Nikky-Guninder Kaur Singh. The Name of My Beloved: Verses of the Sikh Gurus. HarperCollins, 1995.

lessons.title: Introduction: What Is the Dasam Granth?
lessons.summary: An orientation to the Granth's scope, its place alongside the Guru Granth Sahib, and why it remains both spiritually central and academically contested.

lessons.title: Guru Gobind Singh: Poet, Warrior, and Theologian
lessons.summary: A biographical overview of the tenth Guru emphasizing his literary output, the Anandpur court, and the historical conditions under which the Dasam Granth compositions emerged.

lessons.title: Manuscript Tradition and Early Birs
lessons.summary: An examination of the surviving manuscripts of the Dasam Granth, their dating, provenance, and the scholarly methods used to evaluate them.

lessons.title: The Anandpur Court and Its Poets
lessons.summary: A closer look at the literary culture of Guru Gobind Singh's court, the specific poets named in historical sources, and their contributions to Dasam Granth texts.

lessons.title: Major Compositions: An Overview
lessons.summary: A structured survey of all major sections within the Dasam Granth, from Jap Sahib and Akal Ustat through Krishnavtar, Charitropakhyan, and the Zafarnama.

lessons.title: The Nitnem Banis of the Dasam Granth
lessons.summary: A focused study of the three Dasam Granth banis prescribed for daily recitation and Amrit Sanchar: Jap Sahib, Swayye (Savaiye), and Benti Chaupai.

lessons.title: Chandi Compositions and Heroic Literature
lessons.summary: An introduction to the three Chandi compositions in the Dasam Granth and their theological significance as celebrations of divine power operating through heroic agency.

lessons.title: Charitropakhyan and Scholarly Controversy
lessons.summary: An overview of the Charitropakhyan's structure, content, and the range of scholarly interpretations from condemnation to nuanced contextual readings.

lessons.title: The Zafarnama and Persian Compositions
lessons.summary: An introduction to the Zafarnama as historical document, political epistle, and spiritual testimony, drawing on the fetched source text.

lessons.title: Printed Editions and Institutional History
lessons.summary: A history of how the Dasam Granth moved from manuscript to print, the role of the Singh Sabha and SGPC, and how institutional decisions shaped the text's reception.

lessons.title: Contemporary Scholarly Debates
lessons.summary: A survey of the major scholarly positions in current Dasam Granth studies, including the work of Dr. Kamalroop Singh, and the ongoing community discussions.

lessons.title: The Dasam Granth in Sikh Practice Today
lessons.summary: A concluding survey of how the Dasam Granth functions in contemporary Sikh worship, initiation, Gurdwara practice, and personal devotion.

courses.title: Jap Sahib, Swayye, and Benti Chaupai: The Daily Khalsa Banis
courses.summary: Three compositions from the Dasam Granth stand at the heart of Khalsa daily practice: Jap Sahib, the Swayye (Savaiye), and Benti Chaupai. This course provides close textual analysis of each bani, examining their literary structure, theological content, and devotional function within the Nitnem. Students engage with the original texts and their scholarly interpretations to understand why these compositions were chosen for daily recitation and Amrit Sanchar.
outcomes: Recite and explain the theological content of Jap Sahib's 199 divine names
Analyze the Swayye's rejection of idol worship and its monotheistic argument
Interpret the petition structure and divine attributes celebrated in Benti Chaupai
Compare the literary metres and forms used across the three banis
Evaluate the role of these banis in Amrit Sanchar and daily Khalsa discipline
Distinguish the theological vocabulary of the Dasam Granth from that of the Guru Granth Sahib
references: Singh, Kamalroop, and Gurinder Singh Mann. The Granth of the Tenth King. Archimedes Press, 2015.
Jaggi, Rattan Singh. Dasam Granth Parichay. Punjabi University Patiala, 1966.
Loehlin, C. H. The Granth of Guru Gobind Singh and the Khalsa Brotherhood. Lucknow: Lucknow Publishing House, 1971.
Sahib Singh, Prof. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Darpan. Vol. 1. Raj Publishers, Jalandhar, 1972.
Fenech, Louis E., and W. H. McLeod, eds. Historical Dictionary of Sikhism. 3rd ed. Rowman and Littlefield, 2014.
Nikky-Guninder Kaur Singh. The Name of My Beloved: Verses of the Sikh Gurus. HarperCollins, 1995.

lessons.title: The Three Banis in Context
lessons.summary: An orientation to Jap Sahib, Swayye, and Benti Chaupai within the Nitnem and Amrit Sanchar, establishing why their study is foundational for understanding Khalsa spirituality.

lessons.title: Jap Sahib: Literary Form and Structure
lessons.summary: An analysis of the metre, language, and structural organization of Jap Sahib, placing it within the Sanskrit stotra tradition while noting its distinctively Sikh theological content.

lessons.title: Jap Sahib: The Divine Names — God Beyond All Definition
lessons.summary: A close reading of selected divine names in Jap Sahib, exploring their Sanskrit etymologies, theological meanings, and devotional significance.

lessons.title: Jap Sahib: Nirguna and Nirankar Theology
lessons.summary: A theological analysis of Jap Sahib's central claims about divine nature, with attention to the concepts of nirguna, nirankar, and akal purakh.

lessons.title: The Swayye: Structure and Setting
lessons.summary: An introduction to the Swayye as a literary form and an examination of the ten Nitnem verses within their larger context in Akal Ustat.

lessons.title: The Swayye: Rejecting False Paths
lessons.summary: A close reading of the Swayye's central theological argument: the categorical rejection of all idol worship, sectarian rituals, and ascetic practices in favor of direct devotion to the one God.

lessons.title: The Swayye: The Sword as Divine Symbol
lessons.summary: A deeper exploration of the sword symbolism in the Swayye and the Dasam Granth, connecting the literary image to Khalsa theology and practice.

lessons.title: Benti Chaupai: Introduction and Metre
lessons.summary: An introduction to the Benti Chaupai's place within the Dasam Granth's Charitropakhyan section, its metre, and the textual questions surrounding its precise boundaries.

lessons.title: Benti Chaupai: The Theology of Kal
lessons.summary: An examination of the Benti Chaupai's distinctive theological concept of Kal — Time as divine creative principle — and its relationship to the bani's theology of divine sovereignty.

lessons.title: Benti Chaupai: Divine Protection and Human Petition
lessons.summary: A close reading of the Benti Chaupai's petition passages, exploring the relationship between human vulnerability and divine protection that structures the bani's devotional logic.

lessons.title: Comparing the Three Banis: Themes and Theology
lessons.summary: A synthetic comparative analysis of the theological themes shared across Jap Sahib, Swayye, and Benti Chaupai, identifying the coherent theological vision they collectively express.

lessons.title: The Banis in Living Practice: Nitnem and Amrit Sanchar
lessons.summary: A concluding examination of how these three banis function in contemporary Sikh life, from daily Nitnem to the transformative ritual of Amrit Sanchar.

courses.title: Chandi Di Var and Chandi Charitar: Heroic Poetry and the Divine Feminine
courses.summary: The Dasam Granth contains three major compositions celebrating the divine feminine warrior-power: Chandi Di Var, Chandi Charitar I, and Chandi Charitar II. This course examines these compositions as theological reinterpretations of classical Hindu narrative, analyzing how Guru Gobind Singh transforms the Devi Mahatmya tradition into a vehicle for Sikh monotheism and the spiritual rationale for Khalsa heroism. Students engage with the fetched source texts and scholarly analysis to understand the theology of divine power operating through heroic agency.
outcomes: Explain the theological difference between the Guru's use of Chandi imagery and Hindu goddess worship
Analyze the Devi Mahatmya narrative as transformed in the Chandi compositions
Trace the Var metre and its significance in the Punjabi literary tradition
Evaluate the mangalacharan invocations as theological framing devices
Interpret the concept of Bhagauti as the divine power underlying heroic action
Connect the Chandi compositions to the spiritual rationale for Khalsa martial identity
references: Singh, Kamalroop, and Gurinder Singh Mann. The Granth of the Tenth King. Archimedes Press, 2015.
Fenech, Louis E. The Sikh Zafar-namah of Guru Gobind Singh. Oxford University Press, 2013.
Jaggi, Rattan Singh. Dasam Granth Parichay. Punjabi University Patiala, 1966.
Coburn, Thomas B. Devi Mahatmya: The Crystallization of the Goddess Tradition. Motilal Banarsidass, 1984.
Nikky-Guninder Kaur Singh. The Feminine Principle in the Sikh Vision of the Transcendent. Cambridge University Press, 1993.
Loehlin, C. H. The Granth of Guru Gobind Singh and the Khalsa Brotherhood. Lucknow: Lucknow Publishing House, 1971.
Mandair, Arvind-Pal Singh. Religion and the Specter of the West. Columbia University Press, 2009.

lessons.title: The Chandi Tradition in the Dasam Granth
lessons.summary: An orientation to the three Chandi compositions, their sources in Sanskrit tradition, and their distinctive theological reframing in the Guru's work.

lessons.title: The Devi Mahatmya: Sanskrit Source and Its Theology
lessons.summary: An overview of the Devi Mahatmya as literary and theological text, establishing the source that Guru Gobind Singh transformed in his Chandi compositions.

lessons.title: Chandi Di Var: The Punjabi Var Tradition
lessons.summary: An analysis of the Var metre and genre, its place in Punjabi literary tradition, and how Guru Gobind Singh deploys it in Chandi Di Var.

lessons.title: The Mangalacharan: Theological Framing of Chandi Di Var
lessons.summary: A close reading of the opening invocation of Chandi Di Var, showing how the Guru's theological framing transforms the entire narrative that follows.

lessons.title: The Cosmogony of the Khanda
lessons.summary: Analysis of the Chandi Di Var's opening cosmogonic verse, in which the divine sword (Khanda) is identified as the first principle of creation.

lessons.title: The Battle Narrative: Demons, Gods, and Divine Power
lessons.summary: A survey of the battle narratives in Chandi Di Var, examining how the Guru deploys them to communicate the theology of divine power overcoming demonic forces.

lessons.title: Chandi Charitar I and II: Braj Bhasha Retellings
lessons.summary: A comparative analysis of the two Braj Bhasha Chandi Charitar compositions, their literary relationship to Chandi Di Var, and their distinctive theological emphases.

lessons.title: Bhagauti: The Theology of Divine-Heroic Power
lessons.summary: A theological analysis of the concept of Bhagauti as used in the Chandi compositions and in the Ardas, tracing its complex meaning across Sikh tradition.

lessons.title: The Goddess as Instrument, Not Sovereign
lessons.summary: A focused theological analysis of how Guru Gobind Singh systematically repositions the goddess within Sikh monotheism, making her an instrument of divine will rather than an independent sovereign.

lessons.title: Heroic Aesthetics and Khalsa Identity
lessons.summary: An examination of the heroic aesthetic (vir ras) in the Chandi compositions and its role in forming Khalsa martial consciousness.

lessons.title: Modern Interpretive Debates
lessons.summary: A survey of the major modern debates about the Chandi compositions, from reformist critiques to feminist readings and contemporary community discussions.

lessons.title: The Chandi Compositions in Contemporary Sikh Practice
lessons.summary: A concluding survey of how the Chandi compositions function in living Sikh practice today, from devotional recitation to theological education.

courses.title: Charitropakhyan: Narratives, Ethics, Gender, and Scholarly Debate
courses.summary: The Charitropakhyan is the most debated section of the Dasam Granth: a collection of 405 narrative tales addressing themes of ethics, statecraft, gender, deception, and moral discernment. This course examines the Charitropakhyan's literary tradition, its relationship to classical South Asian narrative, the range of scholarly positions on its attribution and theological significance, and the ongoing community debates about its canonical status.
outcomes: Identify the literary traditions — Sanskrit Panchatantra, Kathasaritsagara, Persian narrative — that the Charitropakhyan draws upon
Analyze the framing narrative and its pedagogical function within the text
Evaluate scholarly arguments for and against attribution to Guru Gobind Singh
Interpret the ethical and theological themes that run through the tale collection
Assess the gender and power dimensions present in the narrative material
Situate the Charitropakhyan within the broader debate about Dasam Granth canonicity
references: Singh, Kamalroop, and Gurinder Singh Mann. The Granth of the Tenth King. Archimedes Press, 2015.
Jaggi, Rattan Singh. Dasam Granth Parichay. Punjabi University Patiala, 1966.
McLeod, W. H. Who Is a Sikh? The Problem of Sikh Identity. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1989.
Olivelle, Patrick, trans. Pancatantra: The Book of India's Folk Wisdom. Oxford University Press, 1997.
Loehlin, C. H. The Granth of Guru Gobind Singh and the Khalsa Brotherhood. Lucknow: Lucknow Publishing House, 1971.
Nikky-Guninder Kaur Singh. The Feminine Principle in the Sikh Vision of the Transcendent. Cambridge University Press, 1993.
Penzer, N. M., ed. The Ocean of Story (Somadeva's Kathasaritsagara). 10 vols. Chas. J. Sawyer, 1924.
Oberoi, Harjot. The Construction of Religious Boundaries. University of Chicago Press, 1994.

lessons.title: Introduction to the Charitropakhyan
lessons.summary: An orientation to the Charitropakhyan's scope, structure, and the reasons it has become the most debated section of the Dasam Granth.

lessons.title: Classical South Asian Narrative Traditions
lessons.summary: An overview of the Sanskrit and Persian narrative traditions that provided the source material for the Charitropakhyan.

lessons.title: The Framing Narrative: King, Prince, and Minister
lessons.summary: A close analysis of the Charitropakhyan's framing narrative, in which a minister instructs a king's son through stories, establishing the text's pedagogical context.

lessons.title: The Tales: Categories and Themes
lessons.summary: A survey of the Charitropakhyan's 405 tales by category, examining the range of themes and the moral and philosophical issues each category raises.

lessons.title: Ethics of Discernment: Vivek as Central Virtue
lessons.summary: A theological and philosophical analysis of vivek (discernment) as the central virtue the Charitropakhyan aims to cultivate.

lessons.title: Gender, Power, and the Female Characters
lessons.summary: A focused examination of how female characters are depicted in the Charitropakhyan and the range of scholarly interpretations of these depictions.

lessons.title: The Hikaiyatan: Persian Tales in the Charitropakhyan
lessons.summary: An examination of the Persian Hikayatan section, its literary character, and its relationship to the broader Charitropakhyan framework.

lessons.title: Attribution Debates: Scholarly Positions
lessons.summary: A systematic survey of the major scholarly positions on Charitropakhyan attribution, from full acceptance to partial rejection to agnosticism.

lessons.title: Manuscript Evidence and Textual History
lessons.summary: An examination of the manuscript evidence bearing on the Charitropakhyan's textual history and its consistency across the manuscript tradition.

lessons.title: The Charitropakhyan and Sikh Theological Principles
lessons.summary: An analysis of whether and how the Charitropakhyan's content can be reconciled with core Sikh theological and ethical principles.

lessons.title: Community Debates and Institutional Responses
lessons.summary: A survey of ongoing community debates about the Charitropakhyan, the positions of major Sikh institutions, and the practical implications for Sikh education.

lessons.title: Reading the Charitropakhyan Today
lessons.summary: A concluding reflection on how the Charitropakhyan might be read and taught today, drawing on the course's scholarly and theological analysis.

courses.title: The Zafarnama: Guru Gobind Singh's Letter of Victory
courses.summary: The Zafarnama — the Letter of Victory — is Guru Gobind Singh's Persian epistle to Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, composed in the aftermath of the battles of Chamkaur and Muktsar and the martyrdom of all four of the Guru's sons. This course examines the Zafarnama as historical document, political epistle, theological statement, and literary masterwork, drawing on the fetched source text. Students analyze how a militarily defeated man claims moral and spiritual victory through the power of divine truth and poetic argument.
outcomes: Reconstruct the historical events that led to the Zafarnama's composition
Analyze the Zafarnama's literary form as a Persian nishaan (royal epistle)
Identify the theological arguments Guru Gobind Singh makes about divine justice and sovereignty
Evaluate the Zafarnama's just-war doctrine and its implications for Khalsa ethics
Interpret the political strategy of the letter within its historical context
Connect the Zafarnama's themes to the broader theology of the Dasam Granth
references: Fenech, Louis E. The Sikh Zafar-namah of Guru Gobind Singh. Oxford University Press, 2013.
Singh, Kamalroop, and Gurinder Singh Mann. The Granth of the Tenth King. Archimedes Press, 2015.
Macauliffe, M. A. The Sikh Religion: Its Gurus, Sacred Writings, and Authors. Vol. 5. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1909.
Loehlin, C. H. The Granth of Guru Gobind Singh and the Khalsa Brotherhood. Lucknow: Lucknow Publishing House, 1971.
Richards, J. F. The Mughal Empire. Cambridge University Press, 1993.
Grewal, J. S. The Sikhs of the Punjab. Cambridge University Press, 1990.
Gandhi, Surjit Singh. History of the Sikh Gurus. Gur Das Kapur and Sons, 1978.

lessons.title: The Zafarnama: A Letter of Victory
lessons.summary: An orientation to the Zafarnama, its historical occasion, and why it stands as one of the most remarkable epistolary documents of early modern South Asia.

lessons.title: Historical Context: The Siege of Anandpur and Its Aftermath
lessons.summary: A reconstruction of the historical events leading to the Zafarnama: the siege of Anandpur Sahib, the broken oath, and the evacuation of December 1704.

lessons.title: The Battles of Chamkaur and Muktsar
lessons.summary: An account of the two battles referenced in the Zafarnama: Chamkaur, where the Guru's elder sons fell, and Muktsar, after which the Guru composed the letter.

lessons.title: The Literary Form: Persian Nishaan
lessons.summary: An analysis of the Zafarnama as an example of the Persian nishaan (royal epistle) genre, examining how the Guru deploys and transforms this literary form.

lessons.title: The Opening Theology: God as Supreme Sovereign
lessons.summary: A close reading of the Zafarnama's opening theological passages, in which the Guru establishes divine sovereignty as the framework for all that follows.

lessons.title: The Charge of Treachery: Breaking the Oath
lessons.summary: An analysis of the Zafarnama's central accusation — the broken Quranic oath — and the Guru's argument about truth, covenant, and moral accountability.

lessons.title: The Doctrine of Righteous War
lessons.summary: An analysis of the Zafarnama's articulation of the conditions under which armed resistance becomes not only permissible but obligatory.

lessons.title: Addressing Aurangzeb: Strategy and Theology
lessons.summary: An analysis of the Zafarnama's sophisticated rhetorical strategy toward Aurangzeb, combining theological argument with political pragmatism.

lessons.title: Divine Justice and Human Accountability
lessons.summary: A theological analysis of the Zafarnama's vision of divine justice, exploring how the Guru holds both divine sovereignty and human accountability in creative tension.

lessons.title: The Forty Liberated Ones: Muktsar and the Letter
lessons.summary: An examination of the episode of the Forty Liberated Ones (Chali Mukte) at Muktsar and its relationship to the Zafarnama's composition.

lessons.title: The Zafarnama's Aftermath: Aurangzeb and Beyond
lessons.summary: A survey of the Zafarnama's historical aftermath: Aurangzeb's death, the Guru's meeting with Bahadur Shah, and the letter's influence on subsequent Sikh history.

lessons.title: The Zafarnama in Sikh Memory and Practice
lessons.summary: A concluding examination of how the Zafarnama functions in contemporary Sikh consciousness, education, and the tradition of speaking truth to power.

courses.title: The Theology and Philosophy of the Dasam Granth
courses.summary: This advanced course synthesizes the theological and philosophical themes running across the Dasam Granth as a whole: the nature of God, the theology of creation, the role of divine power in history, the ethics of heroic action, and the eschatological vision of divine justice. Students engage with the Dasam Granth's distinctive theological vocabulary in dialogue with the Guru Granth Sahib, classical South Asian philosophy, and contemporary Sikh theological scholarship.
outcomes: Analyze the Dasam Granth's doctrine of God as Akal Purakh, Nirgun-Sargun, and the Sword of creation
Compare the Dasam Granth's theological vocabulary with that of the Guru Granth Sahib
Evaluate the Dasam Granth's theology of divine power operating through heroic human agency
Interpret the Granth's ethical framework as an integration of devotional and practical-wisdom traditions
Assess scholarly arguments about the theological coherence or diversity of the Dasam Granth
Synthesize the theological insights of the Dasam Granth for contemporary Sikh practice and thought
references: Singh, Kamalroop, and Gurinder Singh Mann. The Granth of the Tenth King. Archimedes Press, 2015.
Fenech, Louis E. The Sikh Zafar-namah of Guru Gobind Singh. Oxford University Press, 2013.
Mandair, Arvind-Pal Singh. Religion and the Specter of the West. Columbia University Press, 2009.
Nikky-Guninder Kaur Singh. The Name of My Beloved: Verses of the Sikh Gurus. HarperCollins, 1995.
Jaggi, Rattan Singh. Dasam Granth Parichay. Punjabi University Patiala, 1966.
Loehlin, C. H. The Granth of Guru Gobind Singh and the Khalsa Brotherhood. Lucknow: Lucknow Publishing House, 1971.
Oberoi, Harjot. The Construction of Religious Boundaries. University of Chicago Press, 1994.
McLeod, W. H. Sikhism. Penguin Books, 1997.

lessons.title: Overview: The Theology of the Dasam Granth
lessons.summary: A synthetic introduction to the Dasam Granth's theology, identifying its central claims and how they relate to the broader Sikh theological tradition.

lessons.title: God as Akal Purakh: The Timeless Sovereign
lessons.summary: An analysis of the Dasam Granth's primary divine name — Akal Purakh, the Timeless Being — and the theological claims it carries.

lessons.title: Nirguna-Saguna: The Formless and the Formed
lessons.summary: An analysis of the Dasam Granth's navigation of the classical Indian philosophical tension between nirguna (without qualities) and saguna (with qualities) conceptions of God.

lessons.title: The Sword as Cosmic Principle
lessons.summary: A synthetic theological analysis of the sword-as-cosmic-principle across the Dasam Granth, connecting the Khanda cosmogony to Khalsa identity and ethics.

lessons.title: Creation Theology in the Dasam Granth
lessons.summary: An examination of the Dasam Granth's accounts of divine creation, focusing on the Bachitar Natak's spiritual autobiography and the cosmogonic verses of the heroic compositions.

lessons.title: Divine Power and Human Agency
lessons.summary: A theological analysis of how the Dasam Granth understands the relationship between divine power and human heroic agency.

lessons.title: The Theology of Avatars: Instruments, Not Incarnations
lessons.summary: An analysis of the Dasam Granth's distinctive treatment of the avatar concept, reinterpreting classical Hindu incarnations as divine instruments rather than true incarnations.

lessons.title: Heroic Ethics: The Theology of Righteous Action
lessons.summary: A systematic analysis of the Dasam Granth's ethics of heroic action, integrating its theological, devotional, and practical-wisdom dimensions.

lessons.title: The Dasam Granth and Maya
lessons.summary: An analysis of the Dasam Granth's treatment of maya (illusion, worldly attachment) and how it relates to the text's celebration of heroic worldly engagement.

lessons.title: Liberation (Mukti) in the Dasam Granth
lessons.summary: An examination of the Dasam Granth's concept of liberation (mukti), its relationship to Khalsa identity, and its connections to the broader Sikh understanding of spiritual liberation.

lessons.title: Comparing Dasam Granth and Guru Granth Sahib Theologies
lessons.summary: A comparative analysis of the theological themes, vocabulary, and emphases of the two Granths, identifying both continuities and distinctive contributions.

lessons.title: The Dasam Granth's Legacy for Contemporary Sikh Thought
lessons.summary: A concluding synthesis of the Dasam Granth's theological legacy, addressing its significance for contemporary Sikh practice, identity, and engagement with modern challenges.

courses.title: Guru Gobind Singh Ji: Early Life, Patna Sahib, and the Crucible Years at Anandpur
courses.summary: This course examines the early life of Guru Gobind Singh Ji from his birth in Patna in 1666 CE through his formative years in the Shivalik hills at Anandpur Sahib. Drawing on Kuir Singh's Gurbilas Patshahi 10 and other primary sources, students trace the Guru's childhood, education, assumption of Guruship after his father's martyrdom, and the socio-political environment that shaped his mission. The course grounds each episode in documented historical evidence while noting where scholarly debate persists.
outcomes: Identify the primary historical sources for Guru Gobind Singh Ji's early life and evaluate their relative reliability
Describe the geographical and political context of Patna Sahib and Anandpur during the late seventeenth century
Analyze the significance of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's martyrdom for the young Gobind Rai's sense of mission
Explain the Guru's educational curriculum, linguistic range, and early literary activity at Anandpur
Distinguish between well-documented events and episodes that rely on later oral tradition
Assess how Kuir Singh's Gurbilas Patshahi 10 fills gaps left by earlier sources such as Bachittar Natak and Sri Gur Sobha

lessons.title: Introduction to Sources and the Problem of Early Biography
lessons.summary: An overview of the primary textual sources for Guru Gobind Singh Ji's life, their authors, dates of composition, and scholarly assessment of their reliability.

lessons.title: Patna Sahib: Birth, City, and Sacred Geography
lessons.summary: The historical and sacred significance of Patna, Bihar as the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, and the establishment of Takht Sri Patna Sahib.

lessons.title: Childhood at Patna: Episodes and Their Historicity
lessons.summary: An examination of the traditional childhood narratives set in Patna, assessing them against the standards of critical historical method while appreciating their devotional function.

lessons.title: The Journey to Punjab: From Patna to Makhowal
lessons.summary: The account of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji bringing the young Gobind Rai from Patna to the Punjab hills, and the establishment of the Anandpur region.

lessons.title: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's Martyrdom and Its Impact
lessons.summary: The historical circumstances of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's execution in Delhi in 1675 CE and the transformative effect on the young Gobind Rai.

lessons.title: Assumption of Guruship: Gobind Rai as the Tenth Guru
lessons.summary: The ceremony of succession, the young Guru's early actions, and the theological significance of his position as the tenth in the line of Nanak.

lessons.title: Anandpur: Geography, Fortifications, and Society
lessons.summary: The physical setting of Anandpur Sahib, its fortifications, and the social composition of the Guru's court and community in the Shivalik hills.

lessons.title: Education, Languages, and Early Literary Formation
lessons.summary: Guru Gobind Singh Ji's multilingual education, his early poetic output, and the court of scholars and poets he assembled at Anandpur.

lessons.title: The Hill Rajas and the Political Landscape of the Shivaliks
lessons.summary: The complex network of hill kingdoms surrounding Anandpur, their relations with the Mughal court and with Guru Gobind Singh Ji, and the dynamics that led to military conflict.

lessons.title: Early Military Encounters: Bhangani and Nadaun
lessons.summary: The battles of Bhangani (1688) and Nadaun (1691) as documented in the Bachittar Natak, the Gurbilas, and Senapati's Sri Gur Sobha.

lessons.title: Building the Khalsa: Conceptual Foundations at Anandpur
lessons.summary: The theological and social ideas that converged at Anandpur in the years before 1699, culminating in the conceptual ground for the creation of the Khalsa.

lessons.title: The Crucible Years: Synthesis and Historical Significance
lessons.summary: A concluding synthesis of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's early life, assessing its historical significance and its place within the broader arc of Sikh history.

courses.title: Guru Gobind Singh Ji as Poet: Jaap Sahib, Swayye, Akal Ustat, and the Zafarnama
courses.summary: This course offers close literary analysis of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's major poetic works: the Jaap Sahib, Tav Prasad Swayye, Akal Ustat, and the Persian Zafarnama. Students examine the Guru's multilingual poetic genius, his use of classical Indian and Persian literary forms, and the theological and political ideas encoded in each composition. The course draws on the scholarly edition of the Dasam Granth and comparative literary analysis to reveal the breadth and depth of the Guru's literary legacy.
outcomes: Analyze the structure, meter, and theological content of the Jaap Sahib's 103 names of the Divine
Explain the spiritual and rhetorical function of the Tav Prasad Swayye as a critique of empty ritual
Describe the literary and theological scope of the Akal Ustat and its vision of divine transcendence
Examine the Zafarnama as a bilingual literary and political document addressed to Aurangzeb
Identify the classical Indian (Braj Bhasha, Sanskrit) and Persian literary traditions Guru Gobind Singh Ji engaged and transformed
Evaluate the significance of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's poetic corpus within both Sikh theology and the broader history of South Asian literature
references: Guru Gobind Singh. Sri Dasam Granth Sahib. 2 vols. Patiala: Punjabi University, 1973.

lessons.title: Guru Gobind Singh Ji as Literary Figure: An Overview
lessons.summary: Introduction to Guru Gobind Singh Ji's place within the history of South Asian literature and the scope of his surviving poetic corpus.

lessons.title: The Dasam Granth: Composition, Compilation, and Scholarly Debate
lessons.summary: The textual history of the Dasam Granth, its compilation after Guru Gobind Singh Ji's time, and the ongoing scholarly discussion of its contents.

lessons.title: Jaap Sahib: Structure, Meter, and the 103 Names of God
lessons.summary: A close analysis of the Jaap Sahib's formal structure, its use of classical meters, and the linguistic range of its 103 divine names.

lessons.title: Jaap Sahib: Theological Analysis and Interfaith Vision
lessons.summary: The theological vision of the Jaap Sahib analyzed in depth, with attention to its treatment of divine transcendence, the beyondness of God, and the implications for Sikh interfaith theology.

lessons.title: Tav Prasad Swayye: Text and Translation
lessons.summary: A close reading of the six Tav Prasad Swayye with attention to their literary form, imagery, and the specific ritual practices they critique.

lessons.title: Tav Prasad Swayye: Critique of Ritual and the Primacy of Love
lessons.summary: The theological argument of the Tav Prasad Swayye analyzed in depth, with attention to the concept of Bhakti (devotion) and the relationship between form and spirit in Sikh theology.

lessons.title: Akal Ustat: Praise of the Timeless One
lessons.summary: An introduction to the Akal Ustat, its place within the Dasam Granth, and the major theological themes of its opening sections.

lessons.title: Akal Ustat: The Vision of Divine Transcendence
lessons.summary: Deep analysis of the Akal Ustat's theological vision, including its treatment of divine immanence and transcendence, and its place within the broader tradition of Sikh theology.

lessons.title: The Zafarnama: Historical Context and Genre
lessons.summary: The historical circumstances in which the Zafarnama was written, its Persian literary genre, and the political context of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's address to Aurangzeb.

lessons.title: The Zafarnama: Literary Analysis and Theological Claims
lessons.summary: A close literary reading of the Zafarnama's major arguments, its Persian rhetoric, and the theological claims the Guru makes to Aurangzeb.

lessons.title: Benti Chaupai and the Devotional Compositions
lessons.summary: Analysis of the Benti Chaupai and other devotional compositions, their place in the Nitnem, and their role in Khalsa spiritual practice.

lessons.title: The Literary Legacy: Synthesis and Ongoing Significance
lessons.summary: A concluding synthesis of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's literary legacy, its ongoing significance for Sikh practice, and its place in South Asian literary history.

courses.title: The Battles, the Sahibzade, and the Siege of Anandpur Sahib
courses.summary: This course examines the military history of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's campaigns from the founding of the Khalsa in 1699 through the siege and evacuation of Anandpur Sahib in 1705. Central to the course is the martyrdom of the four Sahibzade (sons of the Guru) and the theological and historical significance of these sacrifices within Khalsa identity. Drawing on Kuir Singh's Gurbilas Patshahi 10, Giani Gian Singh's Twarikh Guru Khalsa, and the Bachittar Natak, students reconstruct the military, political, and spiritual dimensions of this defining period.
outcomes: Reconstruct the sequence of military engagements around Anandpur Sahib from 1699 to 1705 using primary sources
Analyze the political and military dynamics that led to the siege and evacuation of Anandpur
Examine the martyrdom of the four Sahibzade and its place within the theology of Khalsa sacrifice
Describe the Battle of Chamkaur and its significance for Khalsa identity and memory
Evaluate the sources' reliability for the events of 1704–1705, distinguishing documented events from later elaboration
Explain why the sacrifices of the Sahibzade and Mata Gujri Ji are central to Sikh understanding of faith under persecution

lessons.title: The Founding of the Khalsa: Vaisakhi 1699
lessons.summary: The creation of the Khalsa on Vaisakhi 1699, the ceremony of the Sees Bhet, the Panj Pyare, and the institutional transformation it represented.

lessons.title: The Rehat Maryada: Code of the Khalsa
lessons.summary: The code of conduct (Rehat) given to the Khalsa at its founding, including the Panj Kakar, and its significance for Khalsa identity.

lessons.title: Political Context: Anandpur Under Pressure, 1699–1704
lessons.summary: The escalating political and military pressure on Anandpur Sahib following the founding of the Khalsa, including Mughal and hill-raja mobilization.

lessons.title: The First Phase of the Sieges of Anandpur
lessons.summary: The earlier military engagements around Anandpur before the final great siege, and the Guru's defensive strategy.

lessons.title: The Second Siege: The Promise and Its Betrayal
lessons.summary: The great siege of Anandpur Sahib in 1704–1705, the negotiations for safe passage, and the violation of the sworn promise.

lessons.title: The Evacuation of Anandpur and the Sirsa Crossing
lessons.summary: The detailed sequence of the evacuation from Anandpur, the chaos of the night crossing of the Sirsa river, and the separation of the Guru's family.

lessons.title: The Battle of Chamkaur: The Garhi and the Elder Sahibzade
lessons.summary: The Battle of Chamkaur, where Sahibzade Ajit Singh and Jujhar Singh were martyred fighting alongside the Guru against vastly superior forces.

lessons.title: Sahibzade Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh at Sirhind
lessons.summary: The capture, imprisonment, and execution of the two younger Sahibzade at Sirhind, and the courage they displayed before Nawab Wazir Khan.

lessons.title: Mata Gujri Ji and the Younger Sahibzade: Martyrdom and Memory
lessons.summary: The theological and memorial significance of the younger Sahibzade's martyrdom and its place within Sikh collective memory and identity.

lessons.title: After Chamkaur: Machhiwara, Dina, and the Zafarnama
lessons.summary: Guru Gobind Singh Ji's journey through Machhiwara, his stay at Dina, and the composition of the Zafarnama addressed to Aurangzeb.

lessons.title: The Battle of Muktsar and the Chali Mukte
lessons.summary: The Battle of Muktsar in 1705 CE, the redemption of the Chali Mukte (Forty Liberated Ones), and the theological significance of forgiveness and courage.

lessons.title: The Sahibzade in Khalsa Memory and Theology
lessons.summary: A concluding examination of how the martyrdom of the four Sahibzade has shaped Khalsa identity, theology, and collective memory across generations.

courses.title: The Dasam Granth and Guru Gobind Singh Ji's Literary and Intellectual Legacy
courses.summary: This course provides a comprehensive theological and literary study of the Dasam Granth, examining the major compositions attributed to Guru Gobind Singh Ji and the scholarly debates surrounding their authorship, purpose, and canonical status. Students engage with the Dasam Granth as both a theological document and a literary masterwork, examining how it deploys Indic and Persianate literary traditions in the service of a distinctive Khalsa theology. The course draws on the scholarly edition of the Dasam Granth and critical Sikh studies scholarship.
outcomes: Describe the textual history and manuscript traditions of the Dasam Granth
Analyze the theological content and literary form of the major Dasam Granth compositions
Evaluate scholarly debates about authorship and attribution within the Dasam Granth
Explain the Dasam Granth's relationship to Indic and Persianate literary traditions
Assess the role of the Dasam Granth in Sikh liturgy, the Khalsa initiation, and daily practice
Distinguish between the canonical liturgical core of the Dasam Granth and its larger encyclopedic contents

lessons.title: What Is the Dasam Granth? An Introduction
lessons.summary: An introductory overview of the Dasam Granth, its contents, physical description, and place within Sikh religious life.

lessons.title: Manuscript Traditions and the Process of Compilation
lessons.summary: The textual history of the Dasam Granth, its manuscript evidence, the role of Bhai Mani Singh, and what this history tells us about the anthology's development.

lessons.title: The Bachittar Natak: Autobiography and Divine Mission
lessons.summary: Analysis of the Bachittar Natak as autobiography, divine mission narrative, and the primary source for the Guru's understanding of his own role.

lessons.title: Chandi di Var and the Warrior Goddess Tradition
lessons.summary: The Chandi di Var as a literary and theological composition, its relationship to the Sanskrit Devi Mahatmya tradition, and its central role in Sikh liturgy.

lessons.title: Akal Ustat: The Theology of Divine Transcendence
lessons.summary: Deep analysis of the Akal Ustat's place within the Dasam Granth and its theological contribution to Sikh understanding of God.

lessons.title: Jaap Sahib: Liturgical and Theological Analysis
lessons.summary: A theological analysis of the Jaap Sahib's place within the Dasam Granth, its liturgical function, and the significance of its multilingual approach to divine naming.

lessons.title: The Swayye: Six Verses on Love and Ritual
lessons.summary: Analysis of the Tav Prasad Swayye within the Dasam Granth context, their literary form, and their enduring liturgical and theological significance.

lessons.title: The Krishnaavtar: Epic Narrative and Khalsa Ethics
lessons.summary: The Krishnaavtar as the longest composition in the Dasam Granth, its relationship to the Bhagavata Purana, and its theological and ethical significance for the Khalsa.

lessons.title: The Charitropakhyan: Controversy and Context
lessons.summary: The most contested portion of the Dasam Granth examined in scholarly context, with attention to its literary genre and the reasons for contemporary debate.

lessons.title: The Zafarnama: Politics, Ethics, and Persian Mastery
lessons.summary: The Zafarnama in the context of the Dasam Granth, analyzed as a political-theological document and a masterwork of Persian epistolary literature.

lessons.title: The Dasam Granth in Khalsa Practice: Amrit, Ardas, and Nitnem
lessons.summary: The specific Dasam Granth compositions incorporated into Khalsa initiation, communal prayer, and daily devotional practice.

lessons.title: Scholarly Debates and the Future of Dasam Granth Studies
lessons.summary: An assessment of current scholarly debates about the Dasam Granth, methodological approaches to its study, and directions for future scholarship.

courses.title: Nanded, the Final Hukam, and the Eternal Guruship of the Granth and Panth
courses.summary: This course examines the final years of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's life at Nanded in the Deccan, his encounter with Banda Singh Bahadur, the stabbing incident and its aftermath, and the momentous final Hukam (divine command) that conferred eternal Guruship on the Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji and the Khalsa Panth. The course explores the theological significance of this transition and its enduring consequences for Sikh identity, ecclesiology, and daily practice.
outcomes: Describe the historical circumstances of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's journey to the Deccan and arrival at Nanded
Analyze the significance of the encounter between the Guru and Banda Singh Bahadur (Madho Das)
Explain the stabbing incident, the Guru's response, and the theological interpretation of his final period
Articulate the theological content and institutional consequences of the final Hukam conferring Guruship on the Granth and Panth
Evaluate the primary sources for Nanded events and their relative reliability
Assess the theological meaning of the Shabad Guru concept and its implications for Sikh practice

lessons.title: The Journey South: From Talwandi Sabo to the Deccan
lessons.summary: Guru Gobind Singh Ji's journey from Talwandi Sabo through Rajputana and toward the Deccan, and the significance of this southward journey.

lessons.title: Talwandi Sabo: The Damdami Bir and Preparation
lessons.summary: The Guru's extended stay at Talwandi Sabo (Damdama Sahib), the tradition of the Damdami Bir, and the theological preparation for what was to come.

lessons.title: Aurangzeb, the Zafarnama, and the Deccan Campaign
lessons.summary: The diplomatic dimensions of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's final years, including the Zafarnama's impact and the relationship with Bahadur Shah.

lessons.title: Meeting Banda Singh Bahadur (Madho Das) at Nanded
lessons.summary: The encounter between Guru Gobind Singh Ji and Madho Das, the hermit who would become Banda Singh Bahadur, and the theological dimensions of this meeting.

lessons.title: The Transformation of Madho Das into Banda Singh Bahadur
lessons.summary: The initiation of Madho Das into the Khalsa, the name and mission he received from the Guru, and the significance of this transformation.

lessons.title: Banda Singh's Mission to Punjab
lessons.summary: Banda Singh Bahadur's departure from Nanded and his subsequent campaigns in Punjab, contextualized within Guru Gobind Singh Ji's broader mission.

lessons.title: The Stabbing at Nanded: Events and Sources
lessons.summary: The assassination attempt on Guru Gobind Singh Ji at Nanded, the sources for this event, and the Guru's response.

lessons.title: The Wound Reopens: Final Days
lessons.summary: The reopening of the Guru's wound, the final period at Nanded, and the gathering of the Sangat for the final Hukam.

lessons.title: The Final Hukam: Guruship Conferred on the Granth and Panth
lessons.summary: The central event of the Nanded period: the Guru's final Hukam conferring eternal Guruship on the Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji and the Khalsa Panth.

lessons.title: The Shabad Guru: Theological Foundations
lessons.summary: The theological concept of the Shabad Guru — the divine Word as eternal Guru — and its roots in the teachings of all ten Gurus.

lessons.title: The Panth as Guru: Institutional Implications
lessons.summary: The institutional significance of the Guru Panth concept, the authority of the Sarbat Khalsa, and the Sikh Rehat Maryada.

lessons.title: Takht Sri Hazur Sahib and the Living Legacy of Nanded
lessons.summary: The Gurdwara at Nanded, its significance as one of the five Takhts, and the living legacy of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's final Hukam.

courses.title: Historical Sources: Gurbilas Patshahi Dasvin and the Scholarly Record
courses.summary: This course offers a rigorous examination of the primary and secondary historical sources for Guru Gobind Singh Ji's life, with sustained focus on the Gurbilas Patshahi 10 of Kuir Singh and its relationship to the Bachittar Natak, Sri Gur Sobha, and Twarikh Guru Khalsa. Students develop skills in source criticism, historiographical method, and the evaluation of conflicting testimonies, learning to distinguish between well-documented events, events known primarily through oral tradition, and events that remain historically uncertain. The course equips students to read Sikh historical literature with scholarly precision.
outcomes: Apply source-critical methods to major Sikh historical texts dealing with Guru Gobind Singh Ji
Evaluate the specific merits and limitations of each primary source for Guru Gobind Singh Ji's life
Identify the chronological errors in Kuir Singh's Gurbilas and explain how modern scholarship corrects them
Distinguish between events documented in multiple independent sources and events known from single sources
Explain the relationship between historical biography and hagiographical tradition in Sikh literature
Assess how Persian and Mughal administrative sources can corroborate or complicate Sikh biographical accounts

lessons.title: Introduction to Sikh Historical Methodology
lessons.summary: An introduction to the specific challenges and methods of Sikh historical scholarship, with attention to the unique characteristics of the Sikh source tradition.

lessons.title: The Bachittar Natak: Autobiography as Primary Source
lessons.summary: Analysis of the Bachittar Natak as a primary source for Guru Gobind Singh Ji's life, its value and its limitations.

lessons.title: Sri Gur Sobha: A Near-Contemporary Account
lessons.summary: Analysis of Senapati's Sri Gur Sobha as a near-contemporary source, its strengths, and the significant gaps it leaves in the historical record.

lessons.title: Kuir Singh's Gurbilas: The Most Detailed Early Biography
lessons.summary: An introduction to Kuir Singh as author, the composition and structure of the Gurbilas Patshahi 10, and its overall historical significance.

lessons.title: The Strengths of the Gurbilas Patshahi 10
lessons.summary: A systematic account of the specific historical contributions made by Kuir Singh's Gurbilas, identifying what it tells us that no earlier source records.

lessons.title: The Weaknesses and Errors in the Gurbilas Patshahi 10
lessons.summary: A systematic account of the specific historical errors and limitations in Kuir Singh's Gurbilas as identified by Dr. Fauja Singh and other modern scholars.

lessons.title: Shahid Bilas and the Bhat Vahis
lessons.summary: The Shahid Bilas of Bhai Seva Singh and the Bhat Vahi genealogical registers as independent corroborating sources for key events.

lessons.title: Persian Sources and the Mughal Administrative Record
lessons.summary: The Persian language sources — Mughal administrative chronicles, Persian court histories — and what they contribute to the historical record of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's life.

lessons.title: Giani Gian Singh's Twarikh Guru Khalsa: A Later Synthesis
lessons.summary: The Twarikh Guru Khalsa as a nineteenth-century synthesis, its method, its value, and its limitations as a historical source.

lessons.title: Comparing the Sources: Points of Convergence and Divergence
lessons.summary: A comparative analysis of the four major sources, identifying where they converge (providing stronger historical grounds) and where they diverge (requiring scholarly judgment).

lessons.title: Hagiography and History: Understanding the Relationship
lessons.summary: A theoretical discussion of the relationship between hagiographical and historical writing in the Sikh tradition, and how students should navigate this relationship.

lessons.title: Applying Source Criticism: A Practical Synthesis
lessons.summary: A practical application of the source-critical methods developed throughout the course to specific historical questions about Guru Gobind Singh Ji's life.

courses.title: The First Udasi: Guru Nanak's Journeys East — Sultanpur to Assam
courses.summary: This course traces Guru Nanak's first great journey (udasi) eastward from Sultanpur Lodhi, following the accounts preserved in the Janamsakhis and Kavi Santokh Singh's Sri Nanak Prakash. Students examine key encounters at Hardwar, Benaras, Gaya, Puri, and the distant eastern reaches including Dhubri and Assam. The course grounds devotional narrative in historical geography and critically evaluates the sources that preserve these accounts.
outcomes: Identify the major stopping points of the First Udasi using primary janamsakhi accounts
Analyze the theological significance of Guru Nanak's challenge to ritual water-throwing at Hardwar
Compare the devotional and historical methods used by scholars to evaluate udasi narratives
Explain how the First Udasi established foundational Sikh teachings on naam, seva, and equality
Evaluate the role of Bhai Mardana as companion and musical collaborator throughout the journey
Assess the literary structure of Sri Nanak Prakash as a source for udasi geography and chronology
references: Santokh Singh, Kavi. Sri Nanak Prakash. Amritsar: Khalsa Samachar, 1843.
McLeod, W. H. Guru Nanak and the Sikh Religion. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1968.
McLeod, W. H., trans. and ed. The B40 Janam-Sakhi. Amritsar: Guru Nanak Dev University, 1980.
