courses.title: The Sikh Empire: Advanced Political and Military History
courses.source: Kavi Santokh Singh, Suraj Prakash Granth (1843); Khushwant Singh, A History of the Sikhs (1963)
courses.summary: This graduate seminar examines the Sikh Empire (1799–1849) through advanced political, military, and administrative lenses, drawing on primary Punjabi sources alongside modern historiography. Students engage critically with court records, Anglo-Sikh diplomatic correspondence, and contemporary scholarship to reassess the nature and legacy of Maharaja Ranjit Singh's state. The course ends with the annexation, its causes, and its long interpretive shadow.

Evaluate the role of the ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ Fauj in empire-building and its transformation under European officers.

Reconstruct the internal political tensions of the Lahore Darbar after Ranjit Singh's death.
Situate the annexation of 1849 within broader colonial and postcolonial historiographical debates.

Gurharpal Singh and Giorgio Shani, Sikh Nationalism: From a Dominant Minority to an Ethno-Religious Diaspora (Cambridge University Press, 2021)
Khushwant Singh, A History of the Sikhs, Vol. 2 (Princeton University Press, 1966)
Richard Fox, Lions of the Punjab: Culture in the Making (University of California Press, 1985)

lessons.title: Theology of Resistance: ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ and the Political Imperative
lessons.summary: Examines the theological foundations of Sikh resistance in the doctrine of ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ and the historical martyrdom tradition.

lessons.title: The Misl Confederacies as Resistance Organizations
lessons.summary: Examines the twelve ਮਿਸਲ confederacies as both resistance organizations and proto-state formations, analyzing their military tactics and political structure.

lessons.title: Namdhari Movement: Religious Reform and Colonial Resistance
lessons.summary: Examines the ਨਾਮਧਾਰੀ movement of Baba Ram Singh as a form of anti-colonial resistance combining religious reform with explicit political defiance.

lessons.title: The Singh Sabha and Cultural Resistance
lessons.summary: Examines the Singh Sabha movement as a form of cultural and intellectual resistance to colonial assimilation and Hindu absorptionism.

lessons.title: Gurdwara Reform Movement: The Akali Morcha 1920–1925
lessons.summary: Examines the ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ reform movement of the 1920s — its organization, tactics, and culmination in the Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925.

lessons.title: The Akali Party and Legislative Politics
lessons.summary: Examines the Akali Dal's evolution from protest movement to political party, its participation in legislative politics, and its oscillation between accommodation and resistance.

lessons.title: Partition Politics: The Sikh Demand for Sovereignty
lessons.summary: Examines Sikh political demands during the independence and partition negotiations, including the proposal for a Sikh sovereign state.

lessons.title: Post-Partition Adjustment: Punjab Suba and Language Politics
lessons.summary: Examines the ਪੰਜਾਬ ਸੂਬਾ movement and the reorganization of Indian states on linguistic lines, analyzing the Sikh demand for a Punjabi-speaking state.

lessons.title: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution and its Interpretations
lessons.summary: Examines the Anandpur Sahib Resolution of 1973, its content, its contested interpretation, and its role in precipitating the crisis of the 1980s.

lessons.title: The 1984 Crisis: Blue Star, Assassination, and November Pogrom
lessons.summary: Provides scholarly analysis of Operation Blue Star, the assassination of Indira Gandhi, and the November 1984 anti-Sikh violence in their historical and political context.

lessons.title: Diaspora Activism and Transnational Resistance
lessons.summary: Examines Sikh diaspora communities as sites of political activism, analyzing transnational networks of resistance and their relationships to homeland politics.

lessons.title: Resistance, Memory, and Contemporary Sikh Political Thought
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the history of Sikh resistance movements, examining memory, political theology, and contemporary debates about sovereignty and identity.

courses.title: Critical Analysis of Primary Sources in Sikh History
courses.source: Multiple primary Sikh historical sources; historical methodology
courses.summary: This graduate seminar develops rigorous methodological skills for critically analyzing the diverse primary sources used in Sikh historical research, from ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ and early hagiographic literature through colonial administrative records and oral traditions. Students learn to assess the provenance, authorial perspective, genre conventions, and evidential value of each source type, situating them within the broader historiography of Sikh studies. The course equips scholars with the critical toolkit needed for original archival research.
outcomes: Classify and critically evaluate the major categories of primary sources in Sikh historical research.
Apply source-critical methodology to Sikh ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ, ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ, and court chronicle traditions.
Analyze colonial-era British records and their structural biases for Sikh history.
Reconstruct historical events from multiple conflicting sources using triangulation methodology.
Formulate an original research question grounded in primary source analysis.

W.H. McLeod, The Evolution of the Sikh Community (Oxford University Press, 1976)

Louis E. Fenech and W.H. McLeod, Historical Dictionary of Sikhism, 3rd ed. (Rowman and Littlefield, 2014)

lessons.title: Introduction to Primary Source Criticism in Sikh History
lessons.summary: Establishes the methodological foundations for primary source criticism, surveying the major categories of sources available for Sikh historical research.

lessons.title: The Janamsakhi Tradition: Hagiography and History
lessons.summary: Critical examination of the ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ tradition as both historical evidence and literary genre, analyzing the McLeod methodology and its scholarly reception.

lessons.title: Gurbani as Historical Source: Possibilities and Limits
lessons.summary: Examines methodological approaches to using ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ as historical evidence, distinguishing between theological and historical questions.

lessons.title: The Gurbilas Genre: Heroic Literature and Historical Evidence
lessons.summary: Analyzes the ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ literary genre, its conventions, and its value as historical evidence for the later Guru period and early Khalsa.

lessons.title: Hukamname: Documentary Evidence from the Gurus
lessons.summary: Examines the ਹੁਕਮਨਾਮੇ as the most direct documentary evidence for Guru-period institutional history, analyzing their authentication and evidential value.

lessons.title: Rehatnamas: Prescriptive Literature and Social History
lessons.summary: Examines the ਰਹਿਤਨਾਮੇ as evidence for early Khalsa religious practice and the methodological challenges of using prescriptive literature as historical evidence.

lessons.title: Persian-Language Chronicles: Mughal and Sikh Court Sources
lessons.summary: Examines Persian-language historical chronicles as sources for Sikh history, analyzing their perspectives, conventions, and evidential value.

lessons.title: Colonial British Records: The India Office Archive
lessons.summary: Examines British India Office Records as sources for Sikh history, analyzing their structure, biases, and methodological requirements.

lessons.title: European Traveler Accounts and Their Biases
lessons.summary: Examines European traveler and officer accounts as sources for Sikh history, analyzing Orientalist frameworks and extracting usable historical evidence.

lessons.title: Oral Tradition as Historical Source
lessons.summary: Examines oral traditions in Sikh historical research, analyzing their nature, transmission, and methodological requirements.

lessons.title: Manuscript Studies: Reading the Physical Document
lessons.summary: Introduces manuscript studies methodology as applied to Sikh historical documents, including paleography, codicology, and digital manuscript analysis.

lessons.title: Triangulation and Synthesis: Reconstructing History from Multiple Sources
lessons.summary: Provides advanced methodology for triangulating across multiple source types to reconstruct historical events and processes in Sikh history.

courses.title: Historical Linguistics of Punjabi and Gurmukhi
courses.source: Prof. Sahib Singh, Gurbani Vyakaran; Punjabi linguistic history
courses.summary: This graduate seminar traces the historical development of the Punjabi language and the ਗੁਰਮੁਖੀ script from their Indo-Aryan origins through the medieval period and the Gurbani corpus. Students apply the methods of historical linguistics — phonological reconstruction, morphological change, lexical borrowing — to Punjabi and to the linguistic register of ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ. The course situates Punjabi within the broader context of Indo-Aryan language history and examines the ਗੁਰਮੁਖੀ script's origins, development, and standardization.
outcomes: Apply the comparative method of historical linguistics to trace Punjabi's development from Old Indo-Aryan.
Analyze sound changes, morphological shifts, and syntactic developments in the history of Punjabi.
Assess the origins and development of the ਗੁਰਮੁਖੀ script using paleographic and epigraphic evidence.
Identify and analyze lexical borrowings from Persian, Sanskrit, Arabic, and other languages in Gurbani.
Situate Punjabi within the broader typology of Indo-Aryan and South Asian areal linguistics.
references: Prof. Sahib Singh, Gurbani Vyakaran (Amritsar: Singh Brothers, 1939)
Harkirat Singh, Punjabi Bhasha da Itihas (Patiala: Punjabi University, 1969)

lessons.title: Indo-Aryan Origins: Punjabi in the Family Tree
lessons.summary: Situates Punjabi within the broader Indo-Aryan language family, tracing its genetic relationships and geographic position.

lessons.title: Old Indo-Aryan: Vedic and Sanskrit Foundations
lessons.summary: Examines Old Indo-Aryan (Vedic and Sanskrit) as the historical basis for Punjabi linguistic development.

lessons.title: Middle Indo-Aryan: Prakrits and Apabhramsha
lessons.summary: Examines Middle Indo-Aryan stages — Prakrits and Apabhramsha — as intermediaries between Sanskrit and modern Punjabi.

lessons.title: The Emergence of Punjabi: Early New Indo-Aryan
lessons.summary: Traces the emergence of Punjabi as a distinct New Indo-Aryan language in the medieval period.

lessons.title: Gurmukhi Script: Origins and Development
lessons.summary: Examines the origins, development, and standardization of the ਗੁਰਮੁਖੀ script, situating it within the broader history of Indian writing systems.

lessons.title: Punjabi Phonology: Tones and Their Historical Origins
lessons.summary: Examines the typologically distinctive tonal system of Punjabi, analyzing its historical origins and its significance for reading Gurbani.

lessons.title: Morphological History: Nouns, Cases, and Postpositions
lessons.summary: Traces the development of the Punjabi nominal system from Old Indo-Aryan through the Gurbani period to modern usage.

lessons.title: Verb System History: From Sanskrit to Gurbani
lessons.summary: Traces the development of the Punjabi verb system through Middle Indo-Aryan to the archaic and modern forms found in Gurbani.

lessons.title: Lexical Strata: Sanskrit, Persian, Arabic, and Vernacular
lessons.summary: Analyzes the multiple lexical strata of Gurbani vocabulary, identifying the source languages and patterns of borrowing.

lessons.title: Gurbani's Linguistic Diversity: Sant Bhasha and Regional Languages
lessons.summary: Examines the multiple linguistic registers and regional language elements in Gurbani, including ਸੰਤ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ and the regional compositions.

lessons.title: Standardization and Script Reform: Colonial and Post-colonial
lessons.summary: Examines the standardization of written Punjabi through the colonial and post-independence periods, analyzing the politics of script and language.

lessons.title: Dialectology: Varieties of Punjabi and Their Historical Relationships
lessons.summary: Examines the major dialect varieties of Punjabi and the historical linguistic relationships among them, including their significance for Gurbani interpretation.

courses.title: Sant Bhasha: Advanced Study of Gurbani's Linguistic Register
courses.source: Prof. Sahib Singh, Shabadarth Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji (1962)
courses.summary: This graduate seminar provides an advanced study of ਸੰਤ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ — the pan-regional devotional register of North Indian bhakti literature — as it appears in the ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ. Students analyze the linguistic features of this register across the Gurbani corpus, examining its relationship to Sanskrit, Persian, and regional vernacular traditions. The course develops both linguistic and hermeneutic competencies essential for advanced Gurbani scholarship.
outcomes: Define and characterize ਸੰਤ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ as a distinct pan-regional literary register.
Identify and analyze the major linguistic strata (Sanskrit, Persian, regional vernacular) in Gurbani compositions.
Apply Prof. Sahib Singh's grammatical framework to advanced analysis of selected Gurbani passages.
Compare the linguistic registers of different ਭਗਤਾਂ and Gurus represented in the ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ.
Evaluate major scholarly interpretations of Sant Bhasha and its relationship to Punjabi vernacular tradition.

lessons.title: Defining Sant Bhasha: Historical and Linguistic Parameters
lessons.summary: Establishes the definition, boundaries, and key features of ਸੰਤ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ as a scholarly category.

lessons.title: The North Indian Bhakti Movement and Its Literary Language
lessons.summary: Contextualizes Sant Bhasha within the broader North Indian Bhakti movement, examining the literary traditions and theological concerns that shaped the register.

lessons.title: Guru Nanak Dev Ji's Linguistic Range: A Survey
lessons.summary: Surveys the extraordinary linguistic range of Guru Nanak Dev Ji's compositions, analyzing the multiple registers and languages employed.

lessons.title: The Bhagat Bani: Regional Languages in the Guru Granth Sahib
lessons.summary: Examines the compositions of the non-Guru ਭਗਤਾਂ included in the Guru Granth Sahib, analyzing their diverse linguistic backgrounds.

lessons.title: Sanskrit Register in Gurbani: Sahaskrit and Slokas
lessons.summary: Analyzes the Sanskrit-register compositions in Gurbani, including the ਸਹਸਕ੍ਰਿਤ and ਸਲੋਕ ਸਹਸਕ੍ਰਿਤ sections.

lessons.title: Braj Bhasha in the Guru Granth Sahib
lessons.summary: Examines the Braj Bhasha compositions in the Guru Granth Sahib, analyzing their linguistic features and their relationship to North Indian literary tradition.

lessons.title: Persian and Arabic Vocabulary in Gurbani
lessons.summary: Analyzes the Persian and Arabic vocabulary layer in Gurbani, examining its linguistic features, semantic associations, and theological deployment.

lessons.title: The Ragas as Linguistic Contexts
lessons.summary: Examines how the raga system of the Guru Granth Sahib creates distinct musical and linguistic contexts that shape compositional language.

lessons.title: Prof. Sahib Singh's Shabadarth: Methodology and Achievement
lessons.summary: Provides a critical scholarly assessment of Prof. Sahib Singh's Shabadarth methodology, its strengths, limitations, and its place in Gurbani scholarship.

lessons.title: Hermeneutic Approaches to Gurbani Language
lessons.summary: Surveys major hermeneutic approaches to Gurbani interpretation, examining how linguistic analysis relates to theological understanding.

lessons.title: Sant Bhasha and Vernacular Authenticity
lessons.summary: Examines the theological and literary significance of the choice of vernacular language in Gurbani, analyzing what this choice meant in historical context.

lessons.title: Advanced Textual Analysis: Selected Gurbani Passages
lessons.summary: Applies the course's full analytical apparatus to advanced close reading of selected Gurbani passages, demonstrating integrated linguistic and hermeneutic analysis.

courses.title: Gurmukhi Paleography: Reading Historical Manuscripts
courses.source: Dr. Kamalroop Singh, manuscript studies; Sikh manuscript tradition
courses.summary: This graduate seminar develops the skills required to read, date, and critically analyze historical Gurmukhi manuscripts from the sixteenth through the nineteenth centuries. Students learn the methods of Gurmukhi paleography, codicology, and manuscript studies, applying these to Sikh primary sources including early Guru Granth Sahib manuscripts, Rehatnamas, and court documents. The course bridges linguistic competence and archival research, equipping scholars for original manuscript-based research.
outcomes: Read and transcribe historical Gurmukhi manuscripts from different periods with accuracy.
Date manuscripts using paleographic criteria and compare multiple manuscript traditions.
Apply codicological analysis to assess manuscript production, provenance, and use.
Identify scribal conventions and their significance for textual criticism.
Situate manuscript evidence within the broader history of Sikh scriptural transmission.

lessons.title: Introduction to Gurmukhi Paleography
lessons.summary: Establishes the methodological foundations of Gurmukhi paleography, introducing the historical development of the script and its significance for Sikh studies.

lessons.title: The Script Family: Brahmi to Gurmukhi
lessons.summary: Traces the script-historical lineage from Brahmi through Sharda and Landa to the standardized Gurmukhi of the Sikh tradition.

lessons.title: Dating Methods: Paleographic Criteria
lessons.summary: Develops the practical skills for dating Gurmukhi manuscripts using paleographic evidence, including letter form evolution and diacritical conventions.

lessons.title: Early Manuscripts: The Guru Period (1500s–1700s)
lessons.summary: Examines manuscripts from the Guru period, with particular focus on the scriptural manuscripts and their evidential significance.

lessons.title: Scribal Conventions and Their Variation
lessons.summary: Examines scribal conventions in the Gurmukhi manuscript tradition, analyzing variation and its significance for manuscript study.

lessons.title: Codicology: The Manuscript as Physical Object
lessons.summary: Introduces codicological analysis — the study of the manuscript as a physical object — and its application to Gurmukhi manuscripts.

lessons.title: The Kartarpur Bir and Its Significance
lessons.summary: Examines the Kartarpur manuscript of the Guru Granth Sahib — one of the most significant manuscripts in the Sikh tradition — and its scholarly importance.

lessons.title: Regional and Sectarian Manuscript Traditions
lessons.summary: Examines the diversity of Gurmukhi manuscript traditions associated with different regions and Sikh sectarian communities.

lessons.title: The Damdami Bir and Textual Standardization
lessons.summary: Examines the Damdami recension of the Guru Granth Sahib attributed to Guru Gobind Singh Ji and its role in standardizing the scriptural text.

lessons.title: Court Manuscripts: The Sikh Empire Period
lessons.summary: Examines manuscripts produced under Sikh imperial patronage, analyzing their distinctive features and evidential value.

lessons.title: Colonial-Era Transcription and Its Implications
lessons.summary: Examines the transcription and cataloguing of Gurmukhi manuscripts by colonial scholars and institutions, analyzing the implications for subsequent scholarship.

lessons.title: Digital Paleography: Methods and Resources
lessons.summary: Introduces digital methods and resources for Gurmukhi paleography, including digitization projects, imaging technologies, and online databases.

courses.title: Advanced Gurbani Grammar and Syntax
courses.source: Prof. Sahib Singh, Gurbani Vyakaran (1939); SGGS
courses.summary: This graduate seminar provides a comprehensive and rigorous study of ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ grammar and syntax, using Prof. Sahib Singh's Gurbani Vyakaran as the foundational text while extending the analysis through advanced morphological and syntactic study. Students develop the grammatical competence required for independent advanced analysis of ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ passages, mastering the archaic features, multi-language constructions, and poetic syntactic inversions that characterize the language of the ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ.
outcomes: Apply advanced grammatical analysis to ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ passages, identifying parts of speech and their functions.
Analyze archaic morphological features in Gurbani that differ from modern Punjabi.
Identify and interpret poetic syntactic inversions and ellipses characteristic of Gurbani composition.
Distinguish between multiple linguistic registers in Gurbani and apply appropriate grammatical frameworks to each.
Evaluate competing grammatical interpretations of ambiguous Gurbani passages using philological criteria.

lessons.title: The Grammar of Gurbani: Framework and Methodology
lessons.summary: Establishes the methodological framework for advanced grammatical analysis of Gurbani, situating Prof. Sahib Singh's work within broader linguistic context.

lessons.title: The Noun System: Cases, Gender, and Number
lessons.summary: Provides advanced analysis of the Gurbani nominal system, including archaic case forms, gender agreement, and number marking.

lessons.title: The Pronoun System: Person, Number, and Honorifics
lessons.summary: Analyzes the Gurbani pronoun system, including archaic pronoun forms and the honorific distinctions that carry theological significance.

lessons.title: Adjectives and Adjectival Agreement
lessons.summary: Analyzes adjectival forms and agreement patterns in Gurbani, including archaic forms and their significance for interpretation.

lessons.title: The Verb System: Roots, Stems, and Basic Forms
lessons.summary: Provides systematic analysis of the Gurbani verb system, from root identification through stem formation to the major finite and non-finite forms.

lessons.title: Tense, Aspect, and Modality in Gurbani
lessons.summary: Examines the expression of tense, aspect, and modality in Gurbani, analyzing the theological significance of temporal and modal distinctions.

lessons.title: Participial and Converb Constructions
lessons.summary: Analyzes the participial and converb (verbal adverb) constructions that are among the most characteristic features of Gurbani syntax.

lessons.title: Postpositions and Relational Marking
lessons.summary: Provides advanced analysis of the postpositional system in Gurbani, examining both archaic and standard forms and their syntactic functions.

lessons.title: Sandhi Rules in Gurbani
lessons.summary: Examines the sandhi (phonological junction) rules that apply at word boundaries in Gurbani, and their significance for reading and interpretation.

lessons.title: Compound Formation (Samas)
lessons.summary: Analyzes the formation and interpretation of compound words in Gurbani, particularly the Sanskrit-derived compound types that characterize elevated registers.

lessons.title: Poetic Syntax: Inversion, Ellipsis, and Meter
lessons.summary: Examines the poetic syntactic features of Gurbani — inversions, ellipses, and metrical constraints — and their implications for grammatical analysis.

lessons.title: Grammatical Ambiguity and Interpretation
lessons.summary: Addresses the management of grammatical ambiguity in Gurbani — passages where multiple grammatical analyses are possible — and the interpretive resources for resolving or maintaining ambiguity.

courses.title: Bhai Vir Singh: Advanced Literary and Theological Study
courses.source: Bhai Vir Singh complete works; Sikh literary scholarship
courses.summary: This graduate seminar provides an advanced study of Bhai Vir Singh (1872–1957) — poet, novelist, editor, and scholar — as the central figure in modern Sikh literary and intellectual history. Students engage critically with his major works across genres (poetry, fiction, commentary, journalism), analyzing their literary strategies, theological concerns, and historical significance. The course situates Bhai Vir Singh at the intersection of the Singh Sabha reformist movement, colonial modernity, and the Punjabi literary renaissance he embodied and shaped.
outcomes: Critically analyze Bhai Vir Singh's poetry using both Punjabi literary critical frameworks and comparative literary theory.
Assess Bhai Vir Singh's novels as interventions in colonial-era Sikh religious and cultural politics.
Evaluate his scholarly and editorial work on Sikh scripture and its legacy in Sikh studies.
Situate his career within the Singh Sabha movement and the broader context of colonial Punjab.
Develop original scholarly arguments about specific aspects of his literary or theological achievement.

lessons.summary: Situates Bhai Vir Singh within the Singh Sabha movement and the colonial Punjabi literary environment, establishing his significance as the founder of modern Punjabi literature.

lessons.title: The Sikh Novel: Sundri and the Founding of Punjabi Fiction
lessons.summary: Analyzes Bhai Vir Singh's first novel Sundri (1898) as a foundational text of modern Punjabi fiction, examining its narrative strategies and reformist agenda.

lessons.title: Vijay Singh and Bijay Singh: Historical Romance and Religious Identity
lessons.summary: Analyzes Bhai Vir Singh's second and third novels, examining their development of the historical fiction genre and their construction of Sikh religious identity.

lessons.title: Rana Surat Singh: Epic Poetry and Mystical Vision
lessons.summary: Provides advanced analysis of Bhai Vir Singh's major epic poem Rana Surat Singh (1905), examining its mystical theology and literary achievement.

lessons.title: Nature Poetry: The Khamosh Banat Series
lessons.summary: Analyzes Bhai Vir Singh's nature poetry collections, examining his use of natural imagery for theological reflection.

lessons.title: The Poetry of Longing: ਵਿਰਹ and Mystical Experience
lessons.summary: Examines Bhai Vir Singh's lyric poetry of mystical longing, analyzing the theological content and literary form of his ਵਿਰਹ poetry.

lessons.title: Bhai Vir Singh as Editor: The Khalsa Samachar
lessons.summary: Examines Bhai Vir Singh's editorial career, particularly the Khalsa Samachar newspaper, and its role in shaping modern Sikh public culture.

lessons.title: Scriptural Scholarship: Commentaries on Gurbani
lessons.summary: Examines Bhai Vir Singh's commentaries on Gurbani texts and other scriptural works, analyzing their methodology and scholarly significance.

lessons.title: Theological Vision: ਗੁਰਮਤਿ in Literary Form
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the theological vision expressed across Bhai Vir Singh's literary and scholarly work, analyzing its coherence and distinctiveness.

lessons.title: Gender and the Divine Feminine in Bhai Vir Singh's Work
lessons.summary: Examines representations of gender and the divine feminine in Bhai Vir Singh's poetry and fiction, drawing on feminist theological frameworks.

lessons.title: Colonial Modernity and Sikh Identity in his Writing
lessons.summary: Examines how Bhai Vir Singh's work engaged with and resisted colonial modernity in the construction of a specifically Sikh modern literary identity.

lessons.title: Legacy and Influence: Bhai Vir Singh in Punjabi Literary History
lessons.summary: Assesses Bhai Vir Singh's lasting legacy in Punjabi literature and Sikh intellectual life, examining his influence on subsequent generations.

courses.title: Sikh Narrative Theory and the Janamsakhi Tradition
courses.source: Kavi Santokh Singh, Sri Nanak Prakash; W.H. McLeod, Early Sikh Tradition (1980)
courses.summary: This graduate seminar applies narrative theory to the study of Sikh hagiographic literature, with particular focus on the ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ tradition and the ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ genre. Students engage with contemporary narratological frameworks alongside traditional Sikh literary critical approaches, analyzing how narrative structures, character, point of view, and genre conventions shape the theological meanings of Sikh hagiographic texts. The course develops advanced competence in the literary analysis of Sikh devotional narrative.
outcomes: Apply narratological frameworks (Genette, Bal, Prince) to the analysis of Sikh hagiographic narrative.
Analyze character construction, narrative voice, and focalization in major ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ traditions.
Distinguish the generic conventions of ਜਨਮਸਾਖੀ from ਗੁਰਬਿਲਾਸ and ਸ਼ਬਦ traditions.
Evaluate W.H. McLeod's form-critical methodology and its reception in Sikh studies.
Develop original scholarly readings of specific ਸਾਖੀਆਂ using integrated narrative-theological analysis.

W.H. McLeod, The Evolution of the Sikh Community (Oxford University Press, 1976)

lessons.title: Narrative Theory and Sacred Hagiography

lessons.title: The Janamsakhi Traditions: A Survey

lessons.title: The Sakhi as Narrative Unit: Structure and Function
lessons.summary: Analyzes the ਸਾਖੀ as the basic narrative unit of the Janamsakhi tradition, examining its typical structure and theological function.

lessons.title: Character in Janamsakhi Narrative: The Guru and His Companions

lessons.title: Miracle Narratives: The Karamat Episode
lessons.summary: Provides advanced analysis of miracle narrative as a genre feature of the Janamsakhi tradition, examining its narrative structure and theological function.

lessons.title: Narrative Voice and Focalization
lessons.summary: Applies Genette's and Bal's frameworks for narrative voice and focalization to the analysis of Janamsakhi narrative perspective.

lessons.title: The Bala Janamsakhi: Textual History and Critical Analysis
lessons.summary: Provides advanced critical analysis of the Bala Janamsakhi tradition, examining its textual history, distinctive features, and McLeod's critical assessment.

lessons.title: The Puratan Janamsakhi: The Earliest Tradition
lessons.summary: Analyzes the Puratan Janamsakhi tradition as the earliest surviving major Janamsakhi, examining its distinctive narrative features.

lessons.title: The Miharban Tradition: Hagiography and Exegesis
lessons.summary: Analyzes the distinctive Miharban Janamsakhi tradition, which integrates hagiographic narrative with extended scriptural commentary.

lessons.title: The Gurbilas Genre: Heroic Narrative and Military Hagiography
lessons.summary: Analyzes the Gurbilas genre as a related but distinct hagiographic tradition, examining its narrative features and theological concerns.

lessons.title: Kavi Santokh Singh's Sri Nanak Prakash: Epic Hagiography
lessons.summary: Provides advanced analysis of Kavi Santokh Singh's Sri Nanak Prakash as the culminating text of the classical Sikh hagiographic tradition.

lessons.title: Contemporary Approaches: Janamsakhi in Performance and Community
lessons.summary: Examines the Janamsakhi tradition in its living dimensions — oral performance, community use, and contemporary reinterpretation.

courses.title: Gurmat Poetics: Rasa, Meter, and Sacred Aesthetics
courses.source: SGGS; Bharata Muni Natyashastra; Anandavardhana Dhvanyaloka; Pashaura Singh; Mandair; Mann
courses.summary: This graduate seminar undertakes a systematic study of the poetics of the Guru Granth Sahib, examining the literary dimensions of Gurbani through the frameworks of classical Indian aesthetics (rasa theory, dhvani), Sanskrit prosody, and the specific formal conventions of the SGGS's raag-organized composition. Students develop analytical capacities for close reading of Gurbani as literary-theological text.
outcomes: Apply classical Indian rasa theory and dhvani doctrine to the analysis of specific SGGS compositions
Analyze the metrical structures and prosodic conventions of major Gurbani poetic forms
Examine the theological function of aesthetic experience in Gurmat spiritual epistemology
Critically evaluate the relationship between the raag system and the semantic content of specific banis
Develop original close readings of SGGS compositions that integrate literary and theological analysis
references: Pashaura Singh, The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority (2000)
Gurinder Singh Mann, The Making of Sikh Scripture (2001)
Arvind-Pal Singh Mandair, Religion and the Specter of the West: Sikhism, India, Postcoloniality, and the Politics of Translation (2009)
Nikky-Guninder Kaur Singh, The Name of My Beloved: Verses of the Sikh Gurus (1995)
Bharata Muni, Natyashastra, trans. Adya Rangacharya (1996)
Anandavardhana, Dhvanyaloka, trans. Daniel Ingalls et al. (1990)
Surjit Hans, A Reconstruction of Sikh History from Sikh Literature (1988)
Christopher Shackle and Arvind Mandair, eds., Teachings of the Sikh Gurus (2005)

lessons.title: Introduction: Gurbani as Literary-Theological Text
lessons.summary: Frames the seminar's approach to Gurbani as simultaneously literary, musical, and theological text.

lessons.title: Classical Indian Aesthetics: Rasa Theory and Dhvani Doctrine

lessons.title: The Raag System of the SGGS: Musical Mode and Theological Meaning
lessons.summary: Examines the SGGS's organization by raag and the relationship between musical mode and theological content.

lessons.title: Prosody and Meter in Gurbani: ਛੰਦ and Compositional Form
lessons.summary: Examines the metrical and prosodic structures of Gurbani, including the major compositional forms.

lessons.title: The Vaar Form: Heroic Ballad and Divine Praise
lessons.summary: Examines the vaar as a literary form and its theological adaptation in the SGGS.

lessons.title: Bhagat Bani: The Non-Guru Compositions and Their Integration
lessons.summary: Examines the Bhagat compositions in the SGGS and their theological and literary integration.

lessons.title: Feminine Voice and Bridal Mysticism in the SGGS
lessons.summary: Examines the feminine voice, bridal mysticism, and the theological function of gendered language in the SGGS.

lessons.title: Metaphor, Symbol, and the Language of Sacred Experience
lessons.summary: Examines the major metaphors and symbols of Gurbani and their role in communicating the uncommunicable dimensions of spiritual experience.

lessons.title: Sound Theology: ਅਨਾਹਦ, ਸ਼ਬਦ, and the Ontology of Sacred Sound
lessons.summary: Examines the SGGS's theology of sound and its relationship to the literary and musical dimensions of Gurbani.

lessons.title: Kirtan Performance and the Actualization of Literary Meaning
lessons.summary: Examines the relationship between performance and text in the actualization of Gurbani's literary-theological meaning.

lessons.title: Modern Literary Theory and Gurbani: Hermeneutic Approaches
lessons.summary: Examines how modern literary theory can be productively applied to Gurbani while remaining alert to its limits.

lessons.title: Synthesis: Toward a Comprehensive Gurmat Poetics
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the course into a comprehensive framework for Gurmat poetics as a scholarly discipline.

courses.title: Advanced Sikh Psychology and Contemplative Science
courses.source: SGGS; Transpersonal Psychology; William James; Abraham Maslow; Ken Wilber; Varela
courses.summary: This graduate seminar develops a comprehensive Sikh psychology grounded in the SGGS's account of mind, self, and transformation, in sustained dialogue with contemporary psychological science. Students analyze the Gurmat model of the human mind, the psychology of ਹਉਮੈ and the five vikars, the contemplative science of ਸਿਮਰਨ, and the ultimate states of ਸਹਜ and liberation.
outcomes: Articulate the Gurmat model of the human mind, including its analysis of consciousness, ego, and the path to liberation
Apply psychological frameworks — cognitive, transpersonal, contemplative — to analyze Gurmat accounts of mental functioning
Critically evaluate the relationship between Sikh contemplative practices and psychological wellbeing
Develop integrative frameworks that honor both the first-person phenomenology of Sikh practice and third-person psychological research
Analyze the clinical and pastoral implications of Sikh psychology for mental health care in Sikh communities
references: William James, The Varieties of Religious Experience (1902)
Abraham Maslow, Religions, Values, and Peak-Experiences (1964)
Ken Wilber, Integral Psychology: Consciousness, Spirit, Psychology, Therapy (2000)
Francisco Varela, Evan Thompson, and Eleanor Rosch, The Embodied Mind (1991)
Pashaura Singh, The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority (2000)
Nikky-Guninder Kaur Singh, The Feminine Principle in the Sikh Vision of the Transcendent (1993)
W. H. McLeod, Sikhism (1997)
Jon Kabat-Zinn, Full Catastrophe Living (1990)

lessons.title: Introduction: Toward a Sikh Psychology
lessons.summary: Frames the project of developing a Sikh psychology in dialogue with contemporary psychological science.

lessons.summary: Examines the five vikars as a systematic psychological analysis of ego-driven mental states.

lessons.summary: Examines ਸਿਮਰਨ as a psychological practice and analyzes its mechanisms of transformation.

lessons.title: ਸਹਜ: The Psychology of Equanimity and Non-Reactive Awareness
lessons.summary: Examines ਸਹਜ as the psychological achievement of contemplative transformation.

lessons.title: Emotions in Gurmat Psychology: Beyond Suppression and Expression
lessons.summary: Examines the Gurmat approach to emotions as a middle path between suppression and unmoderated expression.

lessons.title: States of Consciousness in the SGGS: The ਅਵਸਥਾ Framework
lessons.summary: Examines the SGGS's account of progressive states of consciousness in contemplative development.

lessons.title: Transpersonal Psychology and Gurmat: Maslow, Wilber, and Beyond
lessons.summary: Engages Gurmat psychology with the transpersonal psychology tradition.

lessons.title: Contemplative Neuroscience and Gurmat Practice
lessons.summary: Examines what contemplative neuroscience reveals about the neural dimensions of Sikh contemplative practice.

lessons.title: Neuroplasticity and the Transformation of Character through ਸਿਮਰਨ
lessons.summary: Examines the neuroscientific account of character transformation through sustained contemplative practice.

lessons.title: Synthesis: An Integrated Sikh Psychology
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the course into a comprehensive integrated Sikh psychology.

courses.title: Trauma, Healing, and Spiritual Recovery in Sikh Thought
courses.source: SGGS; trauma studies; Peter Levine, Waking the Tiger; Sikh pastoral care
courses.summary: This graduate seminar examines trauma, its somatic and psychological dimensions, and the resources of Sikh thought and practice for healing and recovery. Drawing on the SGGS, contemporary trauma theory including Herman and van der Kolk, and Sikh pastoral care traditions, students develop an integrative framework for understanding how spiritual practice intersects with the healing of deep psychological wounds.
outcomes: Articulate the major theoretical frameworks for understanding trauma and its psychological and somatic effects
Analyze the resources of Sikh theology and practice for understanding and addressing traumatic suffering
Critically evaluate the role of community, ritual, and contemplative practice in trauma recovery
Apply Gurmat frameworks to the specific traumas of Sikh history, including martyrdom and collective violence
Develop evidence-based approaches to integrating Sikh spiritual resources with trauma-informed clinical care
references: Peter A. Levine, Waking the Tiger: Healing Trauma (1997)
Bessel van der Kolk, The Body Keeps the Score (2014)
Judith Herman, Trauma and Recovery (1992)
Louis Fenech, Martyrdom in the Sikh Tradition (2000)
Pashaura Singh and Louis Fenech, eds., The Oxford Handbook of Sikh Studies (2014)

Nikky-Guninder Kaur Singh, The Feminine Principle in the Sikh Vision of the Transcendent (1993)
Richard Tedeschi and Lawrence Calhoun, Trauma and Transformation (1995)

lessons.title: Introduction: Trauma, Suffering, and the Question of Healing
lessons.summary: Introduces trauma theory, the Gurmat understanding of suffering, and frames the course's integrative approach.

lessons.title: Contemporary Trauma Theory: Herman, van der Kolk, and Levine
lessons.summary: Surveys the major frameworks of contemporary trauma theory, including Herman's stages model, van der Kolk's somatic account, and Levine's Somatic Experiencing.

lessons.summary: Examines the SGGS's engagement with suffering, including its causes, spiritual meaning, and the path from suffering to liberation.

lessons.summary: Examines the therapeutic functions of Sikh ritual and prayer, including the role of narrative in trauma processing.

lessons.title: ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ: Resilience and Post-Traumatic Growth
lessons.summary: Examines ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ as a framework for resilience and post-traumatic growth, and its social ethics of collective resistance.

lessons.title: ਸ਼ਹੀਦੀ, Martyrdom Theology, and Traumatic Loss
lessons.summary: Examines the Sikh theology of martyrdom as a resource for understanding and processing catastrophic loss.

lessons.title: Pastoral Care and Trauma-Informed Ministry in Sikh Communities
lessons.summary: Develops practical frameworks for trauma-informed pastoral care in Sikh communities, integrating clinical and theological perspectives.

lessons.title: Synthesis: An Integrated Framework for Sikh-Grounded Trauma Healing
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the course's threads into a coherent framework for trauma-informed, Sikh-grounded healing.

courses.title: Sikh Perspectives on Mental Illness and Social Stigma
courses.source: SGGS; medical anthropology; Bhugra & Bhui; Fernando; Corrigan & Watson
courses.summary: This graduate seminar examines mental illness stigma from sociological, anthropological, and Sikh theological perspectives. It investigates how stigma operates at multiple levels — individual, community, structural — and how Gurmat anthropology and ethics challenge stigmatizing frameworks. Students develop capacities for scholarly analysis, community advocacy, and the design of culturally grounded destigmatization programs for Sikh communities.
outcomes: Analyze the major theoretical frameworks for understanding mental illness stigma across cultural contexts
Apply Gurmat anthropological concepts to critique stigmatizing attitudes toward mental illness
Examine how gender, immigration, and diaspora experience intersect with mental illness stigma in Sikh communities
Design evidence-based, culturally grounded destigmatization programs for Sikh communities
Evaluate the role of the gurdwara and Sikh community institutions in addressing mental health stigma

lessons.title: ਸੇਵਾ as Compassionate Care: The Ethics of Mental Health Ministry
lessons.summary: Develops a Gurmat ethics of compassionate care for those with mental illness, grounded in ਸੇਵਾ.

lessons.title: Community-Based Destigmatization: Programs and Strategies
lessons.summary: Examines evidence-based community destigmatization programs and their adaptation for Sikh community contexts.

lessons.title: Synthesis: Toward a Sikh Model of Mental Health Inclusion
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the course's themes into a comprehensive Gurmat framework for mental health inclusion in Sikh communities.

courses.title: Contemplative Practice, Neuroscience, and Gurmat
courses.source: SGGS; Davidson & Begley; Lutz et al.; Varela, Thompson & Rosch; Wallace
courses.summary: This graduate seminar examines the emerging field of contemplative neuroscience and its relevance to the Gurmat understanding of mind, practice, and transformation. Drawing on first-person phenomenological accounts of Sikh contemplative states, and on the neuroscience of attention, emotion regulation, and consciousness, students develop an integrative, critically sophisticated framework for understanding what happens in the mind and brain during the practices of ਸਿਮਰਨ and ਕੀਰਤਨ.
outcomes: Articulate the major methodological approaches and findings of contemplative neuroscience
Apply neuroscientific frameworks to the analysis of specific Sikh contemplative practices
Critically evaluate the assumptions and limitations of neuroscientific approaches to spiritual experience
Develop integrative frameworks that honor both first-person phenomenological accounts and third-person neuroscientific data
Analyze the relationships between contemplative states, contemplative traits, and long-term psychological transformation

Antoine Lutz, Lawrence Greischar, Nancy Rawlings, Matthieu Ricard, and Richard Davidson, 'Long-Term Meditators Self-Induce High-Amplitude Gamma Synchrony during Mental Practice,' PNAS 101, no. 46 (2004): 16369-73

lessons.title: Contemplative States and Traits: ਸਹਜ and the Neuroscience of Equanimity
lessons.summary: Examines the distinction between contemplative states and traits, and the neuroscience of equanimity as it relates to ਸਹਜ.

lessons.title: The Embodied Mind: Somatic Dimensions of Sikh Practice
lessons.summary: Examines the embodied dimensions of Sikh contemplative practice and the neuroscience of embodied cognition.

lessons.title: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲਾ, Sleep, and the Neuroscience of Optimal Practice Time
lessons.summary: Examines the neuroscience of circadian rhythms and sleep, and what it suggests about the traditional practice of pre-dawn contemplation.

lessons.title: Synthesis: Toward an Integrative Contemplative Science of the Gurmat Mind
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the course's themes into an integrative framework for the neuroscientific and phenomenological study of Sikh contemplative practice.

courses.title: Advanced Mindfulness and Gurmat: Research and Practice
courses.source: SGGS; Kabat-Zinn; Williams and Teasdale; Segal; Thich Nhat Hanh; Purser
courses.summary: This graduate seminar provides a rigorous scholarly examination of mindfulness research and practice in dialogue with Gurmat contemplative science. Students critically evaluate the mindfulness-based intervention literature, examine the cultural and religious roots of mindfulness, and develop a sophisticated understanding of how Sikh ਸਿਮਰਨ and mindfulness practices converge, diverge, and mutually illuminate each other.
outcomes: Critically evaluate the empirical research literature on mindfulness-based interventions including MBSR and MBCT

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence and Sikh Ethics: An Advanced Seminar

Critically analyze major theoretical frameworks in AI ethics from a Sikh philosophical perspective
