lessons.summary: Examines AI-enabled disinformation and applies the Gurmat imperative of ਸੱਚ to evaluate epistemic harms.

lessons.title: Automation, ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰਨੀ, and the Future of Work
lessons.summary: Applies the Gurmat concept of ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰਨੀ to evaluate the ethical dimensions of AI-driven automation.

lessons.title: AI in Healthcare: ਸੇਵਾ, Consent, and Algorithmic Medicine
lessons.summary: Evaluates AI in healthcare applications using the Gurmat framework of ਸੇਵਾ and the ethics of care.

lessons.title: Autonomous Weapons and the Doctrine of ਧਰਮ ਯੁੱਧ
lessons.summary: Applies the Sikh doctrine of ਧਰਮ ਯੁੱਧ to evaluate the ethics of lethal autonomous weapons systems.

lessons.title: AI Consciousness, Personhood, and the Gurmat Account of ਜੋਤਿ
lessons.summary: Examines philosophical questions about AI consciousness and applies the Gurmat concept of ਜੋਤਿ to questions of AI moral status.

lessons.title: Existential Risk, Humility, and the Limits of Human Engineering
lessons.summary: Examines existential risk from advanced AI through the Gurmat lens of humility and the limits of human wisdom.

lessons.title: AI Governance and ਸੰਗਤ: Democratic Oversight of Transformative Technology
lessons.summary: Applies the Sikh model of ਸੰਗਤ to questions of democratic AI governance and institutional accountability.

lessons.title: Generative AI, Creativity, and the Theology of ਕਰਤਾ ਪੁਰਖੁ
lessons.summary: Examines generative AI and questions of creativity, authorship, and originality from the perspective of Gurmat theology.

lessons.title: Synthesis: A Sikh Framework for Responsible AI
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the course into a coherent Sikh ethical framework for evaluating, developing, and governing AI.

courses.title: Graduate Seminar in Technology Ethics and Gurmat
courses.source: SGGS; Vallor; Zuboff; Postman; Winner; Ellul
courses.summary: This graduate seminar develops a Gurmat framework for evaluating the ethical dimensions of digital and emerging technologies. From the attention economy and social media to biotechnology and environmental technology, students apply Sikh ethical concepts — ਮਾਇਆ, ਹਉਮੈ, ਸੇਵਾ, ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰਨੀ — to assess how technological systems shape human character, community, and spiritual development.
outcomes: Apply Gurmat ethical concepts to evaluate the design and deployment of digital and emerging technologies
Critically analyze the ways in which technological systems shape human character, community, and spiritual development
Develop original Gurmat-grounded positions on contested technology ethics debates
Evaluate the environmental and social justice dimensions of technology from a Sikh perspective
Design technology products and policies consistent with Gurmat ethical principles
references: Shannon Vallor, Technology and the Virtues: A Philosophical Guide to a Future Worth Wanting (2016)
Shoshana Zuboff, The Age of Surveillance Capitalism (2019)
Neil Postman, Technopoly: The Surrender of Culture to Technology (1992)
Langdon Winner, The Whale and the Reactor: A Search for Limits in an Age of High Technology (1986)
Jacques Ellul, The Technological Society (1964)
Kate Crawford, Atlas of AI: Power, Politics, and the Planetary Costs of Artificial Intelligence (2021)
Pashaura Singh and Louis Fenech, eds., The Oxford Handbook of Sikh Studies (2014)
Michael Sandel, The Case against Perfection: Ethics in the Age of Genetic Engineering (2007)

lessons.title: Introduction: Gurmat and the Technological Condition
lessons.summary: Frames the seminar's approach to technology ethics from a Gurmat perspective, introducing key theoretical frameworks.

lessons.title: ਮਾਇਆ and the Attention Economy: Distraction as Design
lessons.summary: Applies the Gurmat concept of ਮਾਇਆ to analyze the attention economy and the designed distraction of digital media.

lessons.title: Social Media, ਹਉਮੈ, and the Performance of Self
lessons.summary: Examines social media's exploitation of ਹਉਮੈ through the performance of curated identity.

lessons.title: Digital ਸੰਗਤ: Authentic Community in a Networked Age
lessons.summary: Examines the nature of digital community and asks whether online gathering can fulfill the functions of ਸੰਗਤ.

lessons.title: Surveillance Capitalism and the Ethics of Data
lessons.summary: Applies Gurmat ethics of dignity and community to the challenge of mass data surveillance.

lessons.title: ਸੇਵਾ as Design Orientation: Technology That Serves
lessons.summary: Develops the concept of ਸੇਵਾ as an orienting principle for technology design.

lessons.title: Algorithmic ਨਿਆਉ: Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency
lessons.summary: Develops a Gurmat account of algorithmic justice, examining fairness, accountability, and transparency in automated systems.

lessons.title: Platform Economy, ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰਨੀ, and the Ethics of Gig Work
lessons.summary: Applies the Gurmat framework of ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰਨੀ to evaluate the labor practices of platform economy companies.

lessons.title: Biotechnology, Enhancement, and the Gurmat Account of the Human
lessons.summary: Examines genetic engineering, cognitive enhancement, and the ethics of biotechnology from a Gurmat perspective.

lessons.title: Environmental Technology and the Ethics of ਕੁਦਰਤ
lessons.summary: Develops a Gurmat environmental ethics of technology, examining both green technologies and the ecological costs of digital infrastructure.

lessons.title: Digital Sadhana: Technology in Service of Contemplative Life
lessons.summary: Examines how digital technology can be deployed in service of spiritual practice and community rather than as an obstacle to it.

lessons.title: Synthesis: A Gurmat Framework for Technology Design and Governance
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the course into a coherent Gurmat framework for technology design and governance.

courses.title: Sikh Leadership Theory: Seva, Sovereignty, and Transformation
courses.source: SGGS; Greenleaf; Burns; Heifetz; George; Collins
courses.summary: This graduate seminar develops a comprehensive Sikh theory of leadership grounded in the SGGS and the historical example of the Gurus, engaging major frameworks of contemporary leadership scholarship including servant leadership, transformational leadership, adaptive leadership, and authentic leadership. Students develop both scholarly analysis and personal leadership capacity rooted in Gurmat principles.
outcomes: Articulate a comprehensive Sikh theory of leadership drawing on SGGS theology and the Gurus' historical example
Critically evaluate major contemporary leadership frameworks from a Gurmat perspective
Apply Gurmat leadership concepts to contemporary organizational, community, and political contexts
Analyze the specific leadership contributions of the Guru period and their ongoing relevance
Develop a personal leadership philosophy grounded in Sikh ethical and spiritual principles
references: Robert K. Greenleaf, Servant Leadership: A Journey into the Nature of Legitimate Power and Greatness (1977)
James MacGregor Burns, Leadership (1978)
Ronald Heifetz, Leadership without Easy Answers (1994)
Bill George, Authentic Leadership: Rediscovering the Secrets to Creating Lasting Value (2003)
Jim Collins, Good to Great: Why Some Companies Make the Leap and Others Don't (2001)
Pashaura Singh and Louis Fenech, eds., The Oxford Handbook of Sikh Studies (2014)
W. H. McLeod, Sikhism (1997)
Nikky-Guninder Kaur Singh, The Feminine Principle in the Sikh Vision of the Transcendent (1993)

lessons.title: Introduction: Toward a Sikh Theory of Leadership
lessons.summary: Introduces the seminar's project of developing a comprehensive Sikh theory of leadership in dialogue with contemporary leadership scholarship.

lessons.title: ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ: The Integration of Spiritual and Temporal Authority
lessons.summary: Examines the doctrine of ਮੀਰੀ-ਪੀਰੀ and its implications for a comprehensive theory of Sikh leadership.

lessons.title: ਸੇਵਾ and Servant Leadership: Greenleaf in Gurmat Perspective
lessons.summary: Compares Greenleaf's servant leadership theory with the Gurmat account of ਸੇਵਾ.

lessons.title: Transformational Leadership and Burns: The Gurus as Transformational Leaders
lessons.summary: Applies Burns's transformational leadership framework to the leadership of the Sikh Gurus.

lessons.title: The Gurus as Leaders: Historical Analysis and Leadership Lessons
lessons.summary: Provides a systematic analysis of leadership themes across the Guru period as a historical leadership case study.

lessons.title: ਸੱਚ and Authentic Leadership: George's Framework in Gurmat Perspective
lessons.summary: Compares Bill George's authentic leadership framework with the Gurmat account of ਸੱਚ as the foundation of leadership.

lessons.title: Adaptive Leadership, ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ, and the Leadership of Crisis
lessons.summary: Applies Heifetz's adaptive leadership framework to Sikh leadership in crisis, illuminated by the concept of ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ.

lessons.title: ਨਿਮਰਤਾ and Humble Leadership: Collins's Level 5 in Gurmat Context
lessons.summary: Examines Jim Collins's Level 5 leadership concept in relationship to the Gurmat account of ਨਿਮਰਤਾ.

lessons.title: ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ as Institution: Democratic and Participatory Leadership
lessons.summary: Examines the Khalsa as a model of democratic, participatory leadership and governance.

lessons.title: Women's Leadership in Sikh History and the SGGS
lessons.summary: Examines women's leadership in Sikh history and the SGGS's theological resources for gender-inclusive leadership.

lessons.title: ਸਰਬੱਤ ਦਾ ਭਲਾ: Leadership for Universal Welfare
lessons.summary: Examines the concept of ਸਰਬੱਤ ਦਾ ਭਲਾ as the ultimate purpose that orients Sikh leadership beyond community interests.

lessons.title: Synthesis: A Sikh Leadership Framework for the Twenty-First Century
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the course's analysis into a comprehensive Sikh leadership framework applicable to contemporary contexts.

courses.title: Critical Thinking and Epistemic Responsibility in the Sikh Tradition
courses.summary: This graduate seminar examines the epistemological foundations of Sikh thought, developing a rigorous account of critical thinking and epistemic responsibility grounded in Gurbani concepts such as ਵਿਚਾਰ, ਸੱਚ, and ਬਿਬੇਕ. Students engage with the SGGS as a sophisticated philosophical text that speaks to contemporary debates about knowledge, bias, and intellectual virtue.
outcomes: Analyze the epistemological framework of the SGGS, identifying its key concepts and their relationships
Compare Sikh epistemic virtues with contemporary virtue epistemology and social epistemology
Apply Sikh concepts of ਵਿਚਾਰ and ਬਿਬੇਕ to the evaluation of knowledge claims in academic and public discourse
Evaluate the epistemological dimensions of contemporary debates within the Sikh community
Develop a personal practice of epistemic responsibility informed by ਗੁਰਮਤਿ and relevant scholarship
references: Baehr, Jason. The Inquiring Mind: On Intellectual Virtues and Virtue Epistemology (2011)
Cassam, Quassim. Vices of the Mind: From the Intellectual to the Political (2019)
Fricker, Miranda. Epistemic Injustice: Power and the Ethics of Knowing (2007)
Goldman, Alvin I. Knowledge in a Social World (1999)
Mandair, Arvind-Pal Singh. Religion and the Specter of the West: Sikhism, India, Postcoloniality (2009)
Pashaura Singh. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority (2000)
Mann, Gurinder Singh. The Goindval Pothis (1996)
Zagzebski, Linda. Virtues of the Mind (1996)

lessons.title: Foundations of Sikh Epistemology: ਸੱਚ and the Nature of Knowledge
lessons.summary: This lesson establishes the epistemological foundations of Sikh thought, examining how the SGGS conceptualizes truth, the sources of valid knowledge, and the relationship between reason and revelation.

lessons.title: ਮਨਮੁਖ and ਗੁਰਮੁਖ: Epistemic Orientations in Sikh Thought
lessons.summary: This lesson analyzes the SGGS's fundamental distinction between ego-centered and Guru-oriented modes of knowing, examining how these orientations function as epistemic frameworks with direct implications for critical thinking.

lessons.title: The Role of ਸੰਗਤ in Collective Epistemic Practice
lessons.summary: This lesson examines how the institution of ਸੰਗਤ functions as a community of epistemic practice, exploring its parallels with contemporary social epistemology and its role in correcting individual cognitive biases.

lessons.title: Critical Inquiry and the Rejection of Superstition in Gurbani
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the SGGS's systematic critique of superstition, ritual formalism, and uncritical tradition-following, analyzing these critiques as expressions of an implicit rationalism within Sikh thought.

lessons.title: ਵਿਚਾਰ as Philosophical Method: Contemplative Reasoning
lessons.summary: This lesson develops a systematic account of ਵਿਚਾਰ as a philosophical method, examining how contemplative reasoning in the Sikh tradition compares to methods of inquiry in Western and South Asian philosophy.

lessons.title: Epistemic Humility: ਹਉਮੈ as the Root of Cognitive Distortion
lessons.summary: A deep analysis of ਹਉਮੈ as an epistemological concept, examining how the Sikh critique of ego maps onto contemporary accounts of cognitive bias, motivated reasoning, and epistemic vice.

lessons.title: Sources of Authority in Sikh Epistemology: Text, Tradition, and Community
lessons.summary: This lesson examines how authority functions in Sikh epistemology, analyzing the relationship between scriptural authority (the SGGS as living Guru), the interpretive tradition, and community consensus.

lessons.title: The Ethics of Belief: Responsibility and Accountability in Knowledge Claims
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the ethical dimensions of belief formation and expression, drawing on both Western philosophical accounts of epistemic duty and Sikh concepts of accountability to community and the Divine.

lessons.title: Logic, Rhetoric, and Argumentation in the Sikh Philosophical Canon
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the forms of logic, rhetoric, and argumentation deployed in the SGGS and in the broader Sikh philosophical tradition, comparing them with classical Indian and Western logical traditions.

lessons.title: Critical Thinking as Spiritual Practice: ਜਿਗਿਆਸਾ and the Seeking Mind
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the Sikh concept of ਜਿਗਿਆਸਾ (spiritual inquiry) as a form of critical thinking, arguing that the seeking mind is both a spiritual and an intellectual ideal in the Sikh tradition.

lessons.title: Misinformation, Propaganda, and ਸੱਚ in Contemporary Sikh Discourse
lessons.summary: This lesson applies the course's epistemological framework to contemporary challenges facing the Sikh community: the spread of misinformation, the manipulation of information for political purposes, and the maintenance of epistemic integrity in digital environments.

lessons.title: Integrating Sikh Epistemic Virtues in Graduate Research Practice
lessons.summary: The final lesson synthesizes the course's theoretical insights with practical guidance for graduate research, showing how Sikh epistemic virtues can inform and improve scholarly practice across disciplines.

courses.title: Digital Humanities and Sikh Studies
courses.source: Digital humanities methodology; Sikh archive scholarship
courses.summary: This graduate seminar examines the application of digital humanities methods—computational text analysis, geospatial mapping, network analysis, digital archiving—to Sikh Studies, while maintaining critical awareness of the epistemological and ethical dimensions of these methods. Students develop both technical competence and the critical framework needed to evaluate and contribute to digital Sikh scholarship.
outcomes: Evaluate major digital Sikh Studies projects for their methodological rigor and ethical grounding
Apply computational text analysis tools to the SGGS and Sikh historical texts with appropriate critical awareness
Design a digital humanities project addressing a research question in Sikh Studies
Analyze the politics of digitization in Sikh contexts using postcolonial and critical race frameworks
Develop practical skills in text encoding, database design, or digital archiving relevant to Sikh materials
references: Burton, Antoinette, ed. Archive Stories: Facts, Fictions, and the Writing of History (2005)
Gold, Matthew K., and Lauren F. Klein, eds. Debates in the Digital Humanities (2012, 2016)
Mann, Gurinder Singh. The Making of Sikh Scripture (2001)
Pashaura Singh. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority (2000)
Risam, Roopika. New Digital Worlds: Postcolonial Digital Humanities in Theory, Praxis, and Pedagogy (2018)
Schreibman, Susan, Ray Siemens, and John Unsworth, eds. A Companion to Digital Humanities (2004)
Carroll, Stephanie Russo, et al. The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance. Data Science Journal (2020)
Mandair, Arvind-Pal Singh. Religion and the Specter of the West (2009)

lessons.title: Digital Humanities and the Study of Sikh Texts: An Introduction
lessons.summary: This lesson introduces digital humanities methodologies and their application to Sikh Studies, examining the theoretical assumptions underlying computational approaches to sacred and historical texts.

lessons.title: History and Criticism of Digital Humanities Methodology
lessons.summary: A critical survey of digital humanities as a field, examining its methodological assumptions, internal debates, and the specific challenges it faces when applied to non-Western textual traditions.

lessons.title: Digitizing the ਸ਼੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ: Projects, Standards, and Challenges
lessons.summary: A detailed examination of the major projects digitizing the SGGS, evaluating their methodological choices, standards compliance, and theological implications.

lessons.title: Computational Linguistics and Gurmukhi Script
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the computational linguistic analysis of Gurmukhi script and Punjabi language, surveying available NLP tools, corpus resources, and their applications in Sikh textual research.

lessons.title: Text Encoding and TEI for Sikh Manuscripts
lessons.summary: This lesson provides a technical introduction to the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI) and its application to Sikh manuscripts, examining how XML-based encoding can represent the complex features of Sikh textual materials.

lessons.title: Database Architecture for Sikh Historical Collections
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the design and implementation of database systems for Sikh historical collections, covering relational and linked data approaches, metadata standards, and the challenges of representing complex historical materials.

lessons.title: Geospatial Humanities: Mapping Sikh History
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the application of geographic information systems (GIS) and spatial analysis to Sikh historical research, exploring how maps and spatial visualization can illuminate patterns in Sikh history and culture.

lessons.title: Network Analysis in Sikh Historical Research
lessons.summary: This lesson introduces network analysis methods and their application to Sikh historical research, examining social networks of scholars, political networks of Sikh institutions, and textual networks of intertextual connection.

lessons.title: Oral History, Audio Archives, and Sikh Kirtan Digitization
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the special challenges of digitizing oral and audio materials in Sikh Studies, covering oral history methodology, audio archive standards, and the specific challenges of kirtan digitization.

lessons.title: Critical Race and Postcolonial Approaches to Digital Sikh Archives
lessons.summary: This lesson applies critical race theory and postcolonial critique to the digital Sikh archive, examining how colonial categories and racial hierarchies have shaped the digitization of Sikh materials and how these can be challenged.

lessons.title: Community-Based Digital Humanities in the Sikh Diaspora
lessons.summary: This lesson examines community-based digital humanities projects in the Sikh diaspora, exploring how diaspora communities use digital tools to maintain cultural connections, preserve local histories, and navigate identity formation.

lessons.title: Ethics, Sustainability, and the Future of Digital Sikh Studies
lessons.summary: The final lesson addresses the ethical dimensions of digital humanities work in Sikh Studies and looks toward the future, identifying emerging technologies and research directions that will shape the field.

courses.title: Advanced Raag Studies: Theory, History, and Sikh Kirtan
courses.source: SGGS raag system; classical Indian music theory; Sikh kirtan tradition
courses.summary: This graduate seminar provides advanced study of the raag system as it operates in the SGGS and in the Sikh kirtan tradition, combining classical Indian music theory with musicological analysis, historical study, and critical engagement with the Gurmat Sangeet reform movement. Students develop sophisticated analytical tools for scholarly engagement with Sikh musical practice.
outcomes: Analyze any of the thirty-one SGGS raags according to classical music theory categories including aroha, avaroha, vadi, samvadi, and pakad
Explain the theological significance of the raag framework in the SGGS and its implications for kirtan performance
Critically evaluate the claims of the Gurmat Sangeet movement using both musicological and historical evidence
Apply rasa theory to the analysis of Sikh kirtan performance
Identify current research frontiers in Sikh raag studies and formulate an original research question
references: Gurnam Singh. Gurmat Sangeet. Punjab University (1995)
Kaufmann, Walter. The Ragas of North India. Indiana University Press (1968)
Mann, Gurinder Singh. The Making of Sikh Scripture. Oxford University Press (2001)
Nijhawan, Michael. Dhadi Darbar: Religion, Violence, and the Performance of Sikh History. Oxford University Press (2006)
Pashaura Singh. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority. Oxford University Press (2000)
Tara Singh. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji de Raag. Akal Purakh ki Fauj (1977)
Sharma, Manorma. Musical Heritage of India. APH Publishing (2007)

lessons.title: Foundations of Raag Theory and the SGGS Organizational Structure
lessons.summary: This lesson establishes the foundational principles of classical Indian raag theory and examines how the SGGS deploys the raag system as its organizational framework, with implications for both theology and musicology.

lessons.title: The Historical Development of Raag in Classical Indian Music
lessons.summary: A survey of the historical development of the raag system from ancient Indian music theory through the medieval period to its form at the time of the Sikh Gurus.

lessons.title: Grammar of Raag: Aroha, Avaroha, Vadi, Samvadi, and Pakad
lessons.summary: A technical analysis of the grammatical elements that define a raag, with examples drawn from raags found in the SGGS, equipping students for advanced musicological analysis.

lessons.title: The Thirty-One Raags of the SGGS: Survey and Classification
lessons.summary: A comprehensive survey of all thirty-one raags in the SGGS, examining their classification, characteristic features, and the nature and size of their respective sections in the scripture.

lessons.title: Time Theory (Prahar) and the SGGS: Sacred Time in Musical Performance
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the classical Indian theory of time in music (the prahar system) and its application to SGGS raags, exploring the theological significance of performing specific raags at specific times.

lessons.title: Raag and Rasa: Emotional Content in Sikh Kirtan Performance
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the classical Indian theory of rasa (aesthetic emotion) and its application to kirtan performance, analyzing how the emotional content of raags interacts with the theological content of SGGS compositions.

lessons.title: Dhrupad, Khayal, and the Sikh Kirtan Tradition
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the relationship between the major classical North Indian vocal genres (dhrupad, khayal) and the Sikh kirtan tradition, analyzing continuities and departures.

lessons.title: Taal Systems in Gurbani Kirtan: Rhythm and Meter
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the taal (rhythmic cycle) systems used in Gurbani kirtan, analyzing the complex system of ਘਰ designations in the SGGS and their relationship to classical Indian taal theory.

lessons.title: Regional Kirtan Traditions and Raag Interpretation
lessons.summary: This lesson surveys the major regional kirtan traditions within Sikhism, examining how different traditions have interpreted and performed the same raags and compositions differently.

lessons.title: The Gurmat Sangeet Movement: Historical Background and Contemporary Status
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the Gurmat Sangeet movement — its historical origins, key figures, institutional development, and contemporary status as a force for the reform and standardization of Sikh kirtan practice.

lessons.title: Notation, Transcription, and the Challenge of Representing Raag-Based Music
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the challenges of notating and transcribing raag-based music, surveying existing notation systems for Indian music and their limitations, with specific application to SGGS compositions.

lessons.title: Advanced Seminar: Research Frontiers in Sikh Raag Studies
lessons.summary: The final lesson surveys current research frontiers in Sikh raag studies, identifies methodological challenges, and prepares students for original scholarly contribution to the field.

courses.title: Sikh Musical Manuscripts and Notation Traditions
courses.source: Dr. Kamalroop Singh; Sikh manuscript traditions; musical notation history
courses.summary: This graduate seminar examines Sikh musical manuscripts in major South Asian and European repositories, developing paleographic competence, critically evaluating evidence for musical notation in Sikh manuscripts, and situating Sikh manuscript practice within the broader history of South Asian musical notation. Students engage with the methodological and ethical dimensions of manuscript scholarship.
outcomes: Read and analyze historical Gurmukhi manuscript scripts using foundational paleographic methods
Critically evaluate scholarly claims about musical notation in Sikh manuscripts
Survey the major Sikh manuscript repositories and the scholarly literature on their collections
Apply textual critical methods to the analysis of variant readings in SGGS manuscripts
Assess the ethical and practical dimensions of manuscript access, conservation, and digitization
references: Kamalroop Singh and Gurinder Singh Mann. Prem Sumarag: The Eighteenth Century Sikh Code of Conduct (2006)
Mann, Gurinder Singh. The Goindval Pothis: The Earliest Extant Source of the Sikh Canon (1996)
Mann, Gurinder Singh. The Making of Sikh Scripture (2001)
Pashaura Singh. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority (2000)
Pashaura Singh. The Bhagats of the Guru Granth Sahib (2003)
Gurnam Singh. Gurmat Sangeet. Punjab University (1995)
Tara Singh. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji de Raag (1977)

lessons.title: Introduction to Sikh Musical Manuscripts: Scope, Significance, and Methodology
lessons.summary: This lesson introduces the field of Sikh musical manuscript studies, surveying the major collections, establishing the scholarly significance of manuscript evidence, and outlining methodological approaches.

lessons.title: Paleography of Gurmukhi Script: Historical Development and Variant Forms
lessons.summary: A technical introduction to the historical development of Gurmukhi script, with attention to the variant forms found in early Sikh manuscripts and their implications for dating and interpretation.

lessons.title: The Pothis and Early Manuscript Traditions
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the early Sikh manuscript tradition, focusing on the Goindval Pothis and related early compilations that precede the canonical Kartarpur Bir.

lessons.title: Musical Notation Systems in South Asian Manuscripts
lessons.summary: A survey of musical notation systems used in South Asian manuscripts from antiquity through the medieval period, providing comparative context for the analysis of potential notation in Sikh manuscripts.

lessons.title: The Kartarpur Bir and the Canonical Manuscript Tradition
lessons.summary: This lesson focuses on the Kartarpur Bir — traditionally regarded as the manuscript compiled under the direct supervision of Guru Arjan Dev Ji — examining its physical characteristics, organization, and significance for Sikh musical studies.

lessons.title: Sikh Musical Manuscripts in European and British Collections
lessons.summary: This lesson surveys Sikh musical manuscripts held in European and British collections, examining how they came to be there and what they reveal about Sikh musical culture.

lessons.title: Raag Notation and Performance Instruction in Manuscript Sources
lessons.summary: A detailed examination of evidence for musical notation and performance instruction in Sikh manuscript sources, critically assessing competing scholarly interpretations.

lessons.title: The ਰਾਗਮਾਲਾ Controversy: Manuscript Evidence and Scholarly Debate
lessons.summary: An examination of the ongoing scholarly and community debate about the ਰਾਗਮਾਲਾ — the final composition in the SGGS — using manuscript evidence as a primary analytical tool.

lessons.title: Manuscript Evidence for Taal and Rhythmic Practice
lessons.summary: This lesson examines manuscript evidence for the taal and rhythmic practices of historical Sikh kirtan, including the significance of ਘਰ designations and any other rhythmic indicators found in manuscripts.

lessons.title: Illustrated Sikh Manuscripts: Visual Dimensions of Musical Culture
lessons.summary: This lesson examines illustrated Sikh manuscripts, exploring what visual representations of musical performance and instruments can tell us about historical Sikh musical culture.

lessons.title: Digital Approaches to Sikh Musical Manuscript Analysis
lessons.summary: This lesson examines how digital technologies — from high-resolution imaging to computational analysis — are transforming the study of Sikh musical manuscripts.

lessons.title: Conservation, Access, and Ethical Issues in Sikh Manuscript Studies
lessons.summary: The final lesson addresses the ethical, practical, and political dimensions of Sikh manuscript studies, covering conservation, access, intellectual property, and the responsibilities of manuscript scholars.

courses.title: Performance Practice in Gurbani Kirtan: Graduate Seminar
courses.source: SGGS taal and raag; Sikh kirtan scholarship; performance studies
courses.summary: This graduate seminar examines the theory and practice of Sikh kirtan as a performance tradition, analyzing the relationship between musical structure, theological intention, and devotional experience. Drawing on ethnomusicology, performance studies, and Sikh theology, students develop sophisticated frameworks for understanding and evaluating kirtan performance.
outcomes: Apply performance practice scholarship to the analysis of Sikh kirtan recordings and live performances
Analyze the theological dimensions of specific performance choices in kirtan
Critically evaluate the harmonium debate and related controversies using historical and musicological evidence
Examine the call-and-response structure of kirtan as a theological and sociological phenomenon
Assess the challenges and opportunities of kirtan transmission in diaspora contexts
references: Gurnam Singh. Gurmat Sangeet. Punjab University (1995)
Nijhawan, Michael. Dhadi Darbar: Religion, Violence, and the Performance of Sikh History (2006)
Pashaura Singh. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority (2000)
Taruskin, Richard. Text and Act: Essays on Music and Performance (1995)
Tara Singh. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji de Raag (1977)
Merleau-Ponty, Maurice. Phenomenology of Perception (1945/2012)
Mann, Gurinder Singh. The Making of Sikh Scripture (2001)

lessons.title: Toward a Theory of Sikh Kirtan Performance Practice
lessons.summary: This lesson establishes the theoretical foundations for studying Sikh kirtan as a performance practice, drawing on ethnomusicology, music phenomenology, and the SGGS's own account of musical worship.

lessons.title: The Sonic Theology of Gurbani: Music, Word, and Divinity
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the theology of sound and music in the SGGS, analyzing how the Gurus understood the relationship between music, sacred language, and divine presence.

lessons.title: Pre-Performance Preparation: ਅਭਿਆਸ, ਮਨ ਦੀ ਤਿਆਰੀ, and Devotional Readiness
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the pre-performance practices of Sikh kirtan performers, analyzing how physical, mental, and devotional preparation shapes the quality of kirtan.

lessons.title: The Alaap: Establishing Raag Identity and Devotional Space
lessons.summary: A detailed analysis of the alaap (introductory melodic improvisation) in kirtan performance, examining how it functions to establish raag identity, create devotional atmosphere, and prepare the congregation for the ਸ਼ਬਦ.

lessons.title: Text Setting in Gurbani: Prosody, Melody, and Meaning
lessons.summary: This lesson examines how Gurbani texts are set to music in kirtan performance, analyzing the relationship between the prosodic structure of Punjabi/Braj Bhasha verse and the melodic frameworks of classical raags.

lessons.title: Call and Response in Sikh Kirtan: Congregation and Ragi
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the call-and-response structure of kirtan, analyzing how the relationship between the ਰਾਗੀ and the ਸੰਗਤ structures the devotional experience.

lessons.title: Improvisation and Constraint: The Raag Framework as Creative Space
lessons.summary: This lesson analyzes the relationship between the constraint of the raag framework and the freedom of improvisation in kirtan performance, developing a theoretical account of musical creativity within tradition.

lessons.title: Instrumental Practice: Taus, Dilruba, Sarangi, and Tabla in Kirtan
lessons.summary: A detailed examination of the historical and contemporary use of specific instruments in Sikh kirtan, with attention to their tonal characteristics, historical associations, and roles in the kirtan ensemble.

lessons.title: The Harmonium Question: Historical Context and Contemporary Debate
lessons.summary: A focused analysis of the harmonium's introduction into Sikh kirtan, the debate about its appropriateness, and what this debate reveals about authenticity, change, and tradition in living musical cultures.

lessons.title: The Listening Body: Reception, Affect, and Transformation in Kirtan
lessons.summary: This lesson examines kirtan reception from the perspective of the listener, analyzing the somatic, emotional, and spiritual dimensions of the kirtan experience.

lessons.title: Kirtan in the Diaspora: Adaptation, Innovation, and Identity
lessons.summary: This lesson examines how kirtan practice has evolved in diaspora contexts, analyzing adaptations, innovations, and the role of kirtan in Sikh diaspora identity formation.

lessons.title: Pedagogical Traditions: The Guru-Shishya Relationship in Kirtan Education
lessons.summary: The final lesson examines how kirtan is taught and transmitted, analyzing the guru-shishya (teacher-student) relationship as a pedagogical institution and its implications for the preservation and evolution of performance traditions.

courses.title: Comparative South Asian Music Theory and Gurbani
courses.source: Indian classical music; SGGS; comparative musicology
courses.summary: This graduate seminar situates the musical traditions of the SGGS within the broader landscape of South Asian and global music, applying comparative musicological methods to analyze the raag system, taal structures, and text-music relationships in Sikh kirtan against the Hindustani, Carnatic, Sufi, and bhakti musical traditions that shaped its development.
outcomes: Compare the raag system of the SGGS with Hindustani, Carnatic, and Sufi modal systems using rigorous musicological methods
Analyze the bhakti and Sufi musical influences on the SGGS's compositional tradition
Apply comparative methods to taal and rhythmic analysis across South Asian and global traditions
Evaluate the evidence for and against musical universals with reference to Sikh kirtan
Develop an original comparative analysis of a specific aspect of Sikh music in cross-cultural perspective
references: Gurnam Singh. Gurmat Sangeet. Punjab University (1995)
Kaufmann, Walter. The Ragas of North India. Indiana University Press (1968)
Nettl, Bruno. The Study of Ethnomusicology: Thirty-One Issues and Concepts (2005)
Nijhawan, Michael. Dhadi Darbar: Religion, Violence, and the Performance of Sikh History (2006)
Pashaura Singh. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority (2000)
Qureshi, Regula Burkhard. Sufi Music of India and Pakistan (1986)
Mehr, Samuel A., et al. Universality and Diversity in Human Song. Science (2019)
Sharma, Manorma. Musical Heritage of India. APH Publishing (2007)

lessons.title: Comparative Musicology and Sikh Music: Frameworks and Debates
lessons.summary: This lesson introduces comparative musicology as a framework for studying Sikh music, establishing the theoretical basis for cross-cultural musical analysis.

lessons.title: The Hindustani Classical System: Theoretical Foundations for Comparison
lessons.summary: A systematic overview of Hindustani classical music theory as the primary comparative framework for analyzing SGGS raags.

lessons.title: Carnatic Music Theory and Its Relationship to SGGS Raags
lessons.summary: An examination of South Indian (Carnatic) music theory and whether any SGGS raags show Carnatic influences or parallels.

lessons.title: Persian and Sufi Musical Influences in the SGGS
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the Persian and Sufi musical influences visible in the SGGS, analyzing how the Gurus engaged with and transformed these musical traditions.

lessons.title: Bhakti Music Traditions and Gurbani: Convergence and Divergence
lessons.summary: A comparative analysis of Sikh kirtan and the broader Hindu bhakti music tradition, examining shared features and distinctive Sikh theological and musical departures.

lessons.title: Folk and Regional Traditions in Sikh Musical Culture
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the role of Punjabi folk and regional musical traditions in shaping Sikh kirtan, analyzing the complex relationship between classical and popular musical cultures.

lessons.title: Cross-Cultural Analysis: Sikh Music and Global Devotional Traditions
lessons.summary: This lesson broadens the comparative frame to examine Sikh kirtan in the context of global devotional music traditions, from Christian chant to Sufi qawwali to West African religious music.

lessons.title: Modal Theory Across Traditions: Maqam, Mode, and Raag
lessons.summary: A focused comparative analysis of three major modal systems — the Islamic maqam, the Western ecclesiastical mode, and the Indian raag — examining structural parallels and theoretical divergences.

lessons.title: Rhythmic Systems: Indian Taal, Arabic Iqa, and Western Meter
lessons.summary: A comparative analysis of the Indian taal system, the Arabic rhythmic pattern (iqa) system, and Western metric theory, with reference to their application in devotional music contexts.

lessons.title: Text-Music Relationships in Comparative Perspective
lessons.summary: A comparative examination of how different traditions relate sacred texts to musical settings, with particular attention to the unique theological framework of text-music relationship in the SGGS.

lessons.title: The Question of Musical Universals: Cross-Cultural Perspectives
lessons.summary: This lesson engages the controversial question of musical universals — features of music that appear across all human cultures — with reference to Sikh music as evidence in this debate.

lessons.title: Synthesis: Toward a Comparative Theory of Sikh Music
lessons.summary: The final lesson synthesizes the course's comparative analyses into a theoretical framework for understanding Sikh music in cross-cultural perspective, with attention to research frontiers and open questions.

courses.title: Historical Evolution of Sikh Kirtan Traditions
courses.source: Kavi Santokh Singh, Suraj Prakash; Sikh kirtan historical sources
courses.summary: This graduate seminar traces the historical development of Sikh kirtan from Guru Nanak Dev Ji's founding musical ministry through the colonial reform period, the establishment of the SGPC, and the transformations of the global diaspora era. Using the Suraj Prakash and related historical sources alongside modern scholarship, students develop critical frameworks for understanding Sikh kirtan as a living, historically dynamic tradition.
outcomes: Critically analyze primary literary sources (Suraj Prakash, Bhai Gurdas Vars, Gurbilas texts) as evidence for historical kirtan practice
Trace the development of the Rababi tradition and analyze the significance of its loss after 1947
Explain the Singh Sabha movement's impact on Sikh kirtan and the emergence of Gurmat Sangeet
Analyze how diaspora conditions have transformed kirtan practice in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries
Develop an original historical argument about a specific period or aspect of Sikh kirtan history
references: Kavi Santokh Singh. Srī Gur Pratāp Sūraj Granth. Completed 1844. Ed. Bhai Vir Singh. Khalsa Samachar (1961)
Gurnam Singh. Gurmat Sangeet. Punjab University (1995)
Mandair, Arvind-Pal Singh. Religion and the Specter of the West (2009)
Mann, Gurinder Singh. The Making of Sikh Scripture (2001)
Nijhawan, Michael. Dhadi Darbar: Religion, Violence, and the Performance of Sikh History (2006)
Oberoi, Harjot. The Construction of Religious Boundaries (1994)
Pashaura Singh. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority (2000)
Tara Singh. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji de Raag (1977)

lessons.title: The Historical Study of Sikh Kirtan: Sources, Methods, and Debates
lessons.summary: This lesson establishes the historiographical foundations for studying Sikh kirtan, surveying available sources, methodological challenges, and the major debates in the field.

lessons.title: Guru Nanak Dev Ji and the Founding of the Kirtan Tradition
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the founding of the Sikh kirtan tradition in the ministry of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, analyzing the theological significance of music in his message and practice.

lessons.title: From Guru Angad to Guru Arjan: Institutional Development of Kirtan
lessons.summary: This lesson traces the institutionalization of kirtan from Guru Angad Dev Ji through Guru Arjan Dev Ji, examining how the practice was formalized within the growing Sikh community.

lessons.title: Guru Arjan Dev Ji and the Compilation of the Adi Granth
lessons.summary: A focused examination of Guru Arjan Dev Ji's compilation of the Adi Granth and its implications for the kirtan tradition, analyzing the theological and musical significance of the canonical organization.

lessons.title: The Sixth Guru and the Warrior-Saint: Miri-Piri and Music
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the musical dimensions of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji's ministry, focusing on the development of the dhadi tradition and the relationship between music, martial culture, and Sikh identity.

lessons.title: The Court of the Tenth Guru: Music, Warfare, and Theology
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the musical culture of Guru Gobind Singh Ji's court, analyzing the theological significance of music in the formation of the ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ and the final years of the Guru period.

lessons.title: The Rababi Tradition: Muslim Musicians in Sikh Devotional Practice
lessons.summary: A detailed examination of the ਰਬਾਬੀ tradition — hereditary Muslim musicians who served as the primary kirtan performers at major Sikh centers for generations — and its eventual decline.

lessons.title: Kirtan in the Colonial Period: Reform, Standardization, and Contestation
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the transformation of Sikh kirtan practice during the colonial period, focusing on the tensions between reform movements, popular practice, and colonial influence.

lessons.title: The Singh Sabha Movement and the Transformation of Kirtan Practice
lessons.summary: This lesson focuses on the Singh Sabha movement's impact on kirtan, examining how the late nineteenth and early twentieth century reform movement reshaped Sikh musical practice.

lessons.title: Kirtan in the Twentieth Century: Institutional Development and Innovation
lessons.summary: This lesson surveys the development of kirtan practice through the twentieth century, examining institutional changes, recording technology, and the emergence of new kirtan styles.

lessons.title: The Global Sikh Diaspora and the Transformation of Kirtan
lessons.summary: This lesson examines how the global Sikh diaspora has transformed kirtan practice, with particular attention to the United Kingdom and North America.

lessons.title: Historical Sources for Sikh Kirtan: The Suraj Prakash and Related Texts
lessons.summary: The final lesson examines the major historical sources for the history of Sikh kirtan in detail, developing critical frameworks for reading these sources as evidence of musical practice.

courses.title: Advanced Sikh Child Development and Education Philosophy
courses.source: SGGS; developmental psychology; Sikh educational philosophy
courses.summary: This graduate seminar integrates Sikh educational philosophy with contemporary developmental psychology to develop sophisticated frameworks for understanding Sikh child development. Students engage with the SGGS's theological anthropology, analyze Sikh developmental practices such as ਸੇਵਾ and ਸਿਮਰਨ, and evaluate research on diaspora identity development in Sikh youth.
outcomes: Analyze the theological anthropology of the SGGS as a framework for child development and education
Compare Sikh educational philosophy with major Western developmental theories including Piaget, Vygotsky, and Erikson
Evaluate the developmental function of Sikh practices including ਸੇਵਾ, ਸੰਗਤ participation, and ਸਿਮਰਨ
Apply identity development research to the specific challenges of Sikh diaspora youth
Design a research project addressing an unresolved question in Sikh child development
references: Ainsworth, Mary D. Salter, et al. Patterns of Attachment (1978)
Berry, John W. Immigration, Acculturation, and Adaptation. Applied Psychology (1997)
Bialystok, Ellen. Bilingualism in Development (2001)
Cummins, Jim. Language, Power, and Pedagogy (2000)
Gardner, Howard. Frames of Mind: The Theory of Multiple Intelligences (1983)
Gilligan, Carol. In a Different Voice (1982)
Pashaura Singh. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority (2000)
Vygotsky, Lev S. Mind in Society (1978)
Seligman, Martin E. P. Flourishing (2011)

lessons.title: Foundations of Sikh Educational Philosophy: ਗੁਰਮਤਿ and Child Development
lessons.summary: This lesson establishes the philosophical foundations of Sikh approaches to child development and education, examining how ਗੁਰਮਤਿ conceptualizes the child, the developmental process, and the goals of education.

lessons.title: Developmental Theory in Comparative Perspective: Western and Sikh Frameworks
lessons.summary: A systematic comparison of Western developmental psychology frameworks with Sikh philosophical accounts of human development.

lessons.title: The ਸੰਗਤ as Developmental Environment: Attachment, Community, and Belonging
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the Sikh institution of ਸੰਗਤ as a developmental environment, analyzing how communal participation shapes attachment, identity, and prosocial development in children.

lessons.title: Language, Literacy, and the Gurmukhi Script in Child Development
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the role of Punjabi language and Gurmukhi script literacy in Sikh child development, analyzing the cognitive, cultural, and spiritual dimensions of Gurmukhi literacy acquisition.

lessons.title: Moral Development in Sikh Educational Philosophy
lessons.summary: This lesson examines Sikh educational approaches to moral development, comparing the SGGS's account of virtue with major Western theories of moral development and education.

lessons.title: The Role of ਸੇਵਾ in Child Development: Service as Pedagogy
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the developmental dimensions of ਸੇਵਾ (selfless service) as a pedagogical practice, analyzing how participation in service activities shapes children's prosocial, moral, and spiritual development.

lessons.title: Identity Development in the Sikh Diaspora: The Challenge of Biculturalism
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the specific challenges of Sikh identity development in diaspora contexts, applying acculturation theory and identity development research to the experience of Sikh youth.

lessons.title: ਸਿਮਰਨ and Contemplative Practices in Childhood
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the developmental implications of ਸਿਮਰਨ (contemplative remembrance) and other Sikh contemplative practices for children, drawing on both traditional Sikh educational philosophy and contemporary research on mindfulness and contemplative education.

lessons.title: Play, Creativity, and the ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ Ideal in Child Education
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the role of play, creativity, and physical education in Sikh child development, relating these to the ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ ideal of the fully developed human being.

lessons.title: Family Structure and Parenting Practices in Sikh Tradition
lessons.summary: This lesson examines Sikh traditional understandings of family structure and parenting, analyzing how these compare with contemporary research on effective parenting and family functioning.

lessons.title: Educational Institutions: Sikh Schools, ਗੁਰਮਤਿ Camps, and ਕੀਰਤਨ Classes
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the range of Sikh educational institutions, analyzing their pedagogical approaches, strengths, and challenges.

lessons.title: Research Frontiers in Sikh Child Development: Integrating Scholarship and Tradition
lessons.summary: The final lesson surveys the current state of research on Sikh child development, identifying gaps, challenges, and opportunities for future scholarly work.

courses.title: Sikh Family Systems Theory: A Graduate Seminar
courses.source: SGGS; family systems theory; Murray Bowen scholarship
courses.summary: This graduate seminar brings Murray Bowen's family systems theory into sustained dialogue with Sikh theology and the SGGS's implicit account of family relationships, developing an integrated framework for understanding Sikh family dynamics. Students engage with concepts including differentiation of self, triangulation, multigenerational transmission, and family resilience (ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ) in both theoretical and applied dimensions.
outcomes: Explain the core concepts of Bowen's family systems theory and evaluate their applicability to Sikh family contexts
Analyze the SGGS's theological anthropology as a resource for understanding family functioning and dysfunction
Apply the concept of differentiation of self to Sikh family dynamics, with attention to cultural specificity
Examine the multigenerational transmission of Sikh values and patterns of family functioning
Develop an integrated Sikh-informed framework for understanding family resilience using ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ and related concepts
references: Bowen, Murray. Family Therapy in Clinical Practice. Jason Aronson (1978)
Kerr, Michael E., and Murray Bowen. Family Evaluation: An Approach Based on Bowen Theory (1988)
McGoldrick, Monica, Betty Carter, and Nydia Garcia-Preto. The Expanded Family Life Cycle (2011)
Pargament, Kenneth I. The Psychology of Religion and Coping (1997)
Pashaura Singh. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority (2000)
Singh, Nikky-Guninder Kaur. The Feminine Principle in the Sikh Vision of the Transcendent (1993)
Walsh, Froma. Strengthening Family Resilience (2006)
Berry, John W. Immigration, Acculturation, and Adaptation. Applied Psychology (1997)

lessons.title: Sikh Family Systems Theory: Foundations and Frameworks
lessons.summary: This lesson establishes the theoretical foundations of the seminar, introducing both Murray Bowen's family systems theory and the Sikh theological framework that will be brought into dialogue throughout the course.

lessons.title: Murray Bowen's Family Systems Theory: Core Concepts and Applications
lessons.summary: A systematic overview of Bowen's major theoretical concepts — differentiation of self, triangulation, the nuclear family emotional system, the multigenerational transmission process, emotional cutoff, and societal emotional process.

lessons.title: Differentiation of Self in the Sikh Family Context
lessons.summary: A detailed analysis of Bowen's concept of differentiation of self and its relationship to Sikh theological concepts of ego (ਹਉਮੈ), identity, and relational health.

lessons.title: Triangulation, Coalitions, and Family Emotional Systems in Sikh Families
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the concept of triangulation — the tendency of two-person emotional systems to draw in a third party when anxiety increases — and analyzes how triangulation patterns manifest in Sikh family contexts.

lessons.title: The Multigenerational Transmission Process in Sikh Family Life
lessons.summary: This lesson examines how patterns of family functioning are transmitted across generations in Sikh families, analyzing both the Bowenian framework and the Sikh concepts of ਸੰਸਕਾਰ and tradition.

lessons.title: Sibling Position and Birth Order in the Sikh Family
lessons.summary: This lesson examines Bowen's account of sibling position as a predictor of functional role in family systems, applying it to Sikh family contexts and critiquing its cultural specificity.

lessons.title: The Nuclear Family Emotional System and Sikh Marriage
lessons.summary: This lesson examines the four patterns of the nuclear family emotional system (marital conflict, dysfunction in a spouse, impairment of one or more children, and emotional distance) in the context of Sikh marriage.

lessons.title: The Extended Family and Community as Emotional Systems
lessons.summary: This lesson extends the analysis of family systems to the extended family and community level, examining how Sikh extended family networks and the ਸੰਗਤ function as emotional systems.

lessons.title: Migration, Diaspora, and the Disruption of Family Systems
lessons.summary: This lesson examines how migration and diaspora experience disrupts established Sikh family systems, creating specific stressors and requiring adaptive responses.

lessons.title: Family Transitions: Marriage, Parenthood, Aging, and Death in Sikh Perspective
lessons.summary: This lesson examines major family life cycle transitions from a Sikh family systems perspective, analyzing how Sikh traditions and rituals support healthy navigation of these transitions.

lessons.title: Sikh Family Resilience: ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ and Family Strength
lessons.summary: This lesson examines Sikh family resilience, analyzing the concept of ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ and other Sikh resilience resources through the lens of family resilience theory.

lessons.title: Integrating Sikh Values and Family Systems Theory: A Graduate Synthesis
lessons.summary: The final lesson synthesizes the seminar's theoretical analyses, develops an integrated framework for understanding Sikh family systems, and identifies directions for future research and practice.

courses.title: Adolescent Identity Formation in Sikh Diaspora Families
courses.source: Sikh diaspora studies; identity formation research; SGGS
courses.summary: This graduate seminar examines the complex processes through which Sikh adolescents in diaspora contexts negotiate identity across religious, cultural, and national lines. Drawing on developmental psychology, diaspora studies, and Gurmat principles, students analyze how families transmit heritage while navigating majority-culture pressures. The course integrates empirical research with theological reflection on selfhood and community.
outcomes: Critically analyze major theoretical frameworks for adolescent identity formation as applied to Sikh diaspora contexts
Evaluate the role of Gurmat principles—particularly the concept of ਨਾਮ and ਸੰਗਤ—in shaping adolescent selfhood
Synthesize empirical research on Sikh youth in the UK, Canada, USA, and Australia
Assess the tensions between heritage maintenance and acculturation in Sikh families
Design research-informed interventions to support healthy identity development in Sikh adolescent populations
references: Ajrouch, Kristine J., and Abdi Kusow. 'Racial and Religious Contexts: Situational Identities among Lebanese and Somali Muslim Immigrants.' Ethnic and Racial Studies 30, no. 1 (2007): 72–94.

Tatla, Darshan Singh. The Sikh Diaspora: The Search for Statehood. London: UCL Press, 1999.

lessons.title: Theoretical Foundations: Identity Formation in Adolescence
lessons.summary: Surveys major developmental psychology frameworks for adolescent identity formation and introduces Gurmat anthropology as a necessary theoretical complement.

lessons.title: The Sikh Diaspora: Historical and Demographic Overview
lessons.summary: Provides the historical and demographic context of Sikh diaspora communities across the UK, Canada, USA, and Australia, analyzing different migration waves and their identity implications.

lessons.title: Gurmat Anthropology and the Sikh Self
lessons.summary: Examines the Gurmat account of selfhood, analyzing how the concepts of ਹਉਮੈ, ਨਾਮ, and ਸੰਗਤ frame human development differently from Western psychological models.

lessons.title: Family Transmission of Sikh Identity
lessons.summary: Examines how Sikh families transmit religious and cultural identity across generations, analyzing both formal practices and informal everyday transmission mechanisms.

lessons.title: Peer Relations and Bicultural Navigation
lessons.summary: Analyzes how Sikh adolescents navigate relationships between heritage Sikh identity and mainstream peer-group culture, examining acculturation strategies and their outcomes.

lessons.title: Gender, Identity, and Sikh Adolescence
lessons.summary: Examines gendered dimensions of Sikh adolescent identity, including the differential experiences of young men and women regarding visible markers, marriage expectations, and spiritual formation.

lessons.title: The ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ Ceremony as Developmental Threshold
lessons.summary: Analyzes the Khalsa initiation ceremony as a developmental and theological threshold in adolescent identity formation, examining its timing, preparation, and psychological significance.

lessons.title: Gurdwara, ਸੰਗਤ, and Community Identity
lessons.summary: Examines the Gurdwara as a total community institution in diaspora contexts and analyzes the role of ਸੰਗਤ in adolescent identity formation and belonging.

lessons.title: Digital Media and Sikh Youth Identity
lessons.summary: Analyzes the role of social media, digital content, and online communities in shaping Sikh adolescent identity, examining both opportunities and risks.

lessons.title: Mental Health, Belonging, and Identity Coherence
lessons.summary: Examines the relationship between identity coherence, community belonging, and mental health outcomes for Sikh diaspora adolescents, with attention to discrimination-related stress.

lessons.title: Sikh Education and Identity Reinforcement
lessons.summary: Examines formal and informal Sikh educational institutions—from Gurdwara classes to dedicated Sikh schools—and their role in adolescent identity formation.

lessons.title: Synthesis: Toward a Gurmat-Informed Identity Development Framework
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the course's theoretical, empirical, and theological threads into a coherent framework for understanding and supporting Sikh adolescent identity formation in diaspora contexts.

courses.title: Cross-Cultural Sikh Parenting: Research and Practice
courses.source: Cross-cultural parenting research; Sikh family values; SGGS
courses.summary: This graduate seminar investigates parenting practices and philosophies within Sikh families across diverse cultural contexts, drawing on comparative developmental research, Gurmat family values, and empirical studies of Sikh communities in South Asia and the diaspora. Students examine how Gurmat principles of seva, sach, and sangat shape parental behavior and child outcomes.
outcomes: Critically evaluate cross-cultural parenting research methodologies and their applicability to Sikh family contexts
Analyze Gurmat principles—particularly ਸੇਵਾ, ਸੱਚ, and ਸੰਗਤ—as foundations of Sikh parenting philosophy
Assess empirical evidence on parenting styles and their outcomes within Sikh diaspora families
Evaluate the intersection of Punjabi cultural norms and Gurmat values in contemporary Sikh parenting
Design research-based parenting education programs grounded in Gurmat philosophy for diaspora Sikh communities
references: Baumrind, Diana. 'Effects of Authoritative Parental Control on Child Behavior.' Child Development 37, no. 4 (1966): 887–907.

Roopnarine, Jaipaul L., and James E. Johnson, eds. Approaches to Early Childhood Education. 6th ed. Upper Saddle River: Pearson, 2012.
Singh, Nikky-Guninder Kaur. The Feminine Principle in the Sikh Vision of the Transcendent. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1993.

lessons.title: Frameworks for Cross-Cultural Parenting Research
lessons.summary: Critically examines Western parenting research frameworks and their cross-cultural limitations, introducing Gurmat parental ethnotheory as a distinctive alternative.

lessons.title: Gurmat Philosophy of the Family and Child
lessons.summary: Analyzes the Gurmat theological model of the family, the child as divine being, and the parent's spiritual responsibility for transmission of ਨਾਮ practice.

lessons.title: Parenting Styles in Cross-Cultural Perspective
lessons.summary: Applies and critiques major parenting styles frameworks in cross-cultural Sikh family contexts, examining how Gurmat values shape parental authority and warmth.

lessons.title: Values Transmission: ਸੱਚ, ਸੇਵਾ, and ਧਰਮ
lessons.summary: Examines how Sikh parents transmit core Gurmat values to children through formal instruction, everyday practice, and narrative, analyzing both mechanisms and outcomes.

lessons.title: Language, Literacy, and Identity in Sikh Families
lessons.summary: Examines the role of Punjabi language and Gurmukhi script transmission in Sikh family life, analyzing heritage language maintenance as both practical and identity-forming.

lessons.title: Discipline, Authority, and ਰਹਿਤ in Sikh Parenting
lessons.summary: Examines Sikh approaches to discipline and parental authority, analyzing the relationship between ਰਹਿਤ as a framework for moral formation and developmental research on effective discipline.

lessons.title: Mothers, Fathers, and Gendered Parenting Roles
lessons.summary: Analyzes gendered dimensions of Sikh parenting, examining both traditional role divisions and the Gurmat egalitarian theological framework that challenges them.

lessons.title: Extended Family: Grandparents and Intergenerational Care
lessons.summary: Examines the role of extended family networks in Sikh parenting, analyzing how grandparents and community elders contribute to children's identity formation.

lessons.title: Sikh Parenting in the Context of Poverty and Structural Inequality
lessons.summary: Examines how economic inequality and structural racism shape parenting challenges and resources for Sikh families, analyzing community responses grounded in Gurmat.

lessons.title: Parenting Through Trauma: Post-1984 Families
lessons.summary: Examines the specific parenting challenges and identity formation dynamics in families that experienced the trauma of the 1984 anti-Sikh pogroms and Operation Bluestar.

lessons.title: Parenting Education Programs for Sikh Communities
lessons.summary: Examines existing parenting education programs in Sikh communities, evaluates their effectiveness, and proposes principles for Gurmat-informed parenting education.

lessons.title: Synthesis: A Gurmat Framework for Excellent Sikh Parenting
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the seminar's theoretical and empirical threads into a coherent Gurmat-informed framework for excellent Sikh parenting across cultural contexts.

courses.title: Sikh Educational Philosophy: From Gurmat to Modern Pedagogy
courses.source: SGGS; Sikh education history; Paulo Freire, Pedagogy of the Oppressed (1968)
courses.summary: This graduate seminar examines the philosophical foundations of Sikh education, tracing the tradition from the pedagogical innovations of the Gurus through the colonial encounter with Western schooling to contemporary applications in diaspora Sikh schools. Drawing on SGGS, Freire's critical pedagogy, and empirical education research, students develop a coherent Gurmat-informed educational philosophy for contemporary practice.
outcomes: Analyze the pedagogical principles embedded in SGGS and the Gurus' educational innovations
Critically evaluate the impact of colonial education on Sikh communities and its lasting legacy
Apply Paulo Freire's critical pedagogy framework in dialogue with Gurmat educational philosophy
Assess contemporary Sikh school models in the UK and Canada against Gurmat educational principles
Develop a coherent Gurmat-informed educational philosophy applicable to contemporary Sikh schools and homeschooling contexts
references: Freire, Paulo. Pedagogy of the Oppressed. New York: Herder and Herder, 1968.
Grewal, J. S. The Sikhs of the Punjab. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1990.

Nesbitt, Eleanor. Sikhism: A Very Short Introduction. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2005.
Singh, Pashaura. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2000.
Vygotsky, Lev S. Mind in Society: The Development of Higher Psychological Processes. Cambridge: Harvard University Press, 1978.

lessons.title: Introduction: Philosophy of Education and Gurmat
lessons.summary: Establishes the philosophical foundations of the seminar, comparing Gurmat educational philosophy with Western philosophical traditions.

lessons.title: The Gurus as Educators: Pedagogical Innovations
lessons.summary: Examines the specific pedagogical innovations of the Gurus, from Guru Nanak's egalitarian teaching practice to Guru Gobind Singh's martial-spiritual curriculum.

lessons.title: ਧਰਮਸ਼ਾਲਾ and Early Sikh Learning Institutions
lessons.summary: Examines the historical development of Sikh educational institutions from the early ਧਰਮਸ਼ਾਲਾ through the Singh Sabha movement's school-building program.

lessons.title: SGGS as Educational Text: Content and Method
lessons.summary: Analyzes SGGS as both the primary curriculum content and the pedagogical model of Sikh education, examining its literary, philosophical, and spiritual dimensions as teaching resources.

lessons.title: Colonial Education and the Sikh Response
lessons.summary: Examines the impact of colonial education on Sikh communities and analyzes the Sikh response, from the Singh Sabha movement to contemporary postcolonial educational theory.

lessons.title: Paulo Freire and Gurmat: Critical Dialogue
lessons.summary: Conducts a systematic comparative analysis of Freire's critical pedagogy and Gurmat educational philosophy, identifying significant convergences and important divergences.

lessons.title: Constructivist Pedagogy and ਵਿਚਾਰ
lessons.summary: Examines the affinities between constructivist developmental psychology (Vygotsky, Piaget) and the Gurmat educational practice of ਵਿਚਾਰ.

lessons.title: Language Policy in Sikh Education: ਗੁਰਮੁਖੀ and Multilingualism
lessons.summary: Analyzes language policy choices in Sikh educational institutions, examining the tension between Gurmukhi literacy promotion and multilingual competence development.

lessons.title: Moral and Character Education in Gurmat Perspective
lessons.summary: Examines Gurmat approaches to moral and character education, analyzing how Sikh schools can develop students' moral identity through curriculum, pedagogy, and institutional culture.

lessons.title: Contemporary Sikh Schools: Khalsa Schools and Beyond
lessons.summary: Evaluates contemporary Sikh school models in the UK and Canada against Gurmat educational principles, examining their strengths, limitations, and areas for development.

lessons.title: Homeschooling and Gurmat Educational Practice
lessons.summary: Examines the growing phenomenon of Sikh homeschooling as an alternative educational model, analyzing its potential and limitations from a Gurmat educational philosophy perspective.

lessons.title: Synthesis: A Gurmat Philosophy of Education for the 21st Century
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the seminar's analyses into a coherent Gurmat philosophy of education adequate for contemporary Sikh educational challenges.

courses.title: Gurmat Ontology: Being, Non-Being, and the Divine
courses.source: SGGS; Sikh philosophy; Heidegger, Being and Time; Sikh metaphysics
courses.summary: This graduate seminar conducts a rigorous inquiry into the ontological commitments of Gurmat philosophy, examining SGGS's account of being, non-being, and divine reality in dialogue with Western metaphysical traditions. Through close reading of SGGS and engagement with Heidegger, Spinoza, and process philosophy, students develop a sophisticated understanding of Gurmat as a distinctive metaphysical system.
outcomes: Articulate the major ontological claims of Gurmat philosophy with precision and theological accuracy
Conduct systematic comparative analysis between Gurmat ontology and Western metaphysical traditions including Heidegger and Spinoza
Critically evaluate the concept of ਇਕੁ (the One) as a foundational ontological principle in SGGS
Analyze the relationship between divine being, creation, and the human soul in Gurmat metaphysics
Assess contemporary philosophical debates about divine ontology in light of Gurmat's distinctive contributions
references: Heidegger, Martin. Being and Time. Translated by John Macquarrie and Edward Robinson. New York: Harper and Row, 1962.
Mandair, Arvind-Pal Singh. Religion and the Specter of the West: Sikhism, India, Postcoloniality, and the Politics of Translation. New York: Columbia University Press, 2009.
Mann, Gurinder Singh. The Making of Sikh Scripture. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2001.
Nayar, Kamala Elizabeth. The Sikh Diaspora in Vancouver. Toronto: University of Toronto Press, 2004.

Singh, Bhai Vir. Santhya Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. Amritsar: Khalsa Samachar, 1958.

Singh, Pashaura. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2000.

lessons.title: Introduction: Ontology and the Question of Being in Gurmat
lessons.summary: Establishes the methodological foundations for Gurmat ontological inquiry, positioning it in dialogue with Western metaphysics.

lessons.title: The Mool Mantar as Ontological Statement
lessons.summary: Conducts a detailed philosophical analysis of the Mool Mantar as a compressed ontological declaration, examining each attribute as a metaphysical claim.

lessons.title: ਨਿਰਗੁਣ and ਸਰਗੁਣ: The Divine Beyond and Within
lessons.summary: Analyzes the fundamental Gurmat distinction between nirguna and saguna divine reality, examining its philosophical implications and its relationship to mystical and apophatic theological traditions.

lessons.title: ਹੁਕਮ: Divine Order as Ontological Structure
lessons.summary: Examines the Gurmat concept of ਹੁਕਮ as the ontological structure through which divine reality governs and constitutes all existence.

lessons.title: Creation, ਮਾਇਆ, and the Problem of Appearance
lessons.summary: Examines the Gurmat account of creation and the concept of ਮਾਇਆ as the condition of experienced separation from divine reality.

lessons.title: The Human Soul: ਜੋਤਿ, ਆਤਮਾ, and the Spark of Being
lessons.summary: Examines the Gurmat account of the human soul, analyzing the concepts of ਜੋਤਿ and ਆਤਮਾ as descriptions of the soul's nature and its relationship to divine being.

lessons.title: ਸ਼ਬਦ-Guru: The Ontology of Divine Communication
lessons.summary: Examines the Gurmat concept of ਸ਼ਬਦ-Guru as an ontological account of how divine reality communicates with and transforms human beings.

lessons.title: Gurmat and Heidegger: Being, Dasein, and Authenticity
lessons.summary: Conducts a systematic comparative analysis between Gurmat ontology and Heidegger's Being and Time, examining convergences and divergences on the questions of Being, authenticity, and death.

lessons.title: Gurmat and Spinoza: Immanence, Transcendence, and Divine Unity
lessons.summary: Analyzes the philosophical affinities and divergences between Spinoza's pantheist metaphysics and Gurmat ontology, focusing on divine unity, immanence, and the relationship between God and nature.

lessons.title: Process Philosophy and Gurmat: Becoming and Being
lessons.summary: Examines the relationship between Whitehead's process philosophy and Gurmat ontology, analyzing both the dynamic character of divine reality and the question of temporal becoming.

lessons.title: Death, Liberation, and Ontological Return
lessons.summary: Examines the Gurmat account of death and liberation as ontological concepts, analyzing the soul's return to divine reality and its implications for Gurmat metaphysics.

lessons.title: Synthesis: Gurmat as a Distinctive Metaphysical System
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the seminar's analyses into a comprehensive account of Gurmat as a distinctive and philosophically significant metaphysical system.

courses.title: Sikh Philosophy of Language: Shabad, Meaning, and Reality
courses.source: SGGS; Prof. Sahib Singh exegesis; philosophy of language
courses.summary: This graduate seminar investigates the philosophy of language embedded in SGGS, examining how Gurmat understands the relationship between language, meaning, and ultimate reality through the central concept of ਸ਼ਬਦ. Drawing on SGGS, Prof. Sahib Singh's exegetical tradition, and contemporary philosophy of language (Wittgenstein, Austin, Gadamer), students develop a sophisticated Gurmat theory of linguistic meaning.
outcomes: Articulate the Gurmat theory of ਸ਼ਬਦ as an ontological and epistemological concept, not merely a linguistic one
Analyze the relationship between language, meaning, and reality in SGGS through close hermeneutical reading
Apply Prof. Sahib Singh's exegetical methodology to selected SGGS passages with scholarly precision
Critically evaluate the Gurmat philosophy of language in dialogue with Wittgenstein, Austin, and Gadamer
Assess the implications of the Gurmat philosophy of language for Sikh hermeneutics and scriptural interpretation
references: Austin, J. L. How to Do Things with Words. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1962.
Gadamer, Hans-Georg. Truth and Method. Translated by Joel Weinsheimer and Donald G. Marshall. 2nd rev. ed. New York: Crossroad, 1989.
Mann, Gurinder Singh. The Making of Sikh Scripture. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2001.

Singh, Pashaura. The Guru Granth Sahib: Canon, Meaning and Authority. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2000.

Wittgenstein, Ludwig. Philosophical Investigations. Translated by G. E. M. Anscombe. Oxford: Blackwell, 1953.

lessons.title: Introduction: Language, Meaning, and the Divine Word
lessons.summary: Establishes the philosophical stakes of the seminar, introducing the central role of ਸ਼ਬਦ in Gurmat philosophy of language.

lessons.title: ਨਾਦ and the Ontological Foundation of Language
lessons.summary: Examines the Gurmat concept of ਨਾਦ (primordial sound) as the ontological foundation of all language, analyzing its implications for a Gurmat theory of linguistic meaning.

lessons.title: ਸ਼ਬਦ-Guru: The Word as Living Presence
lessons.summary: Analyzes the Gurmat concept of ਸ਼ਬਦ-Guru as simultaneously a linguistic, theological, and practical concept, examining its implications for understanding scriptural authority.

lessons.title: The Multilingual SGGS: Divine Truth across Languages
lessons.summary: Analyzes the multilingual composition of SGGS as a philosophical statement about the universality of divine truth and the relationship between language diversity and religious meaning.

lessons.title: Prof. Sahib Singh's Exegetical Method
lessons.summary: Provides a detailed analysis of Prof. Sahib Singh's methodology in the Darpan, examining how grammatical analysis and theological interpretation interact in his exegetical practice.

lessons.title: Wittgenstein and Gurmat: Language Games and Forms of Life
lessons.summary: Conducts a systematic comparative analysis between Wittgenstein's later philosophy of language and Gurmat's account of ਬਾਣੀ meaning within the 'form of life' of the Sikh community.

lessons.title: J. L. Austin and ਕੀਰਤਨ: Language as Performative Act
lessons.summary: Applies J. L. Austin's speech act theory to the practice of ਕੀਰਤਨ, analyzing devotional singing as a performative linguistic act that transforms the practitioner.

lessons.title: Gadamer and Gurmat Hermeneutics
lessons.summary: Examines Hans-Georg Gadamer's philosophical hermeneutics in dialogue with Gurmat's tradition of ਵਿਚਾਰ and ਬਾਣੀ interpretation.

lessons.title: Silence, the Ineffable, and the Limits of Language
lessons.summary: Examines the role of silence and the ineffable in Gurmat philosophy of language, analyzing the tradition's account of the limits of linguistic expression in relation to divine reality.

lessons.title: Translation, Transmission, and Meaning Loss
lessons.summary: Examines the philosophical challenges of translating SGGS, analyzing the conditions under which meaning is preserved, transformed, or lost in the translation process.

lessons.title: Contemporary Sikh Hermeneutics: Debates and Directions
lessons.summary: Surveys major contemporary debates in Sikh hermeneutics, including the ਟਕਸਾਲੀ vs. reformist interpretive traditions and the role of gender in scriptural interpretation.

lessons.title: Synthesis: Toward a Gurmat Philosophy of Language
lessons.summary: Synthesizes the seminar's analyses into a coherent Gurmat philosophy of language that integrates SGGS, the exegetical tradition, and contemporary philosophy of language.

courses.title: Gurmat and Contemporary Philosophy: Dialogue and Critique
courses.source: SGGS; Arvind-Pal Mandair scholarship; contemporary philosophy
courses.summary: This graduate seminar engages Gurmat philosophy in critical dialogue with major movements in contemporary Western philosophy—postcolonialism, phenomenology, analytic philosophy of religion, and feminist philosophy. Drawing on Mandair's scholarship and SGGS, students develop the capacity to articulate and defend Gurmat positions in contemporary philosophical debate while critically evaluating Western philosophy's assumptions.
outcomes: Engage contemporary Western philosophical frameworks with Gurmat positions through rigorous critical dialogue
Critically analyze Arvind-Pal Mandair's postcolonial reading of Sikh philosophy and its implications
Apply phenomenological methods to the analysis of Sikh religious experience
Evaluate analytic philosophy of religion's claims in light of Gurmat epistemology and metaphysics
Develop original philosophical arguments drawing on Gurmat resources for contemporary philosophical debates
references: Mandair, Arvind-Pal Singh. Religion and the Specter of the West: Sikhism, India, Postcoloniality, and the Politics of Translation. New York: Columbia University Press, 2009.
